tasks.title: Database schema design and SQLAlchemy models implementation
tasks.description: Design and implement complete SQLAlchemy 2.0 models for all domain entities using mapped_column() and async patterns
tasks.details:
Implement SQLAlchemy models for all core entities:

**Auth domain (src/auth/models.py):**
- User model with email (unique, indexed), hashed_password, full_name, is_active, failed_login_attempts, locked_until, created_at, updated_at
- Use bcrypt for password hashing via passlib

**Products domain (src/products/models.py):**
- Product: id (UUID), name, sku (unique, indexed), description, category_id (FK), unit_cost (Decimal), selling_price (Decimal), currency (default NGN), price_elasticity_coefficient (Decimal, default -1.0), fx_sensitivity_coefficient (Decimal, default 0.5), is_active, created_at, updated_at
- ProductCategory: id (UUID), name (unique), description, created_at, updated_at
- PriceHistory: id (UUID), product_id (FK), old_unit_cost, new_unit_cost, old_selling_price, new_selling_price, reason, effective_date, changed_by (FK -> User), created_at

**Inventory domain (src/inventory/models.py):**
- InventoryLevel: id (UUID), product_id (FK, unique), current_stock (Decimal), low_stock_threshold (Integer), low_stock_threshold_days (Integer), last_stock_update, created_at, updated_at
- StockMovement: id (UUID), product_id (FK), movement_type (enum: SALE, PURCHASE, ADJUSTMENT), quantity (Decimal), reference_id (UUID, nullable), reason, created_at

**Sales domain (src/sales/models.py):**
- DailySales: id (UUID), product_id (FK), sale_date (Date, indexed), quantity_sold (Decimal), selling_price_at_sale (Decimal), total_amount (Decimal), notes, submitted_by (FK -> User), submitted_at, created_at, updated_at
- Index on (product_id, sale_date) for fast queries

**Orders domain (src/orders/models.py):**
- Order: id (UUID), order_number (unique, indexed), supplier_name, order_date (Date, indexed), production_days (Integer), shipping_days (Integer), clearing_days (Integer), estimated_arrival_date (Date, computed), actual_arrival_date (Date, nullable), status (enum: PENDING, IN_PRODUCTION, SHIPPING, CLEARED, DELIVERED), total_order_value_usd (Decimal), notes, created_by (FK -> User), created_at, updated_at
- OrderItem: id (UUID), order_id (FK), product_id (FK), quantity (Decimal), unit_cost_usd (Decimal), total_cost_usd (Decimal), created_at
- OrderPayment: id (UUID), order_id (FK), payment_type (enum: DEPOSIT_30, BALANCE_70), payment_date (Date), amount_usd (Decimal), fx_rate_ngn_usd (Decimal), amount_ngn (Decimal), is_forecasted (Boolean, default False), created_at

**FX domain (src/fx/models.py):**
- FXRate: id (UUID), currency_pair (String, default NGNGSD, indexed), rate_type (enum: PARALLEL_MARKET, OFFICIAL_CBN), rate (Decimal), rate_date (Date, indexed), source (String), created_at
- FXForecast: id (UUID), currency_pair (String, indexed), forecast_date (Date, indexed), target_date (Date, indexed), base_forecast (Decimal), best_case (Decimal), worst_case (Decimal), confidence_level (Decimal), model_version (String), mae (Decimal, nullable), mape (Decimal, nullable), created_at
- Unique constraint on (currency_pair, rate_type, rate_date) for FXRate
- Unique constraint on (currency_pair, forecast_date, target_date) for FXForecast

**Cashflow domain (src/cashflow/models.py):**
- LoanObligation: id (UUID), loan_name, monthly_repayment_amount (Decimal), monthly_salary_offset (Decimal), net_monthly_burden (Decimal, computed), start_date (Date), end_date (Date, nullable), is_active (Boolean), created_at, updated_at
- OperatingCost: id (UUID), cost_category (String), amount (Decimal), frequency (enum: MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, ANNUAL), effective_date (Date), notes, created_at, updated_at
- CashflowProjection: id (UUID), projection_month (Date, indexed), scenario_type (enum: BASE, FX_SHOCK, DEMAND_DROP, COMBINED_STRESS), projected_revenue (Decimal), projected_loan_payment (Decimal), projected_operating_costs (Decimal), projected_fx_obligations (Decimal), net_cashflow (Decimal), cumulative_cashflow (Decimal), cash_runway_months (Decimal), dscr (Decimal), risk_rating (enum: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH), generated_at, created_at

**Pricing domain (src/pricing/models.py):**
- PricingRecommendation: id (UUID), product_id (FK), current_price (Decimal), recommended_price (Decimal), current_margin (Decimal), projected_margin (Decimal), reasoning (Text), priority (enum: HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW), status (enum: PENDING, APPLIED, DISMISSED), created_at, applied_at, dismissed_at
- PortfolioMargin: id (UUID), calculation_date (Date, indexed), total_revenue (Decimal), total_cogs (Decimal), blended_margin (Decimal), target_margin (Decimal, default 0.35), margin_gap (Decimal), created_at

**AI Engine domain (src/ai_engine/models.py):**
- Recommendation: id (UUID), recommendation_type (enum: PRICE, ORDER_TIMING, USD_HEDGE, INVENTORY, LIQUIDITY), title (String), description (Text), expected_impact (String), priority_score (Integer), status (enum: PENDING, APPLIED, DISMISSED), related_entity_type (String, nullable), related_entity_id (UUID, nullable), created_at, applied_at, dismissed_at
- ScenarioSimulation: id (UUID), simulation_name, scenario_type (enum: BASE, FX_SHOCK_10, FX_SHOCK_20, DEMAND_DROP_10, DEMAND_DROP_20, COMBINED_STRESS), fx_shock_pct (Decimal), demand_drop_pct (Decimal), projected_cash_runway (Decimal), projected_dscr (Decimal), projected_margin (Decimal), simulated_at, created_at

**Implementation requirements:**
- Use SQLAlchemy 2.0 Mapped[] type annotations and mapped_column()
- All timestamps use DateTime with timezone=True
- All currency amounts use Decimal type (never float)
- Set up proper relationships between models
- Add __repr__ methods for debugging
- Inherit all models from src.core.database.Base
tasks.testStrategy: Create pytest fixtures for each model in backend/tests/conftest.py using factory_boy. Write unit tests in backend/tests/test_models/ to verify: (1) model instantiation with valid data, (2) field constraints (unique, nullable, defaults), (3) relationship loading (selectinload), (4) computed properties work correctly. Use pytest-asyncio for async tests. Verify models can be instantiated without errors and relationships are properly configured.

tasks.title: Alembic migrations for complete database schema
tasks.description: Create and test Alembic migrations for all SQLAlchemy models with proper indexing and constraints
tasks.details:
Generate initial Alembic migration for the complete database schema:

1. **Configure Alembic** (backend/alembic/env.py):
   - Import all models to ensure Alembic detects them
   - Set target_metadata = Base.metadata
   - Configure async engine for PostgreSQL with asyncpg

2. **Generate initial migration:**
   ```bash
   cd backend
   alembic revision --autogenerate -m "initial_schema"
   ```

3. **Review and enhance generated migration:**
   - Verify all tables, columns, and relationships are included
   - Add explicit indexes on frequently queried columns:
     - User.email
     - Product.sku, Product.name
     - DailySales.sale_date, DailySales.product_id
     - Order.order_date, Order.status
     - FXRate.rate_date, FXRate.currency_pair
     - FXForecast.target_date, FXForecast.currency_pair
   - Verify unique constraints are in place
   - Add check constraints where appropriate (e.g., quantity_sold >= 0)

4. **Apply migration to development database:**
   ```bash
   alembic upgrade head
   ```

5. **Test migration reversibility:**
   ```bash
   alembic downgrade -1
   alembic upgrade head
   ```

6. **Document migration in backend/alembic/README.md** with common commands and troubleshooting tips

**Key considerations:**
- Use async engine configuration in env.py
- Ensure migration is idempotent and can be safely re-run
- Add explicit create_index() calls for composite indexes
- Verify foreign key constraints have proper ON DELETE behavior
tasks.testStrategy: Integration test: (1) Start with empty database, apply migration, verify all tables exist with correct columns using sqlalchemy inspect(), (2) Insert sample data for each model and verify constraints work (unique violations raise errors, FKs enforce referential integrity), (3) Test downgrade and upgrade again to ensure reversibility, (4) Run pytest backend/tests/test_migrations.py to verify schema matches models. Test in docker-compose environment with PostgreSQL 16.

subtasks.title: Configure alembic/env.py to import all domain models
subtasks.description: Update backend/alembic/env.py to import all SQLAlchemy models from each domain module ensuring Alembic can detect them for autogeneration
subtasks.details: Modify alembic/env.py to import models from src/auth/models.py, src/products/models.py, src/sales/models.py, src/orders/models.py, src/fx/models.py, and src/ai_engine/models.py. Set target_metadata = Base.metadata to ensure Alembic uses the correct metadata. Configure async engine using asyncpg driver: create_async_engine(config.get_main_option('sqlalchemy.url'), future=True). Update run_migrations_online() to use async context manager and await connectable.run_sync(do_run_migrations).
subtasks.testStrategy: Manual verification: Run 'alembic check' to ensure configuration is valid. Verify all model imports succeed without errors by running 'python -c "from alembic.env import target_metadata; print(target_metadata.tables.keys())"' and confirming all expected tables are listed.

subtasks.title: Generate initial migration using alembic autogenerate
subtasks.description: Run alembic revision --autogenerate -m 'initial_schema' to create the initial migration file based on all imported models
subtasks.details: Execute 'cd backend && alembic revision --autogenerate -m "initial_schema"' to generate migration file in backend/alembic/versions/. Alembic will compare current database state (empty) with models metadata and generate create_table() operations for all entities: users, products, categories, price_history, inventory_adjustments, daily_sales, orders, order_items, fx_rates, fx_forecasts, recommendations. Verify the generated file includes all expected tables with columns, data types, and foreign key constraints.
subtasks.testStrategy: Review generated migration file to ensure it contains create_table() operations for all 11+ tables. Verify foreign key relationships are correctly defined with proper referencing (e.g., DailySales.product_id -> products.id). Check that Decimal columns use sa.Numeric type and UUID columns use sa.UUID or appropriate dialect type.

subtasks.title: Add explicit single-column indexes to migration
subtasks.description: Enhance the generated migration file by adding explicit create_index() calls for frequently queried single columns
subtasks.details: Edit the generated migration file in upgrade() function to add index creation after table creation: op.create_index('ix_users_email', 'users', ['email'], unique=False) for user lookups, op.create_index('ix_products_sku', 'products', ['sku'], unique=False) for SKU searches, op.create_index('ix_products_name', 'products', ['name'], unique=False) for name searches, op.create_index('ix_daily_sales_sale_date', 'daily_sales', ['sale_date'], unique=False) for date range queries, op.create_index('ix_orders_order_date', 'orders', ['order_date'], unique=False) for order history, op.create_index('ix_orders_status', 'orders', ['status'], unique=False) for status filtering, op.create_index('ix_fx_rates_rate_date', 'fx_rates', ['rate_date'], unique=False), op.create_index('ix_fx_forecasts_target_date', 'fx_forecasts', ['target_date'], unique=False). Add corresponding drop_index() calls in downgrade() function.
subtasks.testStrategy: After applying migration, use SQLAlchemy inspector to verify indexes exist: from sqlalchemy import inspect; insp = inspect(engine); print(insp.get_indexes('users')) and confirm 'ix_users_email' is listed. Repeat for all tables with added indexes.

subtasks.title: Add composite indexes for multi-column queries
subtasks.description: Add composite indexes to optimize common multi-column query patterns in daily sales, FX forecasts, and other frequently joined tables
subtasks.details: Add composite index creation to migration file: op.create_index('ix_daily_sales_product_date', 'daily_sales', ['product_id', 'sale_date'], unique=False) for product sales history queries, op.create_index('ix_fx_forecasts_pair_date', 'fx_forecasts', ['currency_pair', 'target_date'], unique=False) for FX forecast lookups, op.create_index('ix_fx_rates_pair_date', 'fx_rates', ['currency_pair', 'rate_date'], unique=False) for historical rate queries, op.create_index('ix_order_items_order_product', 'order_items', ['order_id', 'product_id'], unique=False) for order detail queries. Add corresponding drop_index() calls in downgrade(). Verify index order matches common query filter order (most selective column first).
subtasks.testStrategy: After migration, verify composite indexes using inspector: insp.get_indexes('daily_sales') should show 'ix_daily_sales_product_date' with columns=['product_id', 'sale_date']. Test query performance improvement by running EXPLAIN ANALYZE on a query filtering by product_id and sale_date before and after index creation (expect index scan instead of sequential scan).

subtasks.title: Apply migration and verify complete schema creation
subtasks.description: Run alembic upgrade head to apply the migration and verify all tables, columns, indexes, and constraints are correctly created in the database
subtasks.details: Execute 'alembic upgrade head' to apply the migration. tasks.title: Complete authentication system with JWT and security features
tasks.description: Implement user registration, login, JWT token management, password hashing, and rate limiting per PRD security requirements
tasks.details:
Build complete authentication system in src/auth/:

**Service layer (service.py):**
- `create_user(email, password, full_name)`: hash password with bcrypt, create user record
- `authenticate_user(email, password)`: verify credentials, handle failed login attempts (lock after 3 failures for 15 minutes)
- `create_access_token(user_id)`: generate JWT with 24-hour expiration using python-jose
- `verify_token(token)`: decode and validate JWT
- `reset_password(user_id, new_password)`: hash and update password

**Router (router.py):**
- POST /register: create new user account
- POST /login: authenticate and return JWT token
- POST /logout: invalidate token (store in Redis blacklist)
- GET /me: get current user profile (protected)
- POST /forgot-password: send password reset email (stubbed for Stage A)
- POST /reset-password: reset password with token

**Security implementation:**
- Password requirements: min 12 chars, uppercase, lowercase, number, special char
- Rate limiting: 100 requests/minute per session using Redis
- Failed login tracking: increment failed_login_attempts, set locked_until after 3 failures
- Token blacklist in Redis for logout
- CORS configuration already in main.py

**Dependencies (dependencies.py):**
- `get_current_user`: dependency that extracts JWT from Authorization header, validates, and returns User object
- `get_current_active_user`: extends get_current_user, verifies is_active=True

**Schemas (schemas.py):**
- UserRegister: email, password, full_name
- UserLogin: email, password
- TokenResponse: access_token, token_type
- UserProfile: id, email, full_name, is_active, created_at

**Implementation notes:**
- Use passlib with bcrypt for password hashing
- JWT secret from settings.SECRET_KEY
- Token expiration from settings.ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES (default 1440 = 24 hours)
- All operations are async
- Use structlog for audit logging of auth events

Use pytest fixtures for test database and Redis.

tasks.title: Products and inventory management CRUD operations
tasks.description: Implement product catalog management with categories, CRUD operations, and inventory level tracking
tasks.details:
Implement products and inventory modules:

**Products service (src/products/service.py):**
- `create_product(data, user_id)`: create product with auto-generated SKU if not provided
- `get_product_by_id(product_id)`: retrieve single product
- `list_products(filters, pagination)`: list products with filtering by category, is_active
- `update_product(product_id, data, user_id)`: update product, create PriceHistory record if prices change
- `deactivate_product(product_id)`: soft-delete by setting is_active=False
- `create_category(name, description)`: create product category
- `list_categories()`: list all categories

**Products router (src/products/router.py):**
- POST /products: create new product (protected)
- GET /products: list products with filters and pagination
- GET /products/{id}: get single product
- PUT /products/{id}: update product (protected)
- DELETE /products/{id}: deactivate product (protected)
- POST /categories: create category (protected)
- GET /categories: list categories
- GET /products/{id}/price-history: get price change history

**Inventory service (src/inventory/service.py):**
- `initialize_inventory(product_id, initial_stock)`: create InventoryLevel record when product is created
- `get_inventory_level(product_id)`: get current stock level
- `update_stock(product_id, quantity_delta, movement_type, reference_id)`: adjust stock and create StockMovement record
- `get_low_stock_products()`: query products where current_stock <= low_stock_threshold
- `calculate_depletion_date(product_id)`: compute predicted stock-out date based on 30-day rolling average sales velocity
- `get_stock_movements(product_id, date_range)`: get movement history

**Inventory router (src/inventory/router.py):**
- GET /inventory: list all inventory levels
- GET /inventory/{product_id}: get inventory for specific product
- POST /inventory/{product_id}/adjust: manual stock adjustment (protected)
- GET /inventory/low-stock: list products at or below threshold
- GET /inventory/{product_id}/movements: get stock movement history
- GET /inventory/{product_id}/depletion-forecast: get predicted stock-out date

**Implementation notes:**
- Use SQLAlchemy async queries with proper error handling
- Price changes trigger PriceHistory records automatically
- Inventory adjustments always create StockMovement audit records
- Depletion forecast requires sales data (gracefully handle products with no sales history)
- Use Pydantic models for request/response validation
- Include user_id from JWT token for audit trails

  - Compute days_until_depletion = current_stock / daily_velocity
  - Return predicted stock-out date
  - Handle products with no sales history (return None)

tasks.title: Daily sales entry with automatic inventory updates
tasks.description: Implement sales data entry system that automatically updates inventory levels and tracks sales history for demand forecasting
tasks.details:
Implement sales module with automatic inventory synchronization:

**Sales service (src/sales/service.py):**
- `create_daily_sales_entry(entries, user_id)`: 
  - Accept list of {product_id, quantity_sold, sale_date} entries
  - Validate product exists and has sufficient stock
  - Create DailySales records
  - Call inventory.update_stock() to reduce inventory by quantity_sold
  - Create StockMovement with type=SALE
  - Calculate total_amount using current product selling_price
  - Transaction rollback on any failure
- `get_sales_by_date_range(start_date, end_date, product_id?)`: retrieve sales data
- `get_sales_velocity(product_id, days=30)`: calculate rolling average daily sales
- `get_sales_summary(date_range)`: aggregate revenue, units sold, by product and date
- `update_sales_entry(entry_id, data, user_id)`: edit previous entry, adjust inventory delta
- `delete_sales_entry(entry_id, user_id)`: delete entry, reverse inventory adjustment, audit log

tasks.title: Order and purchase management with FX exposure tracking
tasks.description: Implement purchase order lifecycle management with 30/70 payment structure and FX exposure calculation
tasks.details:
Implement orders module with FX exposure tracking:

**Orders service (src/orders/service.py):**
- `create_order(supplier_name, items, lead_times, user_id)`:
  - Create Order record with auto-generated order_number (format: ORD-YYYY-NNNN)
  - Create OrderItem records for each product
  - Calculate estimated_arrival_date = order_date + production_days + shipping_days + clearing_days
  - Create 30% deposit OrderPayment with current FX rate (from fx.get_latest_rate())
  - Return order with locked FX exposure calculated
- `update_order_status(order_id, new_status, user_id)`:
  - Update status with validation of allowed transitions
  - If status = DELIVERED, prompt for actual_arrival_date and actual FX rate for 70% payment
  - Create 70% balance OrderPayment record with actual FX rate
  - Trigger inventory.update_stock() to add received quantity
  - Create StockMovement with type=PURCHASE
- `get_order_by_id(order_id)`: retrieve order with items and payments
- `list_orders(filters)`: filter by status, date range, supplier
- `calculate_fx_exposure(order_id)`: compute locked (30% deposit) and floating (70% forecasted) exposure
- `get_orders_by_arrival_window(days=180)`: get orders arriving in next N days for cashflow projection
- `get_profit_projection(order_id, fx_scenario='base')`: calculate expected profit using FX forecast

**Orders router (src/orders/router.py):**
- POST /orders: create new purchase order
- GET /orders: list orders with filters (status, date range, supplier)
- GET /orders/{id}: get order details with FX exposure breakdown
- PUT /orders/{id}/status: update order status
- GET /orders/{id}/fx-exposure: get detailed FX exposure (locked 30%, floating 70%)
- GET /orders/{id}/profit-projection: get profit projection with FX scenarios
- GET /orders/pipeline: get orders grouped by status for pipeline view
- GET /orders/arriving-soon: get orders arriving in next 30 days

**FX exposure calculation:**
```python
def calculate_fx_exposure(order):
    # 30% locked at deposit FX rate
    deposit_payment = order.payments.filter(payment_type='DEPOSIT_30').first()
    locked_exposure_usd = order.total_order_value_usd * 0.30
    locked_fx_rate = deposit_payment.fx_rate_ngn_usd
    locked_exposure_ngn = locked_exposure_usd * locked_fx_rate
    
    # 70% floating - use forecast FX rate at arrival date
    balance_exposure_usd = order.total_order_value_usd * 0.70
    forecast = fx_service.get_forecast_for_date(order.estimated_arrival_date)
    floating_fx_rate = forecast.base_forecast
    floating_exposure_ngn = balance_exposure_usd * floating_fx_rate
    
    return {
        'locked': {'usd': locked_exposure_usd, 'ngn': locked_exposure_ngn, 'fx_rate': locked_fx_rate},
        'floating': {'usd': balance_exposure_usd, 'ngn': floating_exposure_ngn, 'fx_rate': floating_fx_rate},
        'total_ngn': locked_exposure_ngn + floating_exposure_ngn
    }
```

**Implementation notes:**
- Use Decimal type for all currency calculations
- FX rates fetched from fx module (integrates with task 7)
- Order status transitions enforced: PENDING -> IN_PRODUCTION -> SHIPPING -> CLEARED -> DELIVERED
- Profit projection compares total cost (in NGN) vs. revenue from selling at current prices
- Use async transactions for order creation (order + items + payment + inventory)

  - Fetch historical data from API for model training (180 days required)
  - Batch insert into database

**API integration example (using public FX API):**
```python
async def fetch_fx_from_api():
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
        response = await client.get(
            settings.FX_API_URL,
            headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {settings.FX_API_KEY}'},
            timeout=10.0
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
        data = response.json()
        rate = Decimal(str(data['rates']['NGN']))  # Example structure
        return rate
```

tasks.title: FX forecasting engine with Prophet and Monte Carlo simulation
tasks.description: Implement AI-driven FX rate forecasting using Facebook Prophet with Monte Carlo simulation for scenario modeling
tasks.details:
Implement FX forecasting in src/fx/:

**FX forecasting service additions to service.py:**
- `train_fx_forecast_model(currency_pair='NGNGSD')`:
  - Fetch 180 days of historical rates from database
  - Prepare data in Prophet format: {ds: date, y: rate}
  - Initialize Prophet model with multiplicative seasonality
  - Fit model on historical data
  - Store model to disk (pickle) with version identifier
  - Log training metrics (MAE on validation set)
- `generate_fx_forecast(currency_pair='NGNGSD', forecast_horizon_days=180)`:
  - Load trained Prophet model from disk
  - Generate point forecasts for next 180 days
  - Extract confidence intervals from Prophet output (80% and 95%)
  - For each forecast date, run Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 runs) to generate distribution:
    - Use Prophet trend + seasonality as mean
    - Use historical 30-day volatility as standard deviation
    - Generate random samples from normal distribution
    - Calculate percentiles: 5th (best-case), 50th (base), 95th (worst-case)
  - Store forecasts in FXForecast table
  - Return forecast DataFrame
- `get_forecast_for_date(currency_pair, target_date)`:
  - Retrieve forecast from FXForecast table
  - If forecast doesn't exist or is stale (>7 days old), regenerate
  - Return base, best_case, worst_case rates
- `get_forecast_range(currency_pair, start_date, end_date)`:
  - Return forecast time series for date range
- `update_forecast_accuracy()`:
  - Compare past forecasts to actual rates
  - Calculate MAE and MAPE
  - Update FXForecast records with error metrics
  - Log accuracy for model improvement tracking
- `monte_carlo_fx_simulation(base_rate, volatility, days_ahead, num_simulations=10000)`:
  - Geometric Brownian Motion simulation
  - Returns distribution of possible rates

**Prophet model configuration:**
```python
from prophet import Prophet
import numpy as np

def train_model(historical_data: pd.DataFrame):
    model = Prophet(
        yearly_seasonality=True,
        weekly_seasonality=False,
        daily_seasonality=False,
        seasonality_mode='multiplicative',
        interval_width=0.95
    )
    model.fit(historical_data)
    return model

def forecast_with_scenarios(model, periods=180):
    future = model.make_future_dataframe(periods=periods)
    forecast = model.predict(future)
    
    # Extract Prophet forecast
    base_forecast = forecast[['ds', 'yhat', 'yhat_lower', 'yhat_upper']]
    
    # Monte Carlo for scenario generation
    volatility = calculate_volatility()  # From historical data
    scenarios = []
    for _, row in base_forecast.iterrows():
        simulated_rates = np.random.normal(
            loc=row['yhat'],
            scale=volatility * row['yhat'],
            size=10000
        )
        scenarios.append({
            'date': row['ds'],
            'base': row['yhat'],
            'best_case': np.percentile(simulated_rates, 5),
            'worst_case': np.percentile(simulated_rates, 95)
        })
    
    return scenarios
```

**Router additions:**
- POST /fx/train-model: trigger model training (protected, admin)
- POST /fx/generate-forecast: generate new forecast for horizon (protected)
- GET /fx/forecast/{target_date}: get forecast for specific date
- GET /fx/forecast-range: get forecast time series
- GET /fx/forecast-accuracy: get model performance metrics

**Implementation notes:**
- Model training should run weekly or when significant drift detected
- Forecasts regenerated daily
- Store model version with each forecast for traceability
- Use NumPy/SciPy for Monte Carlo simulation performance
- Prophet model files stored in backend/models/ directory
- Async wrappers around Prophet (CPU-intensive, run in thread pool)
- Error bounds widen for longer forecast horizons

tasks.title: Demand forecasting and pricing optimization engine
tasks.description: Implement demand elasticity modeling, sales forecasting, and portfolio margin optimization to maintain 35% target margin
tasks.details:
Implement demand and pricing modules:

**Demand forecasting (src/pricing/service.py - demand functions):**
- `calculate_demand_forecast(product_id, forecast_horizon_days=90)`:
  - Fetch historical sales data from sales module
  - Prepare time series: {ds: sale_date, y: quantity_sold}
  - Train Prophet model with seasonality for demand
  - Generate 90-day forward demand forecast
  - Apply price elasticity adjustment: `demand_adjusted = base_demand * (1 + elasticity * price_change_pct)`
  - Apply FX sensitivity adjustment: `demand_adjusted *= (1 + fx_sensitivity * fx_change_pct)`
  - Return forecast with confidence intervals
- `calculate_price_elasticity_impact(product_id, proposed_price)`:
  - Current price = product.selling_price
  - Price change % = (proposed_price - current_price) / current_price
  - Elasticity coefficient = product.price_elasticity_coefficient (default -1.0)
  - Demand impact % = elasticity * price_change_%
  - Return projected demand change

**Portfolio margin optimization (src/pricing/service.py):**
- `calculate_portfolio_margin()`:
  - Query all active products with recent sales data
  - For each product:
    - Revenue = sum(daily_sales.total_amount) over last 30 days
    - COGS = sum(daily_sales.quantity_sold * product.unit_cost)
    - Margin = (Revenue - COGS) / Revenue
  - Blended margin = total_margin / total_revenue across all products
  - Store in PortfolioMargin table
  - Return {blended_margin, target_margin=0.35, margin_gap, per_product_margins[]}
- `generate_pricing_recommendations(target_margin=0.35)`:
  - Calculate current portfolio margin
  - If blended_margin < target_margin:
    - Identify products with margin < 35%
    - Use optimization algorithm (SciPy minimize) to find price adjustments:
      - Objective: maximize blended margin
      - Constraints: maintain total revenue within 5% of current
      - Consider elasticity: high-elasticity products get smaller increases
    - Generate PricingRecommendation for each product needing adjustment
    - Include cross-subsidization logic: allow high-margin products (>40%) to offset lower-margin volume drivers (28-34%)
  - Prioritize recommendations by impact (HIGH: margin gap >5%, MEDIUM: 2-5%, LOW: <2%)

- GET /pricing/portfolio-margin: get current blended margin and per-product breakdown

**Optimization algorithm (simplified):**
```python
from scipy.optimize import minimize

def optimize_prices(products, target_margin=0.35):
    # Initial prices
    x0 = [p.selling_price for p in products]
    
    def objective(prices):
        # Calculate blended margin with new prices
        total_revenue = 0
        total_cogs = 0
        for i, product in enumerate(products):
            new_price = prices[i]
            price_change = (new_price - product.selling_price) / product.selling_price
            demand_multiplier = 1 + product.price_elasticity_coefficient * price_change
            projected_quantity = product.avg_daily_sales * 30 * demand_multiplier
            revenue = projected_quantity * new_price
            cogs = projected_quantity * product.unit_cost
            total_revenue += revenue
            total_cogs += cogs
        
        margin = (total_revenue - total_cogs) / total_revenue
        # Minimize negative margin (maximize margin)
        return -(margin - target_margin)
    
    # Constraints: prices must be > unit_cost * 1.10 (minimum 10% margin)
    bounds = [(p.unit_cost * 1.10, p.unit_cost * 3.0) for p in products]
    
    result = minimize(objective, x0, bounds=bounds, method='SLSQP')
    return result.x  # Optimized prices
```

- Use Decimal for all price/margin calculations
- Portfolio margin calculated daily via scheduled task
- Recommendations generated when margin falls below threshold
- Cross-subsidization explicitly shown in recommendation reasoning
- Support manual override of elasticity coefficients per product

tasks.title: Cashflow projection and DSCR monitoring system
tasks.description: Implement 6-month rolling cashflow projection, DSCR calculation, cash runway monitoring, and stress scenario simulation
tasks.details:
Implement cashflow module in src/cashflow/:

**Cashflow service (service.py):**
- `create_loan_obligation(data, user_id)`:
  - Create LoanObligation record
  - Calculate net_monthly_burden = monthly_repayment - salary_offset
- `create_operating_cost(data, user_id)`:
  - Create OperatingCost record
  - Normalize frequency to monthly equivalent
- `generate_cashflow_projection(months=6, scenario_type='BASE')`:
  - For each of next 6 months:
    1. **Projected Revenue:**
       - Sum demand forecasts for all products * selling_price
       - If scenario_type='DEMAND_DROP_10', reduce by 10%
       - If scenario_type='DEMAND_DROP_20', reduce by 20%
    2. **Projected Loan Payment:**
       - Sum net_monthly_burden for all active loans
    3. **Projected Operating Costs:**
       - Sum monthly operating costs
    4. **Projected FX Obligations (70% balance payments):**
       - Query orders with estimated_arrival_date in this month
       - Calculate 70% * total_order_value_usd * forecasted_fx_rate
       - If scenario_type='FX_SHOCK_10', increase FX rate by 10%
       - If scenario_type='FX_SHOCK_20', increase FX rate by 20%
    5. **Net Cashflow:**
       - net = revenue - loan_payment - operating_costs - fx_obligations
    6. **Cumulative Cashflow:**
       - cumulative = previous_cumulative + net
    7. **Cash Runway:**
       - If net < 0: runway = cumulative / abs(average_monthly_burn)
    8. **DSCR (Debt Service Coverage Ratio):**
       - DSCR = net_operating_income / total_debt_service
       - net_operating_income = revenue - operating_costs
       - total_debt_service = loan_payment
    9. **Risk Rating:**
       - LOW: DSCR >= 1.5 AND runway > 6 months
       - MEDIUM: DSCR 1.0-1.49 OR runway 3-6 months
       - HIGH: DSCR < 1.0 OR runway < 3 months
  - Store projection in CashflowProjection table
  - Return list of 6 monthly projections
- `run_stress_scenario(scenario_type)`:
  - scenario_type in ['BASE', 'FX_SHOCK_10', 'FX_SHOCK_20', 'DEMAND_DROP_10', 'DEMAND_DROP_20', 'COMBINED_STRESS']
  - COMBINED_STRESS = FX_SHOCK_20 + DEMAND_DROP_20
  - Generate cashflow projection with scenario parameters
  - Store in ScenarioSimulation table
  - Return comparative results (base vs. stress)
- `calculate_cash_runway()`:
  - Query latest cumulative_cashflow
  - Calculate average monthly burn from last 3 months
  - runway_months = cumulative_cashflow / average_burn
  - Return runway_months
- `calculate_dscr(month_projection)`:
  - DSCR = net_operating_income / total_debt_service
  - Return ratio and color code (green/amber/red)
- `check_liquidity_alerts()`:
  - Query next 6 months of projections
  - Flag months with negative net_cashflow
  - Flag if DSCR < 1.0 in any month
  - Return list of alerts with severity

**Cashflow router (router.py):**
- POST /cashflow/loans: create loan obligation
- GET /cashflow/loans: list active loans
- POST /cashflow/operating-costs: create operating cost
- GET /cashflow/operating-costs: list operating costs
- GET /cashflow/projection: get 6-month cashflow projection (defaults to BASE scenario)
- GET /cashflow/projection/{scenario}: get projection for specific scenario
- POST /cashflow/run-scenario: run stress scenario simulation
- GET /cashflow/scenarios: list saved scenario simulations
- GET /cashflow/cash-runway: get current cash runway in months
- GET /cashflow/dscr: get current DSCR
- GET /cashflow/alerts: get liquidity shortage alerts

**Scenario comparison output:**
```json

  "base": {"cash_runway": 8.5, "avg_dscr": 1.8, "risk_rating": "LOW"},
  "fx_shock_20": {"cash_runway": 4.2, "avg_dscr": 1.1, "risk_rating": "MEDIUM"},
  "demand_drop_20": {"cash_runway": 5.1, "avg_dscr": 1.3, "risk_rating": "MEDIUM"},
  "combined_stress": {"cash_runway": 2.8, "avg_dscr": 0.8, "risk_rating": "HIGH"}
}
```

**Implementation notes:**
- Use Decimal for all financial calculations
- Projections regenerated daily
- Scenario simulations run on-demand
- Alerts generated proactively when DSCR < 1.5 or runway < 4 months
- Integrate with FX forecast (task 8), demand forecast (task 9), and orders (task 6)

tasks.title: AI optimization engine with unified recommendations
tasks.description: Implement unified recommendation engine that prioritizes actions across pricing, ordering, hedging, and liquidity management
tasks.details:
Implement AI engine in src/ai_engine/:

**AI Engine service (service.py):**
- `generate_unified_recommendations()`:
  - **Price adjustments:**
    - Call pricing.generate_pricing_recommendations()
    - Convert to Recommendation objects with type=PRICE
    - Priority based on margin gap and revenue impact
  - **Order timing and sizing:**
    - For each product with inventory depletion within lead time:
      - Calculate optimal order date considering FX forecast (lowest predicted rate in next 60 days)
      - Calculate optimal quantity based on demand forecast * lead_time_days * 1.2 (20% buffer)
      - Estimate FX-adjusted cost = (0.3 * current_fx + 0.7 * forecast_fx) * order_value_usd
      - Create Recommendation with type=ORDER_TIMING
    - Priority: HIGH if stock-out within 14 days, MEDIUM within 30 days, LOW beyond
  - **USD accumulation (hedging) strategy:**
    - Query orders with 70% payment due in next 180 days
    - For each order:
      - Total USD needed = 0.7 * order_value_usd
      - Days until arrival = arrival_date - today
      - Weekly purchase amount = USD_needed / (days / 7)
      - Suggest weekly USD purchases at forecasted favorable rates
    - Create Recommendation with type=USD_HEDGE
    - Priority based on amount at risk and FX volatility
  - **Inventory allocation:**
    - If cashflow tight (runway < 4 months):
      - Rank products by margin * turnover_velocity
      - Recommend prioritizing high-margin, fast-moving products for restocking
      - Create Recommendation with type=INVENTORY
  - **Liquidity and DSCR alerts:**
    - If DSCR < 1.5 or cash_runway < 4 months:
      - Recommend corrective actions:
        - Delay non-critical orders
        - Increase prices on low-elasticity products
        - Negotiate loan payment deferral
      - Create Recommendation with type=LIQUIDITY
    - Priority: HIGH if DSCR < 1.0, MEDIUM if DSCR 1.0-1.49
  - **Prioritization algorithm:**
    - Score = financial_impact * urgency * confidence
    - financial_impact = estimated NGN benefit
    - urgency = 1.0 for <7 days, 0.7 for 7-30 days, 0.4 for >30 days
    - confidence = forecast confidence interval width (narrower = higher confidence)
  - Store all recommendations in Recommendation table
  - Return sorted list by priority_score (descending)
- `apply_recommendation(recommendation_id, user_id)`:
  - Route to appropriate service based on recommendation_type:
    - PRICE -> pricing.apply_pricing_recommendation()
    - ORDER_TIMING -> create draft order
    - USD_HEDGE -> create accumulation schedule (manual execution)
    - INVENTORY -> flag in system (manual decision)
    - LIQUIDITY -> flag for user action
  - Mark recommendation status=APPLIED
  - Log application in audit trail
- `dismiss_recommendation(recommendation_id, user_id, reason)`:
  - Mark recommendation status=DISMISSED
  - Store dismissal reason for future model improvement
- `get_active_recommendations()`:
  - Return recommendations with status=PENDING
  - Sorted by priority_score
  - Limit to top 10 for dashboard display

**USD accumulation schedule generation:**
```python
def generate_usd_accumulation_schedule(order):
    usd_needed = Decimal('0.7') * order.total_order_value_usd
    days_until_arrival = (order.estimated_arrival_date - date.today()).days
    weeks = max(1, days_until_arrival // 7)
    
    weekly_amount = usd_needed / weeks
    
    schedule = []
    for week in range(weeks):
        purchase_date = date.today() + timedelta(days=week * 7)
        forecast = fx_service.get_forecast_for_date('NGNGSD', purchase_date)
        schedule.append({
            'week': week + 1,
            'purchase_date': purchase_date,
            'usd_amount': weekly_amount,
            'forecasted_fx_rate': forecast.base_forecast,
            'ngn_amount': weekly_amount * forecast.base_forecast
        })
    
    return schedule
```

**AI Engine router (router.py):**
- POST /ai/generate-recommendations: trigger recommendation generation
- GET /ai/recommendations: get active recommendations (top N)
- GET /ai/recommendations/all: get all recommendations with status filter
- POST /ai/recommendations/{id}/apply: apply a recommendation
- POST /ai/recommendations/{id}/dismiss: dismiss a recommendation
- GET /ai/recommendations/history: get applied/dismissed recommendation history
- GET /ai/usd-accumulation/{order_id}: get USD accumulation schedule for order

**Implementation notes:**
- Recommendations regenerated daily via scheduled task
- Priority scoring uses multi-criteria decision analysis
- Recommendations include clear reasoning and expected impact
- Integration with all other modules (pricing, orders, inventory, cashflow, fx)
- Use async operations for parallel data fetching

tasks.title: Frontend UI/UX design and styling overhaul
tasks.description:
The frontend currently lacks CSS styling — pages render with no visual design. This task covers a complete UI/UX styling overhaul using TailwindCSS v4 and PrimeNG v21 theming to create a polished, professional look for the ModishLog platform.

Scope:
1. **Global theme and design system** — Configure PrimeNG theme (colors, typography, spacing), define CSS custom properties for brand palette, set up consistent spacing/sizing tokens
2. **Login page** — Centered card layout with gradient/branded background, styled form inputs, loading states, error message styling
3. **Shell layout** — Proper sidebar styling (brand logo, active nav highlights, hover states, icons), topbar design (user menu, mobile hamburger), content area padding/max-width
4. **Dashboard page** — Metric cards with proper shadows/borders/colors, grid layout, status badges, alert banners, trend indicators
5. **Data-heavy pages (Sales, Inventory, Orders)** — Table styling (striped rows, hover, responsive), form dialogs, action buttons, status pills, empty states
6. **Chart pages (FX, Cashflow, Pricing)** — Chart container styling, legend positioning, metric cards alongside charts, responsive chart sizing
7. **Recommendations page** — Card-based feed layout, priority color coding, category filter pills, expand/collapse animations
8. **Responsive design** — Mobile sidebar overlay, stacked layouts on small screens, touch-friendly targets, proper breakpoints
9. **Shared components** — Polish metric-card, data-table, alert-banner, status-badge with consistent design language
10. **Micro-interactions** — Button hover/active states, loading spinners, toast notifications, smooth transitions

tasks.title: Set up Neon PostgreSQL staging database
tasks.description: Create modishlog project on Neon and configure staging database branch. Neon free tier provides 0.5 GB storage, branching, and serverless PostgreSQL compatible with asyncpg.
tasks.details:
Steps:
1. Create "modishlog" project on neon.tech (region: aws-eu-central-1 or germanywestcentral nearest equivalent)
2. Create "staging" branch from main in the modishlog project
3. Get the connection string for staging branch (pooled endpoint for asyncpg)
4. Add DATABASE_URL to GitHub repo secrets as STAGING_DATABASE_URL
5. Create .env.staging.example documenting all required environment variables
6. Verify asyncpg connection string format: postgresql+asyncpg://user:pass@ep-xxx-pooler.region.neon.tech/neondb?sslmode=require
tasks.testStrategy: Run alembic upgrade head against staging DB via GitHub Actions job. Verify tables created by querying information_schema. Test connection from backend container.

tasks.title: Build production Docker images and push to GHCR
tasks.description: Create production-ready Dockerfiles for backend and frontend, and set up GitHub Actions workflow to build and push images to GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io/sojisoyoye/modishlog).

2. Create frontend/Dockerfile.prod: multi-stage build (Node 22 build + nginx:alpine serve)
3. Create frontend/nginx.conf: serve Angular SPA, proxy /api to backend
4. Create .github/workflows/build-images.yml: triggers on push to main, builds both images, pushes to ghcr.io/sojisoyoye/modishlog/backend:staging and ghcr.io/sojisoyoye/modishlog/frontend:staging
5. Set GHCR_TOKEN GitHub secret (use existing GitHub PAT from heimpath)
tasks.testStrategy: GitHub Actions build job must succeed. Images must be pullable from ghcr.io. ng build must complete without errors in CI.

tasks.title: Deploy backend staging to Azure Container Apps
tasks.description: Deploy ModishLog backend to Azure Container Apps using docker-compose.staging.yml on the student Azure subscription. Keep within free tier: 180,000 vCPU-seconds/month, 360,000 GiB-seconds/month. Use region germanywestcentral.
tasks.details:
1. Create docker-compose.staging.yml (backend + redis only; DB is on Neon)
2. Create infra/azure/setup-staging.sh: az CLI script to create resource group rg-modishlog-staging, Container App Environment cae-modishlog, deploy via az containerapp compose create
3. Configure Container App: 0.25 CPU / 0.5Gi memory, min_replicas=0 max_replicas=1 (scale to zero saves cost)
4. Set environment variables via --env-vars: DATABASE_URL, SECRET_KEY, REDIS_URL, ENVIRONMENT=staging, CORS_ORIGINS
5. Create GitHub Actions deploy step in deploy-staging.yml: login to Azure with AZURE_CREDENTIALS secret (same service principal as heimpath), update container image
6. Run alembic upgrade head as a Container App Job post-deploy
7. Output backend URL from Container App (https://modishlog-backend-staging.{env}.germanywestcentral.azurecontainerapps.io)
tasks.testStrategy: curl /health endpoint returns 200. Run pytest against staging DB URL. Verify swagger UI accessible at /docs.

tasks.title: Deploy frontend staging to Vercel
tasks.description: Deploy Angular frontend to Vercel free tier. Configure Angular staging environment to point to Azure backend URL. Set up GitHub integration for automatic deploys on push to main.
tasks.details:
1. Create vercel.json: configure build command (npm run build:staging), output dir (dist/modishlog/browser), rewrites for SPA routing
2. Create frontend/src/environments/environment.staging.ts with STAGING_API_URL pointing to Azure Container Apps backend
3. Update frontend/package.json: add build:staging script using --configuration staging
4. Update angular.json: add staging build configuration with fileReplacements for environment.staging.ts
5. Add Vercel environment variable STAGING_API_URL in Vercel project settings
6. Create .github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml step: deploy to Vercel using vercel CLI with --prod flag for staging project
7. Set GitHub secrets: VERCEL_TOKEN, VERCEL_ORG_ID, VERCEL_PROJECT_ID
tasks.testStrategy: Vercel preview URL loads Angular app. API calls from frontend reach Azure backend (check network tab). Login flow works end-to-end.

tasks.title: Fix critical: image tag mismatch in deploy-staging.yml
tasks.description: The build job uses docker/metadata-action with format=short (7-char SHA, e.g. staging-abc1234) but the deploy job references staging-${{ github.sha }} (full 40-char SHA). The Container App update will try to pull a tag that does not exist and fail. Fix: use needs.build-backend.outputs.image_tag in the deploy step.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify the image tag used in az containerapp update matches one of the tags pushed by docker/build-push-action in the same run.

tasks.title: Fix critical: Vercel re-build discards sed substitution for STAGING_API_URL
tasks.description: The deploy-frontend job runs sed on environment.staging.ts locally, then amondnet/vercel-action triggers Vercel to re-build from source. Vercel's machines never see the sed output — __STAGING_API_URL__ remains in the deployed build. Fix: move sed into vercel.json buildCommand so Vercel substitutes it using STAGING_API_URL set as a Vercel project environment variable.
tasks.details:
1. Update frontend/vercel.json buildCommand to:
   "sed -i \"s|__STAGING_API_URL__|$STAGING_API_URL|g\" src/environments/environment.staging.ts && npm run build:staging"
2. Remove the sed + local build steps from deploy-staging.yml deploy-frontend job (let Vercel handle the build)
3. Document in .env.staging.example that STAGING_API_URL must also be set as a Vercel project environment variable (not just a GitHub secret)
tasks.testStrategy: After deploy, check the deployed JS bundle or network requests confirm the API URL is not the literal string __STAGING_API_URL__.

tasks.title: Fix: az containerapp job --args format and missing --subscription flags
tasks.description: Two issues in infra/azure/setup-staging.sh: (1) az containerapp job create uses --args "upgrade,head" with comma separation but Azure CLI expects space-separated args — migration job will fail to run alembic correctly. (2) Individual az containerapp commands do not pass --subscription, risking targeting the wrong subscription if CLI context changes.
tasks.details:
1. Fix migration job command in setup-staging.sh: replace --command "alembic" --args "upgrade,head" with a JSON-array entrypoint or use correct space-separated format per az CLI docs.
2. Add --subscription "$SUBSCRIPTION_ID" to every az containerapp and az containerapp job command in the script.
3. Apply same --subscription flag to az containerapp commands in deploy-staging.yml workflow.
tasks.testStrategy: Dry-run az containerapp job create with --debug to confirm correct command format. Migration job should run alembic upgrade head successfully.

tasks.title: Fix: reduce uvicorn workers to 1 and simplify Vercel SPA rewrite
tasks.description: Two medium/low issues: (1) backend/Dockerfile uses --workers 2 on a 0.25 CPU container — doubles memory and connection pool count against Neon free tier for no benefit at staging scale. Should be 1 worker. (2) frontend/vercel.json uses an overly complex negative-lookahead regex for SPA routing when a simple wildcard is sufficient.
tasks.details:
1. In backend/Dockerfile change --workers 2 to --workers 1
2. In frontend/vercel.json simplify the rewrite: { "source": "/(.*)", "destination": "/index.html" }
tasks.testStrategy: Docker build succeeds. Vercel deploy serves Angular app correctly on all routes including deep links like /products/123.

tasks.title: Forgot password / password reset flow
tasks.description: Implement a complete forgot-password and password-reset flow. User enters their email on a forgot-password page, receives a reset link via email, clicks the link to land on a reset-password page, enters and confirms a new password.
tasks.details: Backend (auth domain): 1) POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password — accepts email, generates a secure random token (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), stores hashed token + expiry (1 hour) in a new PasswordResetToken table (id, user_id FK, token_hash, expires_at, used_at), sends email via SMTP or a transactional email provider (use SMTP env vars: SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASSWORD, FROM_EMAIL). 2) POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password — accepts token + new_password, validates token not expired/used, hashes new password with bcrypt, marks token used. Add Alembic migration. Frontend: add ForgotPasswordPage (/forgot-password) with email input + submit; add ResetPasswordPage (/reset-password?token=xxx) with new-password + confirm inputs. Route both as public (no auth guard). All financial values rule does not apply here. Token must be stored as bcrypt hash, never plaintext.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend: test happy path (valid token resets password), expired token returns 400, already-used token returns 400, unknown email returns 200 (no enumeration). Frontend E2E: fill email → success message shown; navigate to reset URL with valid token → can set new password → redirected to login.

tasks.title: JWT refresh token
tasks.description: Implement a refresh-token mechanism so users are not logged out when their access token expires. Login returns both a short-lived access token (15 min) and a long-lived refresh token (7 days). A POST /api/v1/auth/refresh endpoint issues a new access token given a valid refresh token.
tasks.details: Backend: 1) Add RefreshToken table (id, user_id FK, token_hash, expires_at, revoked_at, created_at) with Alembic migration. 2) Update POST /api/v1/auth/login to also generate and return a refresh_token (opaque random token via secrets.token_urlsafe(64), stored hashed). 3) Add POST /api/v1/auth/refresh — accepts {refresh_token}, validates not expired/revoked, issues new access_token (and optionally rotates the refresh token). 4) Add POST /api/v1/auth/logout — revokes the refresh token. Update ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES default to 15. Add REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS=7 config setting. Frontend: store refresh_token in localStorage alongside access_token. In the HTTP interceptor, on 401 response, attempt one silent refresh via POST /auth/refresh; if refresh succeeds, retry the original request; if refresh fails, redirect to /login. Update AuthService to handle token rotation.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend: test refresh with valid token returns new access token; expired refresh token returns 401; revoked token returns 401; logout revokes token so subsequent refresh fails. Frontend E2E: simulate access token expiry, verify interceptor silently refreshes and original request retries successfully.

tasks.testStrategy: Playwright E2E: toggle shows/hides password text; input type switches between password and text on each click.

tasks.title: Forgot password / password reset flow
tasks.description: Implement a full forgot-password and password-reset flow: user enters email to request a reset link, backend sends a time-limited token via email, user clicks link and sets a new password.
tasks.details: Backend (src/auth/): Add POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password (accepts email, generates a secure token stored in a new PasswordResetToken table with expiry, sends email via SMTP or a simple email service). Add POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password (accepts token + new_password, validates token not expired/used, hashes new password, marks token used). New DB model: PasswordResetToken(id UUID PK, user_id FK, token str unique, expires_at datetime, used_at datetime nullable). Use python-jose or secrets.token_urlsafe for token generation. Token expiry: 1 hour. Frontend: Add "Forgot password?" link on login page → /forgot-password page (email input form). Add /reset-password?token=... page (new password + confirm fields). Both pages are standalone Angular components with OnPush + Signals. Write backend tests: happy path request + reset, expired token error, already-used token error. Write Playwright E2E for the UI flows.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend: pytest happy path (request token, reset with it), expired token returns 400, used token returns 400, invalid token returns 404. Frontend Playwright: forgot-password form submission shows confirmation message; reset-password form with valid token sets new password and redirects to login.

tasks.title: JWT refresh token
tasks.description: Implement JWT refresh tokens so users stay logged in without re-authenticating after the access token expires. Access token: 15 min. Refresh token: 30 days, stored httpOnly cookie or localStorage.
tasks.details: Backend (src/auth/): Shorten ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES to 15. Add a RefreshToken model (id UUID PK, user_id FK, token str unique, expires_at datetime, revoked bool default false). On login, issue both access_token and refresh_token. Add POST /api/v1/auth/refresh (accepts refresh token in request body or cookie, validates not expired/revoked, returns new access_token and rotates refresh_token — revoke old, issue new). Add POST /api/v1/auth/logout (revokes the refresh token). Frontend (auth service): Intercept 401 responses in the HTTP interceptor — attempt a silent refresh via POST /auth/refresh, retry the original request with the new access token, redirect to login if refresh also fails. Store refresh token in localStorage alongside the access token. Write backend tests: refresh issues new token + revokes old, expired refresh token returns 401, revoked token returns 401. Write Playwright E2E: after token expires (mock), app auto-refreshes and stays logged in.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend pytest: happy path refresh, expired token 401, revoked token 401, logout revokes token. Frontend: interceptor retries original request after 401 + silent refresh; redirect to login if refresh fails.

tasks.title: Bulk order import via CSV/Excel file upload
tasks.description:
Add the ability to mass-create purchase orders by uploading a CSV or Excel (.xlsx) file from the orders page. Users download a template, fill in one row per line item (same supplier_name groups rows into one order), upload the file, preview the parsed rows, then submit to create all orders at once.

Required template columns: supplier_name, currency, line_item_sku, line_item_quantity, line_item_unit_cost.
Optional columns: supplier_contact, is_purchase_order (TRUE/FALSE), pay_term_number, pay_term_type (days/months), shipping_cost, clearing_cost, notes, discount_type (percentage/fixed), discount_amount, tax_rate, supplier_invoice_number, supplier_invoice_date (YYYY-MM-DD).
tasks.details:
Backend (orders domain):
1. GET /api/v1/orders/import/template — returns a CSV download with header row + one example data row. Static route; must be registered before /{order_id}.
2. POST /api/v1/orders/import — accepts multipart/form-data with a 'file' field (.csv or .xlsx). Parse with Python csv module for CSV and openpyxl for xlsx (no pandas). Group consecutive rows by supplier_name (blank = continue previous order). Validate required columns present; validate each line item SKU exists in products table; resolve product_id from SKU. Collect all errors before responding — never partially commit. On success: { created: N, orders: [OrderRead] }. On any error: { created: 0, errors: [{row: N, message: str}] } with HTTP 422.

4. Add openpyxl to backend requirements.

Frontend (orders-page.component.ts):

2. Import dialog with three sections: (a) Download Template anchor that hits GET /orders/import/template, (b) file drop-zone accepting .csv and .xlsx with drag-and-drop support, (c) preview table showing filename + row count after file is selected.
3. On upload success: dismiss dialog, show toast X orders created, reload list.
4. On error: show scrollable table of row number + error message inside the dialog.
5. New OrdersService.importOrders(file: File) — POST multipart FormData.
6. New OrdersService.getImportTemplateUrl() — returns the API URL string for the template download anchor.
