tasks.title: Add sell_price_ngn per order line item to seal revenue history
tasks.description: Record the actual selling price charged at order time on each line item, so historical profit calculations remain accurate even after the product's catalog price changes.
tasks.details:
## Context
Currently `productSellingPrice()` on the order detail page reads the live catalog price from the products list. This means if the product price is updated, every historical order's gross profit figure changes retroactively — which is wrong. The unit cost side is already frozen via `unit_cost_ngn` on `OrderLineItem`; the revenue side needs the same treatment.

## Backend

**Migration** (`backend/alembic/versions/`):
- Add column `sell_price_ngn: Numeric(18, 6), nullable=True` to `order_line_items` table
- Check existing migration IDs before choosing a new revision ID (avoid collision — see memory note about `d5e6f7a8b9c0` collision in prior session)

**Model** (`backend/src/orders/models.py`):
- Add `sell_price_ngn: Mapped[Optional[Decimal]] = mapped_column(Numeric(18, 6), nullable=True)` to `OrderLineItem`

**Schemas** (`backend/src/orders/schemas.py`):
- Add `sell_price_ngn: Optional[Decimal] = None` to `OrderLineItemCreate` and `OrderLineItemRead`

**Service** (`backend/src/orders/service.py`):
- Pass `sell_price_ngn` through in `create_order` and `update_order` — same pattern as `unit_cost_ngn`

## Frontend (`frontend/src/app/features/orders/pages/order-detail-page.component.ts`)

**Edit mode**: Add an editable NGN sell price input per line item row, shown next to the existing NGN unit cost input. Only visible for edit mode. Placeholder should show the current catalog sell price as a fallback.

**View mode**: Show the stored `sell_price_ngn` if set; otherwise show catalog price with "(catalog)" label to indicate it's not locked.

**Profit calculations**: Update `productSellingPrice(productId, item)` to prefer `item.sell_price_ngn` over the catalog price. Update `totalRevenueNGN()`, `marginNGN()`, `marginPct()` accordingly.

**`canComputeProfitOverview()`**: Should be satisfied if any line item has either `sell_price_ngn` set or a catalog price > 0.

## Seeding existing orders
- When the user first opens an existing order in edit mode and saves, `sell_price_ngn` will be null for old line items — the frontend should auto-populate `sell_price_ngn` from the current catalog price on save if the field is still null, so the price gets locked from that point forward.

## Rules
- All financial values: Python Decimal, never float
- Static routes before parameterized routes
- Use `selectinload()` before returning ORM objects
- Run `pytest backend/tests/` before committing
- Run `ng build` before committing
tasks.testStrategy:
**Backend (write BEFORE implementation):**
1. `test_create_order_with_sell_price_ngn` — create order with `sell_price_ngn` set, verify it is stored and returned in `OrderLineItemRead`
2. `test_update_order_sell_price_ngn` — update an existing line item's `sell_price_ngn`, verify the new value is persisted
3. `test_sell_price_ngn_defaults_null` — create order without `sell_price_ngn`, verify field is null (not 0)
4. `test_profit_calc_uses_sell_price_override` — verify gross profit uses `sell_price_ngn` when set, not catalog price

**Frontend E2E (Playwright, `frontend/e2e/order-sell-price.spec.ts`):**
1. In edit mode, enter a sell price for a line item, save, verify the value is displayed in view mode
2. Verify margin % column updates live as sell price is changed in edit mode
3. Verify profit overview headline figures reflect the overridden sell price after save

tasks.title: FX rate service — fetch live USD/NGN rate from free API with caching
tasks.description: Build a backend FX rate service that fetches the current USD/NGN exchange rate from a free public API, caches it (4-hour TTL) in the database, and exposes a /api/fx/rates endpoint. The frontend uses this to auto-populate the FX rate on order creation and to power the price suggestion engine.
tasks.details:
## Context
Currently users must type the exchange rate manually when creating an order. The rate also needs to be available to the price suggestion engine (Task 4). The FX rate fluctuates daily; we need a live source with caching to avoid hammering the API.

## External API
Use the ExchangeRate-API free open endpoint — no API key required, updated every 24 hours. Supports NGN. Endpoint pattern: `https://open.er-api.com/v6/latest/USD`.

Optionally support a paid-tier API key via env var `FX_API_KEY` in `.env` — if set, use the authenticated endpoint for higher request limits.

## Backend

**New domain** (`backend/src/fx/`):
- `models.py`: `FxRateCache` model — `id`, `currency_pair` (String, e.g. "USD/NGN"), `rate` (Numeric 18,6), `fetched_at` (DateTime timezone=True), `source` (String). Unique constraint on `currency_pair`.
- `service.py`: 
  - `get_current_rate(currency_pair="USD/NGN") -> Decimal` — check DB cache first; if `fetched_at` < 4 hours ago return cached rate; otherwise fetch from API, store/update, return rate.
  - `fetch_from_api(currency_pair) -> Decimal` — async HTTP call using `httpx.AsyncClient` (add `httpx` to requirements if not present). Parse the JSON response. Log on fetch and on cache hit via structlog.
  - Handle API errors gracefully: if fetch fails and cache is stale, return the stale cached rate with a warning log rather than raising.
- `router.py`: `GET /api/fx/rates` — returns `{ "USD_NGN": rate, "fetched_at": iso_string, "cached": bool }`. Register in `main.py`.
- `schemas.py`: `FxRateResponse` Pydantic schema.
- Alembic migration for `fx_rate_cache` table.

**Config** (`backend/src/core/config.py`):
- Add `FX_API_KEY: Optional[str] = None` and `FX_CACHE_TTL_HOURS: int = 4`.

## Frontend

**Service** (`frontend/src/app/core/services/fx.service.ts`):
- `getCurrentRate(): Observable<FxRateResponse>` — calls `GET /api/fx/rates`.
- `FxRateResponse` model: `{ usd_ngn: number; fetched_at: string; cached: boolean }`.

**Order create form** (`frontend/src/app/features/orders/pages/create-order-page.component.ts`):
- On page load (for USD orders), auto-call `FxService.getCurrentRate()` and pre-fill the FX rate field. Show a small "Live rate" chip next to the field. User can still override manually.

**Order detail edit mode** (`order-detail-page.component.ts`):
- When user clicks into edit mode, if `fx_rate_at_creation` is null, auto-fetch and fill it.

## Rules
- Never call the external API from the frontend (CORS / key exposure)
- Use `structlog` logger, never `print()`
- All rate values: Python Decimal
- Write tests before implementation
tasks.testStrategy:
**Backend (write BEFORE implementation):**
1. `test_get_current_rate_cache_hit` — seed a fresh `FxRateCache` row, call `get_current_rate()`, verify no HTTP call is made and cached rate is returned
2. `test_get_current_rate_cache_miss` — seed a stale cache row (> 4h old), mock the external API response, call `get_current_rate()`, verify rate is updated in DB
3. `test_get_current_rate_api_failure_uses_stale` — mock API to raise an exception, seed stale cache, verify stale rate is returned with no exception raised
4. `test_fx_rates_endpoint` — GET `/api/fx/rates`, expect 200 with `usd_ngn` and `fetched_at` fields
5. `test_fx_rates_endpoint_no_cache` — with empty cache and mocked API, verify endpoint fetches and returns rate

**Frontend E2E:**
1. On order create form (USD selected), verify FX rate field is auto-populated within 3 seconds of page load
2. Verify user can still manually override the auto-filled rate

tasks.title: Lot inventory tracking — link delivered order line items to stock with units_remaining
tasks.description: When an order transitions to DELIVERED, each line item becomes a stock lot. Track how many units from each lot remain in stock as sales are recorded, so the order detail page can show live lot inventory and product history page can show cost-basis per lot.
tasks.details:
## Context
Currently inventory is tracked globally per product (`InventoryLevel.current_stock`). There is no linkage between "which order did this stock come from" and "how many of those units are still unsold." We need lot-level tracking to:
1. Show on the order detail page: "50 units received — 30 remaining in stock from this lot"
2. Power the price suggestion engine (Task 4): weighted-average landed cost across active lots
3. Enable a product history page showing all lots with their cost basis

## Backend

**Model** (`backend/src/orders/models.py`):
- Add `units_remaining: Mapped[Optional[Decimal]] = mapped_column(Numeric(18, 6), nullable=True)` to `OrderLineItem`.
- `units_remaining` starts as `null` (pre-delivery). On DELIVERED transition it is set to `quantity`.

**Service** (`backend/src/orders/service.py`):
- In the status-update logic (wherever `status` is written), detect transition TO `DELIVERED`:
  - For each line item in the order, set `item.units_remaining = item.quantity`.
  - Create a `StockMovement` record (type=PURCHASE) for each line item and update `InventoryLevel.current_stock` — this replaces/enhances whatever the existing delivery handler does.

**Lot deduction on sale** (`backend/src/sales/service.py`):
- When a `DailySales` record is created for a product, find the oldest active lot for that product (lowest `order.order_date`, `units_remaining > 0`) and deduct the sold quantity from it (FIFO). If the lot runs out, spill over to the next lot.
- If no active lot covers the quantity (e.g. older manual stock), deduct from `InventoryLevel` only and log a warning.

**New endpoint** (`backend/src/orders/router.py`):
- `GET /api/orders/{order_id}/lots` — returns each line item with `units_remaining`, `quantity`, `unit_cost_ngn`, `sell_price_ngn`, `product_id`, product name.

**Migration**: Add `units_remaining` column to `order_line_items`. Check for existing revision IDs before creating.

## Frontend

**Order detail page** (`order-detail-page.component.ts`):
- In the line items table, add a "In Stock" column showing `units_remaining` if the order is DELIVERED and `units_remaining` is not null. Show "—" for non-delivered orders.
- Color-code: green if `units_remaining > 0`, grey if `0`.

**Product detail page** (future page — at minimum, expose the lot data via the endpoint for later use).

## Rules
- FIFO deduction: always deduct from the oldest lot first
- Use `selectinload()` before returning ORM objects
- Decimal everywhere, never float
- Write tests before implementation
tasks.testStrategy:
**Backend (write BEFORE implementation):**
1. `test_order_delivered_sets_units_remaining` — transition order to DELIVERED, verify each line item has `units_remaining == quantity`
2. `test_sale_deducts_fifo_from_lot` — create 2 delivered orders for the same product, record a sale, verify oldest lot is deducted first
3. `test_sale_spills_to_next_lot` — sell more than the oldest lot's `units_remaining`, verify both lots are correctly decremented
4. `test_lots_endpoint` — GET `/api/orders/{id}/lots`, verify response includes `units_remaining` per line item
5. `test_units_remaining_null_before_delivery` — verify `units_remaining` is null for PENDING/SHIPPING orders

**Frontend E2E:**
1. Deliver a test order, verify "In Stock" column shows correct quantities on order detail page
2. Record a sale for a product from that lot, verify the count decrements on next order detail load

tasks.title: Price suggestion engine — compute and track sell price recommendations from lot cost + live FX + target margin
tasks.description: Build a pricing engine that computes recommended selling prices for each product based on its lot cost basis, the current live FX rate, and a configurable target margin. Store a history of suggestions so users can see how the recommended price has evolved as the exchange rate changes.
tasks.details:
## Context
When the NGN/USD rate moves, the cost to restock imported goods changes — and therefore the minimum viable selling price changes too. This engine answers: "Given my landed cost and today's FX rate, what should I charge per unit to hit my target margin?" It also stores a history so the user can see the trend over time.

This builds on:
- Task 73 (`sell_price_ngn`) — locked historical sell prices per lot
- Task 74 (FX rate service) — live rate from API
- Task 75 (lot tracking) — `units_remaining` and cost basis per lot

## Backend

**New model** (`backend/src/pricing/models.py` — extend existing file):
- `PriceSuggestion`: `id` (UUID), `product_id` (FK), `source_order_id` (FK, nullable — null means blended/average), `unit_cost_ngn` (Numeric 18,6 — landed cost at time of suggestion), `fx_rate_used` (Numeric 18,6), `target_margin_pct` (Numeric 5,4, default 0.40), `suggested_price_ngn` (Numeric 18,6), `current_catalog_price_ngn` (Numeric 18,6), `suggested_at` (DateTime timezone=True), `notes` (Text, nullable).
- Formula: `suggested_price_ngn = unit_cost_ngn / (1 - target_margin_pct)` where `unit_cost_ngn` = weighted-average landed cost of active lots at the given FX rate.

**Service** (`backend/src/pricing/service.py`):
- `compute_suggestion(product_id, target_margin=0.40) -> PriceSuggestion`:
  1. Fetch all active lots for the product (from `order_line_items` where `units_remaining > 0`)
  2. Get current FX rate via `FxRateService.get_current_rate()`
  3. Compute weighted-average `unit_cost_ngn`:
     - For each lot: `cost_ngn = (item.unit_cost_ngn or (item.unit_cost * fx_rate)) * item.units_remaining`
     - Weighted avg = sum(cost_ngn) / sum(units_remaining)
  4. Apply formula: `suggested_price = weighted_avg_cost / (1 - target_margin)`
  5. Persist `PriceSuggestion` record and return it
- `get_suggestion_history(product_id, limit=30) -> list[PriceSuggestion]`

**Router** (`backend/src/pricing/router.py`):
- `POST /api/pricing/suggest/{product_id}` — body: `{ target_margin_pct?: float }` — runs `compute_suggestion`, returns result
- `GET /api/pricing/suggest/{product_id}/history` — returns last 30 suggestions for the product

**Migration**: Add `price_suggestions` table.

## Frontend

**Product detail page** (or a dedicated "Pricing" tab):
- "Suggest Price" button that calls `POST /api/pricing/suggest/{product_id}`
- Shows result: "Suggested ₦X at ₦Y/$ (40% margin)" with target margin slider (30%–60%)
- Suggestion history table: date | FX rate | landed cost | suggested price | catalog price at time

**Order detail page — Profit Overview card**:
- Add a "Restock Cost Today" row showing what the same goods would cost at the current FX rate (fetched via `/api/fx/rates`). This makes the historical-vs-today delta visible.

## Rules
- Weighted average across active lots only (`units_remaining > 0`)
- Never float for financial calculations — Python Decimal throughout
- `structlog` logger for suggestion events
- Write tests before implementation
- Alembic migration for new table
tasks.testStrategy:
**Backend (write BEFORE implementation):**
1. `test_compute_suggestion_single_lot` — one active lot, verify formula: `cost / (1 - margin)`
2. `test_compute_suggestion_weighted_average` — two active lots with different costs and quantities, verify weighted average is used
3. `test_compute_suggestion_uses_live_fx` — mock FX service, verify returned suggestion uses mocked rate
4. `test_compute_suggestion_no_active_lots` — verify raises a clear `PricingError` (not a 500) when no lots with `units_remaining > 0` exist
5. `test_suggestion_history_endpoint` — POST suggest twice, GET history, verify both records returned newest-first
6. `test_target_margin_override` — pass 0.35 as target margin, verify suggested price uses 35% not default 40%

**Frontend E2E:**
1. On product detail, click "Suggest Price", verify suggestion appears with correct FX rate and margin displayed
2. Move the margin slider, verify suggested price updates live
3. After two suggestions, verify history table shows both entries

tasks.title: Fix orders list pipeline status cards showing wrong counts
tasks.description: The summary cards on the orders list page (Pending, In Production, Shipping, Cleared, Delivered) always show 0 orders because the pipelineStatuses array uses display-cased strings that don't match the uppercase enum values returned by the API.
tasks.details:
## Root cause

`orders-page.component.ts` line 821:
```typescript
readonly pipelineStatuses = ['ORDERED', 'Pending', 'In Production', 'Shipping', 'Cleared', 'Delivered'];
```

The backend `OrderStatus` enum returns: `ORDERED`, `PENDING`, `IN_PRODUCTION`, `SHIPPING`, `CLEARED`, `DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`.

`ordersByStatus(status)` does a strict equality filter (`o.status === status`), so only `'ORDERED'` ever matches. The other 5 cards always show 0 even when orders exist in those states.

## Fix

1. Change `pipelineStatuses` to the correct uppercase API values:
```typescript
readonly pipelineStatuses = ['ORDERED', 'PENDING', 'IN_PRODUCTION', 'SHIPPING', 'CLEARED', 'DELIVERED'] as const;
```

2. Add a display-label mapping so the card headings stay human-readable (the template currently uses the `uppercase` CSS class but the label text still shows the raw value):
```typescript
readonly statusLabel: Record<string, string> = {
  ORDERED: 'Ordered',
  PENDING: 'Pending',
  IN_PRODUCTION: 'In Production',
  SHIPPING: 'Shipping',
  CLEARED: 'Cleared',
  DELIVERED: 'Delivered',
};
```

3. Update the card heading in the template from `{{ status }}` to `{{ statusLabel[status] }}`.

## Rules
- No float, no raw SQL — frontend only change
- Run `ng build` before committing
tasks.testStrategy:
**Frontend E2E (Playwright, `frontend/e2e/orders-pipeline-cards.spec.ts`):**
1. Seed orders in several different statuses via the API; load the orders list page; verify each pipeline card shows the correct non-zero count matching the number of seeded orders for that status.
2. Transition an order to a new status, reload the page, verify the source and destination card counts update correctly.
3. Verify the card heading displays the human-readable label (e.g. "In Production") not the raw enum string (e.g. "IN_PRODUCTION").

tasks.title: Stock count — log physical inventory counts and calculate variance against system stock
tasks.description: Allow users to conduct a full stock take, recording physically-counted quantities per product or per lot (purchase order line item) on a chosen date. The system calculates variance (counted minus system snapshot) so shortages and surpluses are immediately visible. Counts are read-only after finalisation to preserve the audit trail.
tasks.details:
## Context

Stock is tracked at two levels already:
- **Product level**: `InventoryLevel.current_stock` (total units on hand)
- **Lot level**: `OrderLineItem.units_remaining` (units left in each delivered purchase order, from Task #75)

A stock count session lets the user say "on this date I physically counted X units" and see where the system disagrees.

## Count types

- **PRODUCT** — one row per product; system quantity from `InventoryLevel.current_stock`
- **LOT** — one row per active lot (`units_remaining > 0`); system quantity from `OrderLineItem.units_remaining`

The type is chosen when creating the session and is immutable.

## Backend

### Models (`backend/src/inventory/models.py` or new `backend/src/stockcount/` domain)

```python
class StockCountStatus(str, enum.Enum):
    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
    FINALIZED = "FINALIZED"

class StockCountType(str, enum.Enum):
    PRODUCT = "PRODUCT"
    LOT = "LOT"

class StockCount(UUIDMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
    __tablename__ = "stock_counts"
    count_date: date
    count_type: StockCountType  # PRODUCT | LOT
    status: StockCountStatus    # DRAFT | FINALIZED
    notes: str | None
    created_by: UUID (FK users.id)
    finalized_at: datetime | None

class StockCountItem(UUIDMixin, Base):
    __tablename__ = "stock_count_items"
    stock_count_id: UUID (FK stock_counts.id, ondelete=CASCADE)
    product_id: UUID (FK products.id)
    order_line_item_id: UUID | None (FK order_line_items.id) — set for LOT type, null for PRODUCT
    system_quantity_at_count: Decimal(18,6) | None  # null until finalization; snapshotted from live stock at finalize time
    counted_quantity: Decimal(18,6) | None  # null until entered
    variance: Decimal computed on read: counted_quantity - system_quantity_at_count (null until finalized)
    notes: str | None
```

### Service (`backend/src/stockcount/service.py`)

- `create_stock_count(db, count_date, count_type, notes, user_id) -> StockCount`:
  - Creates the header
  - For PRODUCT: queries all products, creates one `StockCountItem` per product with `system_quantity_at_count = null` (snapshot deferred to finalization)
  - For LOT: queries all `OrderLineItem` where `units_remaining > 0`, creates one item per lot with `system_quantity_at_count = null`
- `update_count_item(db, item_id, counted_quantity) -> StockCountItem`: updates counted_quantity; only allowed in DRAFT
- `finalize_stock_count(db, stock_count_id) -> StockCount`: snapshots live system stock into `system_quantity_at_count` for every item (PRODUCT: reads `InventoryLevel.current_stock`; LOT: reads `OrderLineItem.units_remaining`), then sets status=FINALIZED, finalized_at=now(). Stock that moved between session creation and finalization is correctly captured — the variance reflects system state at the moment you committed the count, not when you started it.
- `get_stock_count(db, stock_count_id) -> StockCount` with items selectinloaded
- `list_stock_counts(db) -> list[StockCount]` newest-first

### Schemas
- `StockCountCreate`: count_date, count_type, notes
- `StockCountRead`: header fields + items list
- `StockCountItemRead`: product_id, product_name, order_line_item_id, system_quantity_at_count, counted_quantity, variance (counted_quantity - system_quantity_at_count; null until finalized)
- `StockCountItemUpdate`: counted_quantity

### Router (`backend/src/stockcount/router.py`)
- `POST /api/stockcount/` — create session (requires auth)
- `GET /api/stockcount/` — list all (requires auth)
- `GET /api/stockcount/{id}` — detail with items (requires auth)
- `PATCH /api/stockcount/{id}/items/{item_id}` — update counted_quantity (DRAFT only)
- `POST /api/stockcount/{id}/finalize` — finalize (DRAFT only)

Register in `main.py`.

### Migration
New tables: `stock_counts`, `stock_count_items`. Use `values_callable` on Enum columns.

## Frontend

### New page: `frontend/src/app/features/stockcount/pages/`

**Stock count list page** (`/stock-counts`):
- Table of past stock count sessions: date | type | status | items counted | created by
- "New Stock Count" button → opens creation dialog

**Creation dialog**:
- Date picker (count_date)
- Radio: Product-level / Lot-level
- Optional notes
- On confirm → POST, navigate to detail page

**Stock count detail page** (`/stock-counts/:id`):
- Header: date, type, status, notes, "Finalise" button (only in DRAFT)
- Table of items:
  - For PRODUCT: Product name | System qty | Counted qty (editable input in DRAFT) | Variance (colour-coded: red=negative, green=positive, grey=zero/null)
  - For LOT: Product name | Order # | System qty | Counted qty | Variance
- Variance column: negative = red badge, positive = green badge, zero = grey, null = "—"
- "Finalise" button: confirms via dialog, then POST /finalize

Add route and nav link in the sidebar (under Inventory section).

## Rules
- Python Decimal, never float
- `structlog` logger, never print()
- `selectinload()` on all relationships before returning
- Static routes before parameterised routes
- `values_callable` on all new Enum columns
- Write tests before implementation
- `ng build` before committing
tasks.testStrategy:
**Backend (write BEFORE implementation):**
1. `test_create_product_stock_count` — create a PRODUCT-type session; verify one StockCountItem is created per product with correct system_quantity snapshot
2. `test_create_lot_stock_count` — create a LOT-type session; verify one item per active lot (units_remaining > 0) with system_quantity = units_remaining
3. `test_update_counted_quantity` — PATCH an item in DRAFT; verify counted_quantity and variance are updated
4. `test_update_rejected_when_finalized` — attempt PATCH after finalise; expect 422
5. `test_finalize_stock_count` — finalize a DRAFT; verify status=FINALIZED, finalized_at is set
6. `test_variance_calculation` — counted_quantity=80, system_quantity=100 → variance=-20; counted=110 → variance=+10
7. `test_system_quantity_snapshotted_at_finalization` — create session; change InventoryLevel.current_stock after creation but before finalization; finalize; verify StockCountItem.system_quantity_at_count matches the stock level AT finalization time, not at creation time

**Frontend E2E (Playwright, `frontend/e2e/stock-count.spec.ts`):**
1. Create a PRODUCT-type stock count; verify all products appear in the detail page with system quantities
2. Enter counted quantities for each product; verify variance column updates with correct colour coding
3. Create a LOT-type stock count; verify active lots appear with correct order numbers
4. Finalise a count; verify inputs become read-only and status shows FINALIZED
5. Verify a finalised count appears in the stock counts list with correct date and type

tasks.title: Add sub-categories to product categories (parent/child hierarchy)
tasks.description: Allow product categories to have sub-categories via a self-referential parent_id FK. For example, "Edge Tape" (parent) → "Matt", "Embossed", "Gloss" (children). Products can be assigned to a sub-category or directly to a top-level category.
tasks.details:
## Backend

### Migration
- Add `parent_id: UUID | None` (FK to `product_categories.id`, ondelete=SET NULL, nullable) to `product_categories` table
- Add index on `parent_id`

### Model (`backend/src/products/models.py`)
- Add `parent_id: Mapped[Optional[uuid.UUID]] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("product_categories.id", ondelete="SET NULL"), nullable=True, default=None)`
- Add relationships: `parent: Mapped[Optional["ProductCategory"]] = relationship(back_populates="children", remote_side=[id], lazy="raise")` and `children: Mapped[list["ProductCategory"]] = relationship(back_populates="parent", lazy="raise")`

### Schemas (`backend/src/products/schemas.py`)
- Add `parent_id: Optional[uuid.UUID] = None` to `CategoryCreate` and `CategoryRead`
- Add `CategoryRead` to `CategoryRead` as `children: list["CategoryRead"] = []` (nested read schema for tree display)
- Add `CategoryTreeRead` schema: full tree including children, used by the GET /products/categories endpoint

### Service
- `list_categories()`: return categories with `selectinload(ProductCategory.children)` so children are available
- `create_category()`: accept `parent_id`, validate that parent exists and is itself a top-level category (max 2 levels — no grandchildren)
- GET `/products/categories` returns full tree (top-level categories with their children nested)

### Rules
- Maximum 2 levels deep (category → sub-category only, no sub-sub-categories)
- A sub-category cannot itself be a parent

## Frontend

### Category selector on product create/edit
- Replace the flat `<select>` with a grouped selector: top-level categories as `<optgroup>`, sub-categories as `<option>` inside
- If a top-level category has no children, it can be selected directly as a product category

### Category management (Settings or Products page)
- When creating a category, show an optional "Parent category" dropdown to make it a sub-category
- Display categories as a tree (indented list) in the category list

## Rules
- `selectinload()` on relationships before returning
- `values_callable` not needed here (no new Enum columns)
- Write tests before implementation
tasks.testStrategy:
**Backend:**
1. `test_create_subcategory` — create a child category with parent_id set; verify it appears under the parent in list_categories
2. `test_create_category_max_depth` — attempt to create a sub-category whose parent is itself a sub-category; expect a validation error (max 2 levels)
3. `test_list_categories_tree` — verify GET /products/categories returns nested structure with children array
4. `test_product_assigned_to_subcategory` — create product with a sub-category id; verify it reads back correctly

**Frontend E2E:**
1. Create a top-level category then a sub-category under it; verify the sub-category appears indented in the list
2. Create a product and assign it to a sub-category via the grouped selector; verify it displays the sub-category name in the product list

tasks.title: Category-aware price suggestions — default margin per category/sub-category
tasks.description: Store a default target margin percentage on each product category (and sub-category). When the price suggestion engine runs for a product, it pre-fills the margin from the product's category (sub-category margin overrides parent margin; both fall back to the system default of 40% if unset). This removes the need for users to manually set the margin each time for products in the same category.
tasks.details:
## Context

Depends on task #79 (sub-categories). The price suggestion engine (`POST /api/pricing/suggest/{product_id}`) currently defaults to 40% margin unless the caller overrides it. With category-aware margins, each product carries its category's configured margin automatically.

## Backend

### Migration
- Add `default_margin_pct: Numeric(5, 4) | None` (nullable) to `product_categories`
- Null means "not configured — inherit from parent or use system default"

### Model (`backend/src/products/models.py`)
- Add `default_margin_pct: Mapped[Optional[Decimal]] = mapped_column(Numeric(5, 4), nullable=True, default=None)`

### Schemas
- Add `default_margin_pct: Optional[Decimal] = None` to `CategoryCreate`, `CategoryRead`, `CategoryTreeRead`

### Service (`backend/src/pricing/service.py`) — `compute_suggestion`
- After fetching active lots, load the product's category (and parent category if sub-category)
- Resolve effective margin: `sub_category.default_margin_pct ?? parent_category.default_margin_pct ?? Decimal("0.40")`
- Use resolved margin as the default when `target_margin` is not explicitly passed by the caller

### Router (`backend/src/pricing/router.py`)
- `SuggestRequest.target_margin_pct` is now optional (omit it → use category default)
- If provided, the caller's value overrides the category default (existing behaviour)

## Frontend

### Products page — Suggest Price panel
- After clicking "Suggest Price", the margin slider pre-fills with the product's category default margin (fetched as part of the product's category data)
- If no category margin is configured, defaults to 40% as before
- User can still move the slider to override

### Category management (Settings or Products page)
- Add a "Default margin %" input field to the category create/edit form (optional, 0–100 %)
- Display the configured margin next to each category in the list

## Rules
- Decimal everywhere, no float
- Margin inheritance: sub-category → parent → system default (40%)
- Explicit caller override always wins over category default
- Write tests before implementation
tasks.testStrategy:
**Backend:**
1. `test_compute_suggestion_uses_category_margin` — product with category having default_margin_pct=0.35; call compute_suggestion without explicit margin; verify 35% is used
2. `test_compute_suggestion_inherits_parent_margin` — product in sub-category with no margin; parent has 0.30; verify 30% is inherited
3. `test_compute_suggestion_explicit_overrides_category` — product has category margin 0.35; pass target_margin=0.50 explicitly; verify 50% is used
4. `test_compute_suggestion_falls_back_to_default` — product in category with no margin and no parent; verify 40% system default is used

**Frontend E2E:**
1. Set a default margin on a category; open Suggest Price for a product in that category; verify the slider pre-fills with that margin
2. Move the slider after opening; verify the override value is used instead

tasks.title: E2E Chrome tests — tasks #73, #75, #76, #78 user journey validation
tasks.description: Write and run Playwright E2E tests in Chrome covering the full user journeys for the four features: sell price per line item (#73), lot inventory tracking (#75), price suggestion engine (#76), and stock count (#78). Tests must simulate real user interactions against the running backend — no mocks.
tasks.details:
## Scope

Each feature gets its own spec file (or extend existing ones if they exist). All tests run in Chrome (`chromium` project in playwright.config.ts) against the local dev stack (`http://localhost:4200` frontend, `http://localhost:8000` backend).

---

### #73 — Sell price per line item (`e2e/order-sell-price.spec.ts`)
- Create a USD order and add a line item; verify `sell_price_ngn` field is visible and editable
- Save the order; reload; confirm the stored sell price is shown (not the catalog price)
- Edit the line item sell price to a different value; save; reload; confirm the new value persists
- Verify the revenue total on the order detail reflects the stored sell price

### #75 — Lot inventory tracking (`e2e/order-lot-tracking.spec.ts`)
- Create a USD order, add line items, transition it to DELIVERED
- On the order detail page verify the "In Stock" column appears with the correct `units_remaining` value
- Navigate to the order lots endpoint (`GET /api/orders/{id}/lots`) via the UI or direct assertion and confirm lot records exist
- Create a sale for a product with an open lot; verify `units_remaining` decreases (FIFO deduction)

### #76 — Price suggestion engine (`e2e/price-suggestion.spec.ts`)
- Navigate to the Products page; open the action menu for a product that has delivered lots
- Click "Suggest Price"; verify the margin slider is visible (range 20–70%)
- Adjust the slider to a specific margin (e.g. 40%); confirm the suggested price, avg cost, FX rate, and margin % are displayed
- Submit a second suggestion with a different margin; verify both appear in suggestion history

### #78 — Stock count (`e2e/stock-count.spec.ts`)
- Navigate to `/stock-counts`; create a new stock count
- Add at least two line items with physical counts that differ from system stock
- Submit the stock count; verify it transitions to COMPLETED status
- Confirm the variance values shown match the difference between physical and system counts
- Verify a completed stock count is read-only (edit controls disabled/hidden)

---

## Acceptance criteria
- All specs pass with `npx playwright test --project=chromium` against the running local stack
- No test uses `page.route()` to mock API calls — all hits go to the real backend
- Each spec cleans up its own test data (delete created orders/products/stock counts after assertions, or use a dedicated test user/business)
tasks.testStrategy: Run with `npx playwright test --project=chromium` against local stack. CI: add to existing playwright GitHub Actions workflow.

tasks.title: sec: gate user registration behind admin auth — prevent open ADMIN self-registration
tasks.description: POST /api/v1/auth/register is fully public and hard-codes role=UserRole.ADMIN for every registrant. Any anonymous caller can register an account with full admin privileges.
tasks.details: In backend/src/auth/service.py line 62, create_user hard-codes role=UserRole.ADMIN. In backend/src/auth/router.py lines 43-52, the register endpoint has no Depends(get_current_active_user) guard. Fix: (a) Add Depends(require_admin) to the /register endpoint so only an existing admin can create new users, OR (b) change the default role in create_user to UserRole.VIEWER and add a separate admin-only PATCH /users/{id}/role endpoint. Option (a) is simplest for this single-tenant app. Also write a pytest test confirming unauthenticated registration is rejected (HTTP 401) and authenticated admin registration succeeds.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend pytest: test_unauthenticated_register_returns_401, test_admin_can_create_user, test_new_user_has_viewer_role_not_admin

tasks.title: sec: add get_current_active_user dependency to all unauthenticated data endpoints (~50 routes)
tasks.description: Over 50 financial data endpoints across sales, orders, cashflow, inventory, pricing, fx, and ai_engine routers serve full business data to anonymous HTTP clients with no authentication dependency.
tasks.details: Convert every router to use a router-level dependency so auth is the default. In each of: backend/src/sales/router.py, orders/router.py, cashflow/router.py, inventory/router.py, pricing/router.py, fx/router.py, ai_engine/router.py — change the APIRouter constructor to: router = APIRouter(dependencies=[Depends(get_current_active_user)]). Then audit every endpoint that should remain public (health check only) and add an explicit exclude. Specific unauthenticated endpoints to fix include: GET /sales, /sales/export.csv, /sales/{id}, /orders, /orders/export.csv, /cashflow/loans, /cashflow/global-exposure, /inventory, /pricing/portfolio-margin, /fx/rates/current, /fx/export.csv, /ai/recommendations, and ~40 more listed in the security review. Write a pytest test for each router confirming that unauthenticated GET returns 401.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend pytest: one test per router confirming unauthenticated GET / returns 401; one test confirming authenticated request returns 200

tasks.title: sec: remove SECRET_KEY default fallback and add startup validation
tasks.description: SECRET_KEY defaults to the literal string "dev-secret-change-in-production" in both config.py and docker-compose.yml. A deployment without the env var set uses this publicly-visible string as the HS256 JWT signing key, allowing anyone to forge valid tokens.
tasks.details: 1. In backend/src/core/config.py line 81: change SECRET_KEY: str = "dev-secret-change-in-production" to SECRET_KEY: str with no default, so Pydantic raises a ValidationError at startup if unset. 2. Add a model_validator(mode="after") that raises if SECRET_KEY == "dev-secret-change-in-production" or len(SECRET_KEY) < 32. 3. In docker-compose.yml line 25: change SECRET_KEY: ${SECRET_KEY:-dev-secret-change-in-production} to SECRET_KEY: ${SECRET_KEY} (no fallback). 4. Ensure backend/.env has a proper secret. Write a test confirming startup fails with the dev default.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend pytest: test_settings_rejects_dev_default_secret_key, test_settings_rejects_short_secret_key

tasks.title: sec: hash password reset tokens with SHA-256 before DB storage
tasks.description: Password reset tokens (uuid4().hex) are stored plaintext in the password_reset_tokens table. If the DB is read (SQL injection, backup leak, insider), all live tokens are immediately usable to take over accounts. Refresh tokens in the same file already use _hash_token() — apply the same pattern here.
tasks.details: In backend/src/auth/service.py around line 129: change token_str = _uuid.uuid4().hex to use secrets.token_urlsafe(32) for better entropy. Store _hash_token(token_str) in the DB (not token_str). In the reset_password service (line 155), hash the submitted token before the DB lookup: query WHERE token = _hash_token(submitted_token). The _hash_token helper using hashlib.sha256 already exists in the same file for refresh tokens — reuse it. Write pytest tests: test_reset_token_stored_as_hash (confirm raw token not in DB), test_reset_password_with_valid_token_succeeds, test_reset_password_with_wrong_token_fails.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend pytest: test_reset_token_stored_as_hash, test_reset_password_with_valid_token_succeeds, test_reset_password_with_invalid_token_fails

tasks.title: sec: add ownership checks to all individual-resource endpoints (IDOR fix)
tasks.description: No endpoint that accepts a resource {id} in the path verifies the resource belongs to the authenticated user. User A can read, modify, or delete User B's sales, orders, and payments by guessing a UUID.
tasks.details: For every service function that fetches a single resource by ID, add an ownership check. Affected endpoints: GET/PUT/DELETE /sales/{sale_id} (sales/service.py), GET /sales/{sale_id}/audit, GET/PUT/DELETE /orders/{order_id} (orders/service.py), DELETE /orders/{order_id}/payments/{payment_id} (void_payment — orders/service.py:659), GET /orders/{order_id}/payments, GET /orders/{order_id}/status-history, GET /inventory/{product_id}. Pattern: after fetching the resource, assert resource.recorded_by == current_user.id (or resource.created_by). Raise HTTP 403 if mismatch. Pass current_user into the relevant service calls. This requires updating router signatures to include current_user: User = Depends(get_current_active_user) where missing. Write pytest tests: test_user_cannot_read_other_users_sale, test_user_cannot_delete_other_users_order.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend pytest: test_user_cannot_read_other_users_sale (403), test_user_cannot_delete_other_users_order (403), test_user_can_read_own_sale (200)

tasks.title: sec: add SELECT FOR UPDATE row lock to adjust_stock to prevent oversell race condition
tasks.description: adjust_stock in inventory/service.py follows read-modify-write with no pessimistic lock. Two concurrent sale requests both read quantity_on_hand=1, both pass the negativity check, and both commit — selling the same unit twice. fifo_deduct already uses .with_for_update() but adjust_stock does not.
tasks.details: In backend/src/inventory/service.py around line 132, find the SELECT for InventoryLevel inside adjust_stock. Add .with_for_update() to the SQLAlchemy query: result = await db.execute(select(InventoryLevel).where(InventoryLevel.product_id == product_id).with_for_update()). This is a one-line change. Write a pytest test that uses asyncio.gather to fire two concurrent sales of the last unit and asserts only one succeeds (the second raises InvalidStockAdjustmentError) and final stock is 0 not -1.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend pytest: test_concurrent_sales_cannot_oversell (two concurrent requests, one succeeds one fails, stock ends at 0)

tasks.title: sec: move JWT tokens from localStorage to memory/HttpOnly cookie
tasks.description: Both JWT access token and 7-day refresh token are stored in localStorage, accessible to any JavaScript on the page. Any XSS payload can exfiltrate both tokens with localStorage.getItem(). With no CSP and no HttpOnly cookies the blast radius of any XSS is complete session compromise for up to 7 days.
tasks.details: Frontend: In frontend/src/app/core/services/auth.service.ts, change access token storage from localStorage to an in-memory Angular Signal (private, never serialized). Remove localStorage.setItem('modishlog_token', ...) and localStorage.getItem('modishlog_token') calls. For the refresh token: work with the backend to set it as an HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict cookie from the /auth/login and /auth/refresh responses (Set-Cookie header). Backend: In auth/router.py login endpoint, add response.set_cookie(key="refresh_token", value=token, httponly=True, secure=True, samesite="strict", max_age=7*24*3600). Update /auth/refresh to read the refresh token from the cookie instead of the request body. Update /auth/logout to clear the cookie. Write E2E test: after login, confirm localStorage does not contain modishlog_token; confirm authenticated requests succeed; confirm after tab close (sessionStorage cleared) re-login is required.
tasks.testStrategy: Playwright E2E: after login localStorage.getItem('modishlog_token') === null; authenticated API call succeeds; logout clears session

tasks.title: sec: restrict auth interceptor to same-origin requests only
tasks.description: The Angular HTTP interceptor unconditionally attaches Authorization: Bearer token to every outbound HttpRequest with no same-origin check. Any future HttpClient call to an external URL will silently leak the JWT to that server's access logs.
tasks.details: In frontend/src/app/core/interceptors/auth.interceptor.ts lines 12-14, add an origin check before cloning the request with the auth header: const isOwnApi = req.url.startsWith(environment.apiBaseUrl) || req.url.startsWith('/api/'); const authedReq = token && isOwnApi ? req.clone({ setHeaders: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } }) : req; This ensures tokens are only sent to the application's own backend. Write a Jest/Spectator unit test confirming: (1) requests to apiBaseUrl include Authorization header; (2) requests to 'https://external.example.com' do not include Authorization header.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test: interceptor attaches token to own-API requests; interceptor does NOT attach token to external-domain requests

tasks.title: sec: add Content-Security-Policy header to nginx config
tasks.description: nginx.conf adds X-Frame-Options and X-Content-Type-Options but has no Content-Security-Policy. Without a CSP, any XSS vulnerability has unlimited scope: injected scripts can read all localStorage values (tokens, API keys), exfiltrate data, and make authenticated requests on the victim's behalf.
tasks.details: In frontend/nginx.conf, add the following header inside the server or location block: add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' https://fonts.googleapis.com; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com; img-src 'self' data: blob:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self';" always; Also add: add_header Permissions-Policy "geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=()" always; Test that Angular app loads correctly with the CSP in place (no console CSP violations). Note: Angular runtime does not need unsafe-inline for scripts in production builds (uses compiled templates). If PrimeNG inline styles trigger violations, switch style-src to include a nonce or hash. Also switch Google Fonts to self-hosted @fontsource/inter to remove the fonts.googleapis.com exception (see task M11).
tasks.testStrategy: Playwright E2E: load app, check browser console has zero CSP violation errors; check response headers include Content-Security-Policy

tasks.title: sec: pin JWT signing algorithm to HS256 with startup validator (prevent algorithm confusion)
tasks.description: ALGORITHM is a plain string config field settable via environment variable with no validation. Setting ALGORITHM=none causes python-jose to accept unsigned tokens. Setting ALGORITHM=RS256 against an HS256-signed key produces confusion attacks.
tasks.details: In backend/src/core/config.py, add a Pydantic field_validator for ALGORITHM: @field_validator("ALGORITHM") @classmethod def validate_algorithm(cls, v: str) -> str: allowed = {"HS256", "HS384", "HS512"}; if v not in allowed: raise ValueError(f"ALGORITHM must be one of {allowed}"); return v. Also hard-code the algorithm list in security.py decode_access_token rather than reading from settings: use algorithms=["HS256"] directly, or algorithms=[settings.ALGORITHM] only after the validator guarantees it is in the safe set. Write pytest: test_invalid_algorithm_rejected_at_startup, test_none_algorithm_token_rejected.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend pytest: test settings raise ValueError for ALGORITHM=none; test a token signed with alg=none is rejected by decode_access_token

tasks.title: sec: sanitize CSV exports and imports against formula injection
tasks.description: All CSV export endpoints write user-controlled strings (supplier_name, product_name, category, order_number) directly into csv.writer rows without escaping formula-trigger prefixes (=, +, -, @). Excel/LibreOffice evaluate these as formulas on open. CSV imports also store raw formula strings in the DB, creating a stored-payload attack path.
tasks.details: 1. Create a shared utility in backend/src/core/csv_utils.py: def csv_safe(value: str) -> str: return ("'" + value) if value and value[0] in ('=', '+', '-', '@', '\t', '\r') else value. 2. Apply csv_safe() to every user-supplied string field in: backend/src/orders/router.py lines 262-275 (supplier_name, order_number), backend/src/sales/router.py lines 270-308 (channel, notes), backend/src/fx/router.py lines 127-135 (pair), backend/src/reports/router.py lines 65-78 (product_name, sku, category). 3. Also apply csv_safe() at import ingest time in: sales/service.py process_bulk_upload, orders/service.py import_orders_from_file, products/router.py bulk import — strip formula prefixes from free-text fields before storing in DB. Write pytest: test_csv_export_sanitizes_formula_in_supplier_name, test_csv_import_strips_formula_from_product_name.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend pytest: test_csv_export_sanitizes_formula_prefix (supplier_name starting with = is prefixed with apostrophe in output); test_csv_import_strips_formula_from_notes

tasks.title: sec: remove is_active from ProductUpdate schema (mass assignment fix)
tasks.description: ProductUpdate in products/schemas.py includes is_active: bool | None = None. update_product applies all non-None fields via setattr. Any authenticated user can PATCH {"is_active": false} to silently deactivate any product, or re-activate a deliberately deactivated one.
tasks.details: In backend/src/products/schemas.py line 68, remove the is_active field from ProductUpdate. The is_active state should only be changed via the dedicated DELETE /products/{id} endpoint (which calls deactivate_product) and a new admin-only PATCH /products/{id}/activate endpoint. If needed, add activate_product(product_id, db) to products/service.py and a route POST /products/{id}/activate with Depends(require_admin). Write pytest: test_update_product_cannot_set_is_active (400 or field ignored), test_deactivate_product_sets_is_active_false.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend pytest: test_patch_product_with_is_active_field_is_rejected_or_ignored; test_only_delete_endpoint_deactivates_product

tasks.title: sec: remove DELIVERED from EDITABLE_STATUSES to prevent retroactive order mutation
tasks.description: EDITABLE_STATUSES in orders/service.py includes OrderStatus.DELIVERED. Editing a delivered order's line items retroactively changes unit_cost on committed FIFO batches and corrupts balance_remaining, making paid orders appear unpaid.
tasks.details: In backend/src/orders/service.py lines 67-74, remove OrderStatus.DELIVERED from EDITABLE_STATUSES. If post-delivery annotations are needed, create a narrow PATCH /orders/{id}/notes endpoint that only allows updating a notes/memo field and nothing that affects financials. Update update_order service to verify the status transition is valid before applying any changes. Write pytest: test_cannot_edit_delivered_order_line_items (expect 422 or 403), test_can_edit_confirmed_order.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend pytest: test_cannot_edit_delivered_order (returns 422); test_can_still_edit_pending_order (returns 200)

tasks.title: sec: enforce minimum price floor on ProductCreate/ProductUpdate to prevent division-by-zero
tasks.description: ProductCreate uses ge=0 for unit_cost and selling_price, making 0 a valid value. The pricing engine divides by selling_price in elasticity and sensitivity calculations, causing an unhandled ZeroDivisionError when selling_price is 0.
tasks.details: In backend/src/products/schemas.py lines 57-58, change: unit_cost: Decimal = Field(..., ge=0) to unit_cost: Decimal = Field(..., gt=Decimal("0")) and selling_price: Decimal = Field(..., ge=0) to selling_price: Decimal = Field(..., gt=Decimal("0")). Apply the same change to ProductUpdate for these fields. Also add a guard in pricing/service.py calculate_price_elasticity_impact and calculate_demand_forecast: if current_price == 0: raise PricingValidationError("selling_price must be greater than zero"). Write pytest: test_create_product_with_zero_price_rejected (422), test_pricing_engine_raises_on_zero_price.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend pytest: test_product_create_rejects_zero_selling_price (422); test_product_create_rejects_zero_unit_cost (422)

tasks.title: sec: fix auth guard to validate JWT expiry, not just token presence
tasks.description: authGuard returns true for any non-empty string in localStorage. Running localStorage.setItem('modishlog_token', 'x') in DevTools bypasses all route guards, loading the full app shell and any cached Signal state before any API call is made.
tasks.details: In frontend/src/app/core/guards/auth.guard.ts, update the guard to decode the JWT payload and check expiry: const token = localStorage.getItem('modishlog_token'); if (!token) return router.createUrlTree(['/login']); try { const payload = JSON.parse(atob(token.split('.')[1])); if (payload.exp * 1000 < Date.now()) { authService.logout(); return router.createUrlTree(['/login']); } return true; } catch { authService.logout(); return router.createUrlTree(['/login']); }. Note: once task H3 (tokens moved out of localStorage) is implemented, update this guard accordingly. Write Playwright E2E: set localStorage with a fake/expired token, navigate to /dashboard, confirm redirect to /login.
tasks.testStrategy: Playwright E2E: set localStorage.modishlog_token = 'fake', navigate to /dashboard, assert redirected to /login; set expired JWT, navigate to /dashboard, assert redirected to /login

tasks.title: sec: add global unhandled-exception handler to prevent stack trace leakage
tasks.description: No catch-all exception handler is registered in main.py. An unhandled exception from openpyxl, Prophet, or scipy returns a full Starlette traceback in the HTTP 500 response body — including local variable values, internal file paths, and library versions.
tasks.details: In backend/src/main.py, register a catch-all handler after the app is created: from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse; from fastapi import Request; @app.exception_handler(Exception) async def unhandled_exception_handler(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse: logger.error("unhandled_exception", path=str(request.url), exc_info=True); return JSONResponse(status_code=500, content={"detail": "Internal server error"}). Test that this does NOT suppress HTTPException (FastAPI's own exception handler must still run for 4xx errors). Write pytest: test_unhandled_exception_returns_500_without_traceback (mock a route to raise RuntimeError, confirm response body is {"detail": "Internal server error"} not a stacktrace).
tasks.testStrategy: Backend pytest: mock route raises RuntimeError, confirm 500 response body is generic JSON with no traceback; confirm HTTPException 404 still returns correct detail

tasks.title: sec: tighten CORS config — restrict allow_headers and add wildcard-origin guard
tasks.description: CORS middleware uses allow_credentials=True with allow_headers=["*"]. This combination is undefined per the CORS spec and inconsistently handled by browsers. If CORS_ORIGINS is ever misconfigured to include "*", credentials become exploitable from any origin.
tasks.details: In backend/src/main.py lines 29-35, change allow_headers=["*"] to allow_headers=["Authorization", "Content-Type", "X-Requested-With"]. Add a startup check in the lifespan or as a Settings validator: if "*" in settings.CORS_ORIGINS and app_settings.allow_credentials: raise RuntimeError("Cannot use allow_credentials=True with wildcard CORS origins"). Also consider removing allow_credentials=True entirely since the app uses Bearer tokens in the Authorization header (not cookies) — credentials mode is not needed for Bearer token auth. Write pytest: test_cors_does_not_allow_wildcard_with_credentials.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend pytest: test that Settings raises if CORS_ORIGINS contains "*"; test CORS preflight response does not include Access-Control-Allow-Headers: * when credentials are enabled

tasks.title: Write golden-path E2E spec: Login → Product → PO → Deliver → Sale → P&L
tasks.description: Create frontend/e2e/golden-path.spec.ts — a single end-to-end spec that walks the complete MVP business cycle in sequence, proving every critical handoff works on a clean database.
tasks.details:
Steps the spec must cover in order:
1. Login with E2E credentials, assert redirect to /dashboard
2. Create a new product (name, unit cost, sell price, category) — assert it appears in the products list
3. Create a purchase order with that product as a line item (qty 10, unit cost) — assert order appears in Orders table with status ORDERED
4. Transition the order through each status step via the UI status-advance button: ORDERED → PENDING → IN_PRODUCTION → SHIPPING → CLEARED → DELIVERED — assert the status badge updates at each step
5. After DELIVERED, assert the product's stock level in /inventory increased by 10
6. Record a sale for that product (qty 3) — assert success toast, sale appears in sales list, stock drops to 7
7. Navigate to /reports/profit-loss, fill start/end date to bracket the session, click Generate Report — assert revenue and profit figures are non-zero ₦ amounts

Use helpers from frontend/e2e/helpers/auth.ts for login. Create/clean up all data via API calls in beforeAll/afterAll so the spec is fully self-contained and does not pollute shared E2E data.

Notes:
- This is the single most important missing test. A beta user's first session follows exactly this path.
- Run with: cd frontend && npx playwright test e2e/golden-path.spec.ts --headed to observe during development
tasks.testStrategy: The spec IS the test. Verify it passes on a clean DB (after docker compose down -v && docker compose up). Also run it twice back-to-back to confirm afterAll cleanup works and no stale data bleeds between runs.

tasks.title: Dashboard Overview Page — KPI Summary Cards
tasks.description: Implement the main dashboard overview page with a personalized welcome header, location filter, date filter, and 8 KPI summary cards displaying financial totals for the selected location and date range.
tasks.details:
## Layout & Structure

### Header Section
- Blue-to-dark-navy gradient banner spanning full width
- Personalized greeting: **"Welcome {firstName},"** (bold, white, large text) rendered from the authenticated user's profile
- Two controls on the same row below the greeting:
  - **Left**: "Select location" dropdown — filters all KPI cards by the chosen business location (shows all locations when blank)
  - **Right**: "Filter by date" button (calendar icon + caret) — opens a date-range picker; filters all KPI cards by the chosen period

---

## KPI Cards — Row 1

All cards share a white card container with a rounded coloured circle icon on the left, a label above the value, and the financial total in **large bold text** formatted as `₦ X,XXX.XX`.

### 1. Total Sales
- **Icon**: Shopping cart, teal/cyan background
- **Label**: TOTAL SALES
- **Value**: Sum of all completed sale amounts for the selected location + date range

### 2. NET
- **Icon**: Document/ledger, green background
- **Label**: NET (with an ℹ info icon that shows a tooltip explaining the calculation: Total Sales − Cost of Goods Sold − Expenses)
- **Value**: Net profit for the selected filters

### 3. Invoice Due
- **Icon**: Invoice/alert document, orange background
- **Label**: INVOICE DUE
- **Value**: Total outstanding (unpaid) invoice balance for the selected filters

### 4. Total Sell Return
- **Icon**: Bidirectional arrows (swap), pink/red background
- **Label**: TOTAL SELL RETURN
- **Value**: Combined sell-return total
- **Sub-lines** (smaller text below the main value):
  - `Total Sell Return: ₦ X.XX` — gross return amount
  - `Total Sell Return Paid: ₦ X.XX` — portion already refunded to customers

---

## KPI Cards — Row 2

### 5. Total Purchase
- **Icon**: Cash/banknotes, teal/cyan background
- **Label**: TOTAL PURCHASE
- **Value**: Sum of all purchase order amounts for the selected filters

### 6. Purchase Due
- **Icon**: Exclamation mark circle, orange background
- **Label**: PURCHASE DUE
- **Value**: Total outstanding (unpaid) purchase balance owed to suppliers

### 7. Total Purchase Return
- **Icon**: Circular refresh/undo arrow, pink/red background
- **Label**: TOTAL PURCHASE RETURN
- **Value**: Combined purchase-return total
- **Sub-lines** (smaller text below the main value):
  - `Total Purchase Return: ₦ X.XX` — gross return amount
  - `Total Purchase Return Paid: ₦ X.XX` — portion already credited/received back

### 8. Expense
- **Icon**: Minus/subtract circle, pink/red background
- **Label**: EXPENSE
- **Value**: Total logged business expenses for the selected filters

---

## Backend API

Create `GET /api/dashboard/summary` endpoint:
- **Query params**: `location_id` (optional UUID), `date_from` (ISO date), `date_to` (ISO date)
- **Response schema**:
```json
{
  "total_sales": "Decimal",
  "net": "Decimal",
  "invoice_due": "Decimal",
  "total_sell_return": "Decimal",
  "total_sell_return_paid": "Decimal",
  "total_purchase": "Decimal",
  "purchase_due": "Decimal",
  "total_purchase_return": "Decimal",
  "total_purchase_return_paid": "Decimal",
  "expense": "Decimal"
}
```
- All monetary values must use Python `Decimal`; never `float`
- Use async SQLAlchemy queries with `selectinload()` where relationships are involved
- Scope all queries to the authenticated user's business (`current_user.business_id`)

## Frontend

- Angular standalone component `DashboardOverviewComponent` at `frontend/src/app/features/dashboard/pages/`
- Use Angular Signals for reactive state (`locationSignal`, `dateRangeSignal`)
- Call `DashboardService.getSummary(locationId, dateFrom, dateTo)` which hits the API above
- Currency pipe: display all values as Nigerian Naira `₦` with 2 decimal places
- KPI card subcomponent `KpiCardComponent` (reusable): accepts `label`, `value`, `iconClass`, `iconColor`, `subLines?: {label, value}[]`
- Responsive grid: 4 columns on desktop, 2 on tablet, 1 on mobile (TailwindCSS)
- Loading skeleton state while API call is in flight
- Error state with retry button if API call fails

## Tech notes
- Static `/dashboard` route before any parameterized routes (FastAPI rule)
- PrimeNG `p-dropdown` for location selector, `p-calendar` with range mode for date filter
- Icon colours: teal = `#17A2B8`, green = `#28A745`, orange = `#FFC107`, pink/red = `#E74C3C`
tasks.testStrategy:
**Backend (pytest — TDD: write tests first)**
1. Happy path: `GET /api/dashboard/summary` returns correct aggregated totals for a seeded dataset
2. Location filter: totals change when `location_id` is supplied vs omitted
3. Date range filter: totals only include transactions within the specified window
4. Empty state: all values return `0.00` when no transactions exist
5. Auth guard: unauthenticated request returns 401
6. Cross-business isolation: user cannot see another business's data

**Frontend (Playwright E2E — TDD: write tests first)**
1. Dashboard loads and displays all 8 KPI card labels
2. All values default to `₦ 0.00` on a fresh account with no data
3. Selecting a location from the dropdown re-fetches and updates card values
4. Applying a date filter updates card values accordingly
5. Sell Return card shows both sub-lines (`Total Sell Return` + `Total Sell Return Paid`)
6. Purchase Return card shows both sub-lines
7. Loading skeleton is visible during API call; disappears on completion
8. Error state renders correctly when API returns 500

tasks.title: Editable sale payment method/status and transaction-level notes
tasks.description: Sale payment method and payment status should be editable after creation. Sale notes should belong to the transaction group (shared across all items in a transaction), not to individual sale items.
tasks.details:
## Backend

### 1. New schema — SaleTransactionUpdate (schemas.py)
- `payment_method: Optional[str]`
- `payment_status: Optional[str]`
- `status: Optional[SaleStatus]` — allow PENDING↔COMPLETED only; reject VOIDED (use void endpoint for that)
- `notes: Optional[str]`

### 2. New service function — update_transaction() (service.py)
- Accept `transaction_id: str`, `payload: SaleTransactionUpdate`, `current_user`
- Fetch all Sale records WHERE transaction_id = ? AND business_id = current_user.business_id
- 404 if no records found; 403 if business mismatch
- Reject payload.status == VOIDED with 422
- Update each Sale record with non-None payload fields
- Create one audit entry per updated Sale record
- Return updated records

### 3. New router endpoint (router.py)
- `PUT /sales/transactions/{transaction_id}` — must be registered BEFORE `PUT /sales/{sale_id}` (static segment before parameterized)
- Body: SaleTransactionUpdate
- Auth: require current_user

### 4. Existing SaleUpdate schema — add payment_method + payment_status
- Also add these two fields to SaleUpdate so individual-item edits can update them too

## Frontend

### 1. sales.service.ts
- Add `SaleTransactionUpdatePayload` interface: `payment_method?`, `payment_status?`, `status?`, `notes?`
- Add `updateTransaction(transactionId: string, payload)` method calling `PUT /sales/transactions/{transactionId}`

### 2. sales-page.component.ts
- Add "Edit transaction" button at the TRANSACTION header level (next to Void)
- New transaction-level edit dialog: fields for payment_method (dropdown), payment_status (dropdown), notes (textarea)
- Remove `notes` from the per-item SaleUpdatePayload and edit dialog — notes now live at transaction level only
- On save, call `updateTransaction(transaction.transaction_id, payload)` — this updates all items in the group

## Route ordering check
Verify `PUT /sales/transactions/{transaction_id}` is declared BEFORE `PUT /sales/{sale_id}` in router.py to avoid FastAPI matching "transactions" as a sale_id.
tasks.testStrategy:
**Backend (pytest — TDD: write tests FIRST)**
1. Happy path: PUT /sales/transactions/{id} updates payment_method, payment_status, notes on all items in group
2. Status transition: PENDING → COMPLETED succeeds; VOIDED → anything via this endpoint returns 422
3. Auth guard: unauthenticated returns 401
4. Cross-business isolation: cannot update another business's transaction (404)
5. Not found: unknown transaction_id returns 404

**Frontend (Playwright E2E — TDD: write tests FIRST)**
1. Edit transaction button is visible on the transaction header
2. Opening edit dialog shows payment_method, payment_status, notes fields
3. Saving updated payment_method reflects in the transaction view
4. Notes field appears at transaction level, not per-item

tasks.title: Inline editing for transaction detail line items
tasks.description: Replace the per-item Edit dialog on the Transaction Detail page with inline cell editing. Quantity, unit price, and discount cells should be editable directly in the table row. The edit (pencil) button should be removed from the Actions column; only void (trash) and audit (clock) remain.
tasks.details:
Frontend only — transaction-detail-page.component.ts:

1. Remove the Edit Sale Item p-dialog and all state that drives it (editDialogVisible, editingItem, editForm, openEditDialog, submitEdit).

2. Add per-row edit state:
   - Signal: `editingRowId = signal<string | null>(null)` — tracks which row (by sale id) is being edited
   - Signal: `rowDraft = signal<{ quantity: number; unit_price: number; discount_amount: number | null }>({ ... })` — holds the in-progress values

3. In the table, for each non-voided row:
   - Qty cell: when editingRowId() === item.id show `<input type="number" min="1">` bound to rowDraft().quantity, else show plain text
   - Unit Price cell: when editing show `<input type="number" min="0" step="0.01">` bound to rowDraft().unit_price, else show currency pipe
   - Discount cell: when editing show `<input type="number" min="0" step="0.01">` bound to rowDraft().discount_amount (nullable), else existing display
   - Line Total cell: always computed from rowDraft when editing: quantity * unit_price - discount_amount
   - Actions cell: remove edit button. Add a save (check) and cancel (x) button when editingRowId() === item.id. Show only void+audit when not editing.
   - Clicking anywhere on a non-voided row (or a dedicated "click to edit" affordance on the product name cell) activates inline edit for that row.

4. openInlineEdit(item): set editingRowId(item.id), set rowDraft to current values.
5. cancelInlineEdit(): set editingRowId(null).
6. submitInlineEdit(): call salesService.update(editingRowId(), { quantity, unit_price, discount_amount }), on success reload transaction, on error show toast.
7. Computed lineTotalForRow(): quantity * unit_price - (discount_amount ?? 0).

Actions column should only ever contain: [save+cancel when editing] OR [void + audit when not editing]. No edit pencil button at any time.

Tests: update/add Playwright E2E in frontend/e2e/transaction-detail.spec.ts — clicking a qty cell activates edit, changing value and saving reflects in the table.
tasks.testStrategy: Playwright E2E: activate inline edit on a row, change quantity, save, verify updated quantity shown in table without page reload. Also verify no edit (pencil) button is present in action cells.

tasks.title: Add fiscal year start to business settings — backend
tasks.description: Store the user's fiscal year start date (month + day) in the database so the app can use it as the default report period start. Add two nullable integer columns to the business_settings table: fiscal_year_start_month (1–12) and fiscal_year_start_day (1–31), both defaulting to NULL (meaning "not configured"). Expose via the existing settings API.
tasks.details:
1. Write tests FIRST (TDD):
   - Happy path: GET /settings returns fiscal_year_start_month and fiscal_year_start_day fields
   - Happy path: PUT /settings with {fiscal_year_start_month: 4, fiscal_year_start_day: 1} saves correctly
   - Error case: PUT with month=13 or day=32 returns 422
   - Error case: PUT with month set but day missing returns 422
2. Alembic migration: add fiscal_year_start_month (Integer, nullable) and fiscal_year_start_day (Integer, nullable) to business_settings table (or user_preferences if that is the correct settings table)
3. Update the settings SQLAlchemy model and Pydantic schema (SettingsRead + SettingsUpdate) to include both fields
4. Update the settings service: validate that if one field is provided, both must be provided; validate month in 1–12, day in 1–31
5. No new router needed — extend the existing GET /settings and PUT /settings endpoints
6. Run pytest and confirm all pass
tasks.testStrategy: TDD: write failing tests first. Backend unit tests: SettingsService with AsyncMock DB. Integration tests: TestClient hitting the settings endpoints. Validate 422 on invalid month/day combinations. Confirm migration is reversible (downgrade removes columns).

tasks.title: Report endpoints — default to YTD date range when no dates supplied
tasks.description: Make date_from and date_to optional query parameters on all report endpoints (P&L, revenue summary, and any other report routes). When omitted, default to: date_to = today, date_from = most recent occurrence of the configured fiscal year start (or today minus 365 days if fiscal year start is not set). This lets the frontend load reports immediately on page open without requiring the user to pick dates.
tasks.details:
1. Write tests FIRST (TDD):
   - Happy path: GET /reports/profit-loss with no params returns 200 with data covering the last 365 days
   - Happy path: GET /reports/profit-loss with no params, fiscal_year_start configured as April 1, returns data from April 1 of the current or previous fiscal year to today
   - Happy path: GET /reports/profit-loss?date_from=2025-01-01&date_to=2025-12-31 still works as before
   - Error case: date_from after date_to still returns 422
2. In the report router(s), change date_from and date_to from required to Optional[date] = None
3. In the report service(s), add a helper resolve_default_date_range(settings) that:
   - Fetches the current business settings (fiscal_year_start_month, fiscal_year_start_day)
   - If not set: returns (today - 365 days, today)
   - If set: computes the most recent fiscal year start date that is ≤ today and returns (fys_date, today)
4. Apply this helper in every report endpoint that currently requires dates
5. Run pytest and confirm all pass
tasks.testStrategy: TDD: failing tests first. Unit test resolve_default_date_range() with various fiscal year configurations. Integration tests via TestClient: no-params call returns data, explicit params still respected. Test fiscal year rollover logic (today is before fiscal year start month/day → use prior year).

tasks.title: Reports page — auto-load with default YTD date range on open
tasks.description: On the reports page, pre-populate the date range to today-minus-365-days → today (or fiscal year start → today if configured) and fetch the report automatically on init. The user should see data immediately without having to select dates or click a button. They can still change the date range and re-fetch as desired.

5. Run the E2E test and confirm it passes

tasks.title: Fix sales N+1 query — rewrite list_transactions to single SQL query
tasks.description: The sales list_transactions service function runs 1 + N SQL queries per page (one to fetch transaction IDs, then one per transaction in a Python loop). For a page of 25 transactions this is 26 queries. Rewrite to a single query using GROUP BY or a subquery so the entire page loads in one DB round trip.
tasks.details: In backend/src/sales/service.py, the list_transactions function fetches distinct transaction_ids then loops over them doing individual SELECT per txn. Replace with a single query: SELECT * FROM sales WHERE transaction_id IN (SELECT transaction_id FROM ... GROUP BY transaction_id ORDER BY min(created_at) DESC LIMIT N OFFSET M) ORDER BY transaction_id, created_at. Use selectinload where appropriate. Update any dependent tests in tests/test_sales.py.
tasks.testStrategy: Run existing pytest tests. Add a test that asserts list_transactions issues at most 2 DB queries (paginated ID fetch + bulk fetch) for a page of 25 items using SQLAlchemy query count tracking.

tasks.title: Parallelize page init API calls with forkJoin on all data pages
tasks.description: Sales, Products, Orders, and Inventory pages fire their ngOnInit API calls sequentially. Each call waits for the previous to complete, stacking latencies. Replace sequential subscriptions with forkJoin so all independent calls fire simultaneously. Inventory has nested subscriptions (inventory waits for products) — restructure to parallel forkJoin then join on the client side.
tasks.details: Sales: wrap productsService.getAll(), loadInventory, loadTransactions, loadCustomers, loadLocations in forkJoin. Products: wrap loadProducts, loadCategories, loadStock, fxService.getLatest in forkJoin. Orders: wrap loadOrders + productsService.getAll in forkJoin. Inventory: use forkJoin([productsService.getAll(), inventoryService.getCurrent(), inventoryService.getMovements()]) then build nameMap client-side. Import forkJoin from rxjs in each component.
tasks.testStrategy: Manual verification: open browser network tab and confirm all API calls fire simultaneously (overlapping waterfall) rather than sequentially (staircase pattern). Page load time should drop noticeably.

tasks.title: Add shareReplay caching to Angular services for reference data
tasks.description: ProductsService.getAll(), LocationsService.getAll(), and CustomerService.getAll() are called fresh on every page navigation even though this data rarely changes. Add shareReplay(1) caching so the HTTP call fires once and subsequent subscribers get the cached result instantly. Invalidate on mutation (create/update/delete) by resetting the cached observable.
tasks.details: In each service, store a private cache$: Observable | null = null. In getAll(), return (this.cache$ ??= this.api.get(...).pipe(shareReplay(1))). In create/update/delete methods, set this.cache$ = null to bust the cache. Apply to: products.service.ts (getAll, getCategories), locations.service.ts (getAll), customers.service.ts (getAll). Sales transactions should NOT be cached as they change frequently.
tasks.testStrategy: Navigate to Sales page, then Products, then back to Sales — confirm browser network tab shows no repeat HTTP calls for products/locations/customers on the second visit.
