tasks.title: POS Live Data Migration — seed local dev DB from pos.virtualrx.com.ng
tasks.description: Replace all local mock/stale data with real production data fetched from the live POS system (UltimatePOS at https://pos.virtualrx.com.ng). Covers: DB wipe (keep schema), POS auth, data pull, migration into ModishLog local dev DB, and E2E test isolation so test runs never touch the migrated dataset.
tasks.details:
## Context
- POS URL: https://pos.virtualrx.com.ng (UltimatePOS / Laravel)
- Auth: cookie-based with CSRF token; creds in /workspace/modish-standard/.env (INVENTORY_APP_USERNAME=soji, INVENTORY_APP_PASSWORD=M0di$h$tandard331)
- POSClient reference implementation: /Users/sojisoyoye/workspace/modish-standard/scripts/pos-client.ts
- ModishLog DB: Docker Compose PostgreSQL (local dev), SQLAlchemy 2.0 async ORM
- Staging Neon DB URL is in /workspace/modishlog/.env — DO NOT wipe this; only wipe local Docker DB

## Subtasks

### 1. Verify POS connectivity
- Confirm login to https://pos.virtualrx.com.ng with cookie+CSRF flow
- Log products count, purchases count, sales count to stdout

### 2. Local DB wipe (keep schema)
- Truncate all data tables in CORRECT dependency order (FK-aware)
- Do NOT drop tables or run migrations; schema must remain intact
- Script: backend/scripts/pos_migrate.py (or similar)
- Use: docker compose exec backend python scripts/pos_migrate.py --step=wipe

### 3. POS → ModishLog data migration script
Write backend/scripts/pos_migrate.py covering these entities in order:
  a. Users — create a single admin user (soji.soyoye@gmail.com) so FK references work
  b. ProductCategories — map POS category strings to ModishLog ProductCategory rows
  c. Products — map POS products: name, sku, slug, unit_cost (max_price), selling_price, is_active
  d. InventoryLevels — one row per product, quantity_on_hand from POS current_stock
  e. Suppliers — pull /contacts?type=supplier from POS, map to Supplier model
  f. SupplierProducts — link suppliers to the products they supply (via purchase history)
  g. Sales — pull /sells from POS; map each line to a Sale row (best-effort, use RETAIL channel)
  h. Purchases/Expenses — pull /purchases from POS; store as cashflow entries or expense records

Rules:
  - Use Python Decimal for all financial values (never float)
  - Use SQLAlchemy ORM — no raw SQL
  - Use structlog for logging (never print())
  - Use async/await for all DB writes
  - Idempotent: running twice should upsert, not duplicate

### 4. E2E test isolation
- Add TEST_DATABASE_URL env var support to backend (separate DB for tests)
- Update docker-compose.yml to spin up a second Postgres service (modishlog_test) used only when ENVIRONMENT=test
- Update frontend/playwright.config.ts: add globalSetup/globalTeardown hooks that:
  * Before suite: reset test DB (run migrations fresh, seed minimal fixtures)
  * After suite: drop/truncate test DB data
- The main dev DB with migrated POS data must NEVER be touched by E2E runs

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `python scripts/pos_migrate.py --step=verify` prints POS product/sales/purchase counts
- [ ] `python scripts/pos_migrate.py --step=wipe` clears all local data, schema intact
- [ ] `python scripts/pos_migrate.py --step=migrate` populates all tables from live POS
- [ ] `docker compose exec backend pytest tests/` still passes after migration
- [ ] `ng e2e` uses isolated test DB, never touches dev data
- [ ] Dev DB persists across `docker compose restart`
tasks.testStrategy:
1. After --step=verify: manually check POS product count matches what we see on the POS UI
2. After --step=wipe: run SELECT COUNT(*) on key tables to confirm 0 rows
3. After --step=migrate: run SELECT COUNT(*) on products, sales, suppliers — must be non-zero; spot-check a known product (e.g. a board SKU) exists with correct price
4. Run pytest — all existing tests must still pass (they use fixture data, not the dev DB)
5. Run ng e2e — confirm test DB gets created, tests run, dev DB unchanged after run

tasks.title: Live POS sync — incremental polling from staging
tasks.description: Investigate and implement continuous sync between the live POS (pos.virtualrx.com.ng) and the staging environment so that new sales, purchases, and stock updates in the POS automatically reflect in ModishLog without a full wipe-and-reimport.
tasks.details:
1. First verify POS date-filter support: probe GET /sells?start_date=X&end_date=Y and GET /purchases?start_date=X&end_date=Y with real credentials to confirm the endpoints honour the params and filter by transaction date (not just created_at). Also check whether updated/voided records are catchable via a modified-since param.

2. Design an incremental sync strategy: store a last_synced_at watermark (e.g. in a settings table or a flat file), pull only records newer than that watermark on each run, upsert by POS ID (add a pos_id column to sales/purchase_orders if not already present to avoid duplicates), advance the watermark on success.

3. Implement a background scheduler (APScheduler or a simple cron via docker-compose) that runs the incremental pull every 5–15 minutes inside the backend container.

4. Handle edge cases: session expiry re-auth (already done in POSClient), partial failures (roll back watermark on error), deleted/voided records in POS (soft-delete or mark cancelled in ModishLog).

5. Write tests for the incremental upsert logic (mock POS responses, assert no duplicate records, assert watermark advances).
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests for upsert logic with mock POS data. Integration test: run two sync cycles with overlapping date windows and assert idempotency (no duplicate sales or orders created).

tasks.title: User management — admin panel for users and roles

tasks.details:
## Current state

- Auth router exposes: register, login, refresh, logout, forgot-password, reset-password, admin/unlock, /me.

- No frontend page for user management exists.

## Backend work

### 1. Extend UserRole if needed
Review whether additional roles are required (e.g. `VIEWER`, `CASHIER`). Add via Alembic migration if so.

### 2. New admin-only endpoints (add to `src/auth/router.py` or a new `src/users/` domain)
All endpoints require `role == ADMIN` via a `require_admin` dependency.

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/admin/users` | Paginated list of all users (id, email, full_name, role, is_active, created_at, last_login) |
| POST | `/admin/users/invite` | Create a new user account with a temporary password; send invite email |
| PATCH | `/admin/users/{user_id}` | Update full_name, role, is_active |
| POST | `/admin/users/{user_id}/deactivate` | Set is_active=False, revoke all refresh tokens |
| POST | `/admin/users/{user_id}/activate` | Set is_active=True |
| POST | `/admin/users/{user_id}/reset-password` | Admin-initiated password reset (generates reset link / temp password) |
| DELETE | `/admin/users/{user_id}` | Soft-delete (set is_active=False + anonymise PII) — cannot delete self |

### 3. Schema additions (`src/auth/schemas.py`)
- `UserListItem` — id, email, full_name, role, is_active, created_at
- `UserListResponse` — items: list[UserListItem], total, page, page_size
- `UserInvite` — email, full_name, role
- `UserUpdate` — full_name?, role?, is_active?

### 4. Service additions (`src/auth/service.py`)
- `list_users(db, page, page_size, search)` — paginated query with optional name/email search
- `invite_user(db, data)` — create User with hashed temp password, send invite email via existing email utility
- `update_user(db, user_id, data, requesting_user_id)` — guard: cannot demote self, cannot deactivate self
- `deactivate_user(db, user_id)` — is_active=False + delete all RefreshToken rows for that user
- `admin_reset_password(db, user_id)` — reuse existing PasswordResetToken flow

### 5. Tests (TDD — write first)
- `test_list_users_returns_paginated_results`
- `test_list_users_search_by_email`
- `test_invite_user_creates_active_account`
- `test_invite_user_duplicate_email_raises`
- `test_update_user_role`
- `test_admin_cannot_deactivate_self`
- `test_deactivate_user_revokes_refresh_tokens`
- `test_non_admin_cannot_access_user_management` (403)

## Frontend work (`frontend/src/app/features/settings/` or new `users/` feature)

### Pages / components
1. **Users list page** — table with columns: Name, Email, Role (badge), Status (Active/Inactive), Joined, Actions.

   - Pagination.

2. **Invite User modal/dialog**
   - Fields: Full Name, Email, Role (dropdown: Admin / Sales Manager).
   - On submit: POST `/admin/users/invite`, show success toast with note that an invite email was sent.

3. **Edit User slide-over / dialog**
   - Fields: Full Name, Role.
   - Toggle: Active / Inactive (with confirmation dialog before deactivating).
   - "Reset Password" button → calls admin reset endpoint, shows toast.
   - Cannot edit own role or deactivate self (disable controls + tooltip).

4. **Role badge component** — reuse/extend existing `StatusBadgeComponent`; green for ADMIN, blue for SALES_MANAGER, grey for inactive.

5. **Guard**: settings/users route requires `currentUser.role === 'admin'`; non-admins see a 403 page.

### Navigation
Add "Users" entry to the Settings sidebar (or a top-level nav entry), visible only to ADMIN role.

### E2E tests (`frontend/e2e/`)
- `users-management.spec.ts`: invite user → appears in list → deactivate → status badge changes → reactivate.
- `users-access-control.spec.ts`: SALES_MANAGER user cannot see Users nav link and gets 403 on direct URL.

## Alembic migration
If new columns are added to `users` table (e.g. `last_login_at`) or `UserRole` enum is extended, generate a new migration: `alembic revision --autogenerate -m "add user management fields"`.

tasks.title: Migration v2 — complete POS data import (customers, returns, payments, FIFO batches, stock history)
tasks.description: The current POS migration (pos_migrate.py) leaves large categories of data unimported: customers, sell returns, purchase returns, stock adjustment history, sale invoice numbers, payment details, per-line discount/tax, and InventoryBatch records. This task fixes all of those gaps so ModishLog has a complete, faithful copy of the POS data.
tasks.details:
## Background / current state

`pos_migrate.py` currently imports: products, suppliers (partial fields), sales (partial fields), purchases (partial fields). It does NOT import customers, sell returns, purchase returns, stock adjustments, or InventoryBatch records. Payment fields, discount/tax per line, invoice numbers, and several product/supplier fields are all silently ignored.

---

## 1. Customers — add fetch and import

**POS endpoint:** `GET /contacts?type=customer&per_page=500`

**Add to POSClient:**
```python
def fetch_customers(self) -> list[dict]:
    data = self._json_get("/contacts?type=customer&per_page=500")
    return data.get("data", [])
```

**Fields to map to `Customer` model** (all present in the POS contact response):

| POS field | Customer column |
|-----------|----------------|
| `name` | `name` |
| `email` | `email` |
| `mobile` | `contact_number` |
| `contact_no` | `alternate_number` (add column — see model changes below) |
| `address_line_1` + `address_line_2` | `address` (concatenate) |
| `city` | `city` (add column) |
| `state` | `state` (add column) |
| `country` | `country` (add column) |
| `zip_code` | `zip_code` (add column) |
| `tax_number` | `tax_number` (add column) |
| `pay_term_number` | `pay_term_number` (add column) |
| `pay_term_type` | `pay_term_type` (add column, reuse PayTermType enum) |
| `opening_balance` | `opening_balance` (add column, Numeric 18,6) |
| `credit_limit` | `credit_limit` (add column, Numeric 18,6, nullable) |
| `contact_status` | `is_active` (add column, Boolean default True) |
| `customer_group_id` | `customer_group` (add String(100) column, nullable) |

**Model changes needed:** Add all columns above to `src/customers/models.py`. Generate Alembic migration: `alembic revision --autogenerate -m "enrich_customer_model_for_pos_import"`.

**Build a `customer_map: dict[str, uuid.UUID]` (POS id → local uuid)** for linking sales.

---

## 2. Suppliers — fill in missing fields

The migration calls `/contacts?type=supplier` but only reads 7 of the available fields. Add mapping for the rest (all columns exist on the `Supplier` model already):

| POS field | Supplier column | Currently imported? |
|-----------|----------------|---------------------|
| `contact_no` | `alternate_number` | NO — add |
| `address_line_2` | `address_line_2` | NO — add |
| `zip_code` | `zip_code` | NO — add |
| `pay_term_number` | `pay_term_number` | NO — add |
| `pay_term_type` | `pay_term_type` | NO — add |
| `opening_balance` | `opening_balance` | NO — add |
| `tax_number` | `tax_number` | NO — add |

---

## 3. Products — fill in missing fields

Add to the product import loop (all columns exist on Product model or need adding):

| POS field | Product column | Action |
|-----------|---------------|--------|
| `product_description` | `description` | Add to mapping |
| `image` (URL) | `image_url` | Add to mapping |
| `alert_quantity` | `InventoryLevel.low_stock_threshold` | Use POS value instead of hardcoded `10` |
| `barcode` | `barcode` | Add `String(100)` column to Product model + migration |
| `unit` | `unit` | Add `String(50)` column to Product model + migration |

---

## 4. Sales — capture missing fields

**In `_parse_sell_lines_from_html()`** — the receipt HTML table has 7 columns; currently only cols 1 (product), 2 (qty), 3 (unit_price), 7 (subtotal) are used. Add:
- **Col 4** (`discount`) → `Sale.discount_amount` (already on model, never populated)
- **Col 5** (`tax`) → Add `tax_amount: Decimal` column to `Sale` model + migration
- **Col 6** (`price_inc_tax`) → store as reference on sale line (or use to cross-check total)

**From the `/sells` list row header**, read and store:
- `invoice_no` / `ref_no` → Add `invoice_number: String(100)` column to `Sale` model + migration
- `name` (customer name from contact) → `Sale.customer_name` (column exists, never populated)
- `payment_method` → `Sale.payment_method` (column exists, never populated)
- `payment_status` (actual value, not hardcoded "paid") → `Sale.payment_status`
- `total_paid` → `Sale.payment_amount` (column exists, never populated)
- `final_total - total_paid` → derive `Sale.payment_date` where applicable

**Customer linkage:** After importing customers, match `sale_header["name"]` against `customer_map` by name (fuzzy if needed) and set `Sale.customer_id`.

---

## 5. Sell returns — new import section

**Add to POSClient:**
```python
def fetch_sell_returns(self) -> list[dict]:
    data = self._json_get("/sell-returns?per_page=2000")
    return data.get("data", [])
```

**Map to `SellReturn` model** (already exists: `sale_id, return_date, total_amount, amount_paid, notes, created_by`):

| POS field | SellReturn column |
|-----------|------------------|
| `transaction_date` | `return_date` |
| `final_total` | `total_amount` (convert NGN→USD) |
| `total_paid` | `amount_paid` (convert NGN→USD) |
| link via `invoice_no` → original `sale_id` | `sale_id` |
| `notes` from detail if available | `notes` |

Add `ref_no: String(100)` to `SellReturn` model to store POS reference.

---

## 6. Purchase returns — new import section

**Add to POSClient:**
```python
def fetch_purchase_returns(self) -> list[dict]:
    data = self._json_get("/purchase-returns?per_page=2000")
    return data.get("data", [])
```

**Map to `PurchaseReturn` model** (already exists: `original_order_id, ref_no, return_date, total_amount, amount_paid, notes, created_by`):

| POS field | PurchaseReturn column |
|-----------|----------------------|
| `ref_no` | `ref_no` |
| `transaction_date` | `return_date` |
| `final_total` | `total_amount` (convert NGN→USD via usdngn_rate) |
| `total_paid` | `amount_paid` (convert NGN→USD) |
| link via original purchase ref → `original_order_id` | `original_order_id` |

---

## 7. Stock adjustment history — new import section

**Add to POSClient:**
```python
def fetch_stock_adjustments(self) -> list[dict]:
    data = self._json_get("/stock-adjustments?per_page=2000")
    return data.get("data", [])
```

**Map to `StockMovement`** — add new `MovementType` enum values first:
- `STOCK_ADJUSTMENT` — general manual correction
- `OPENING_STOCK` — opening balance entry
- `STOCK_TRANSFER` — inter-location move (if applicable)

Per adjustment line from POS:
- `type` → map to `MovementType` (`opening` → `OPENING_STOCK`, `normal` → `STOCK_ADJUSTMENT`)
- `quantity` (signed) → `quantity_change`
- `product_id` → lookup from product_map
- `date` → `created_at`
- `reason` / `note` → `reason`
- Set `quantity_before` / `quantity_after` from cumulative running total (compute in sequence, ordered by date)

---

## 8. InventoryBatch — populate from purchase line items

Currently zero `InventoryBatch` records are created during migration even though every delivered purchase order has line items. The FIFO engine is blind without these.

For every `OrderLineItem` on a DELIVERED `PurchaseOrder`, create an `InventoryBatch`:

```python
batch = InventoryBatch(
    product_id=item.product_id,
    order_id=po.id,
    quantity_received=int(item.quantity),
    quantity_remaining=int(item.quantity),   # assume all still in stock at migration time
    unit_cost_usd=item.unit_cost,
    fx_rate_at_arrival=po.fx_rate_at_creation or usdngn_rate,
    logistics_allocation_per_unit=Decimal("0"),
    landed_cost_per_unit=item.unit_cost,
    received_at=po.actual_delivery_date or po.order_date,
)
```

Then deduct sold quantities from batches (FIFO order) using the existing `InventoryBatch` depletion logic in `src/inventory/service.py`, or replay StockMovements in chronological order.

---

## 9. Expenses — new entity

UltimatePOS has a full expense module (`/expenses`, `/expense-categories`). ModishLog has no Expense model at all. Add:

**Add to POSClient:**
```python
def fetch_expense_categories(self) -> list[dict]: ...
def fetch_expenses(self) -> list[dict]: ...
```

**New models** (`src/expenses/models.py` — new domain):
```
ExpenseCategory: id, name, description, created_by
Expense: id, category_id, amount (Numeric 18,6), currency, fx_rate, amount_usd, expense_date, ref_no, note, payment_method, location_id, created_by
```

tasks.title: Reports completeness — fix placeholders, add missing reports, wire sales returns and location filters
tasks.description: Multiple critical gaps exist in the current reports: hardcoded-zero placeholders for sales returns, purchase due, and sales due; opening/closing stock values that are identical (both use current snapshot instead of point-in-time); and entirely missing report types (expense, per-product, tax, trending products, customer ledger). This task fixes all gaps and adds the missing report pages.
tasks.details:
## Current broken values (fix first)

### 1. Profit & Loss — fix hardcoded zeros

File: `backend/src/reports/service.py`

**`purchase_due`** (currently `Decimal("0")` at line 143):
Replace with: sum of `PurchaseOrder.balance_remaining` for orders where `payment_status IN (UNPAID, PARTIAL)` and `order_date` within the report period.

**`sales_due`** (currently `Decimal("0")` at line 144):
Replace with: sum of `(Sale.total_amount - Sale.payment_amount)` for completed sales where `payment_status != 'paid'` and `sale_date` within the period.

**`total_sales_returns`** — add to P&L schema and service:
```python
total_sales_returns = sum of SellReturn.total_amount where return_date in period
```

**`opening_stock_value` vs `closing_stock_value`** (currently identical):
- `closing_stock_value`: current batch snapshot (keep as-is).
- `opening_stock_value`: sum of `InventoryBatch.quantity_remaining * InventoryBatch.landed_cost_per_unit` where `received_at < start_date` MINUS `StockMovement.quantity_change` for `SALE_DEPLETION` movements between `received_at` and `start_date`. This requires the batch data from Migration v2 task to be populated first.

### 2. Purchase & Sale report — fix sales returns

File: `backend/src/reports/service.py`

**`total_sales_returns`** (currently `Decimal("0")` at line 293):
Replace with: sum of `SellReturn.total_amount` where `return_date` within period.

---

## 3. Add location filter to all report endpoints

All three existing report endpoints (`/reports/profit-loss`, `/reports/stock`, `/reports/purchase-sale`) currently have no `location_id` filter even though `Sale`, `PurchaseOrder`, and `InventoryLevel` all carry `location_id`.

Add optional `location_id: uuid.UUID | None = Query(None)` to each router endpoint and pass down to service queries. When provided, filter all subqueries by `location_id`.

---

## 4. Add CSV/PDF export to P&L and Purchase & Sale

Currently only the stock report has CSV export.

- Add `GET /reports/profit-loss/export-csv` endpoint (mirrors stock export pattern).
- Add `GET /reports/purchase-sale/export-csv` endpoint.
- Frontend: add "Export CSV" button to both report pages (same UI pattern as stock report page).

---

## 5. New report: Per-product sales report

**New endpoint:** `GET /reports/product-sales?start_date=&end_date=&category_id=&location_id=&page=&page_size=`

**New schema `ProductSalesReport`:**
```python
class ProductSalesRow(BaseModel):
    product_id: uuid.UUID
    sku: str
    product_name: str
    category: str
    quantity_sold: int
    total_revenue: Decimal
    total_cogs: Decimal          # sum of fifo_cogs where not null
    gross_margin: Decimal        # total_revenue - total_cogs
    gross_margin_pct: Decimal    # gross_margin / total_revenue * 100
    avg_unit_price: Decimal
    return_quantity: int         # from SellReturn lines
    net_quantity: int            # quantity_sold - return_quantity

class ProductSalesReport(BaseModel):
    rows: list[ProductSalesRow]
    total_revenue: Decimal
    total_cogs: Decimal
    total_gross_margin: Decimal
    period_start: date
    period_end: date
    total: int
    page: int
    page_size: int
```

**Service query:** Group `Sale` rows by `product_id` where `status=COMPLETED` and `sale_date` in range. JOIN `SellReturn` for net quantities.

**Frontend page:** `frontend/src/app/features/reports/pages/product-sales-page.component.ts`
- Date range picker (same pattern as existing report pages).
- Category dropdown filter.
- Sortable table: SKU, Product, Category, Qty Sold, Revenue, COGS, Gross Margin, Margin %, Avg Price, Returns, Net Qty.
- CSV export button.
- Add card to `reports-index.component.ts`.

---

## 6. New report: Expense report

Depends on the Expense model from Migration v2 task (task #156).

**New endpoint:** `GET /reports/expenses?start_date=&end_date=&category_id=&location_id=`

**New schema `ExpenseReport`:**
```python
class ExpenseCategoryRow(BaseModel):
    category: str
    total_amount: Decimal
    transaction_count: int

class ExpenseReport(BaseModel):

    total_expenses: Decimal
    period_start: date
    period_end: date
```

**Frontend page:** `frontend/src/app/features/reports/pages/expense-report-page.component.ts`
- Date range, category filter, location filter.
- Summary KPI cards: Total Expenses, Category breakdown bar chart.
- Detailed table: Date, Category, Ref#, Amount, Payment Method, Note.
- Add card to reports index.

---

## 7. New report: Trending products

**New endpoint:** `GET /reports/trending-products?start_date=&end_date=&limit=10&sort_by=revenue|quantity`

**Schema:**
```python
class TrendingProductRow(BaseModel):
    rank: int
    product_id: uuid.UUID
    product_name: str
    sku: str
    category: str
    quantity_sold: int
    total_revenue: Decimal
    gross_margin_pct: Decimal | None
```

**Frontend:** Add a "Trending Products" section to the dashboard page (top 5 by revenue) and a dedicated report card in the reports index.

---

## 8. New report: Tax report

Depends on `tax_amount` being populated on Sale and PurchaseOrder (from Migration v2 task).

**New endpoint:** `GET /reports/tax?start_date=&end_date=&location_id=`

**Schema:**
```python
class TaxReport(BaseModel):
    output_tax: Decimal       # tax collected on sales
    input_tax: Decimal        # tax paid on purchases
    net_tax_liability: Decimal  # output - input
    period_start: date
    period_end: date
```

**Frontend page:** Simple summary + date range picker. Add to reports index.

---

## 9. Fix stock report — add date range and product drill-down

**Backend:** Add `start_date` / `end_date` params to `GET /reports/stock`. When provided, return stock level as-at that date by replaying `StockMovement` history backwards from current.

**Backend:** Add `GET /reports/stock/{product_id}/history` endpoint:
- Returns all `StockMovement` rows for the product, paginated, with date range filter.
- Schema: date, movement_type, qty_change, qty_before, qty_after, reference_type, reference_id, reason.

**Frontend — drill-down:** On the stock report table, clicking a product row opens a slide-over showing:
- Product summary (current stock, value, threshold).

**Frontend — category filter:** Wire up the `category_id` query param (backend supports it, UI never sends it). Add a category dropdown above the stock report table.

---

## 10. Dashboard — fix and enrich KPIs

- **Gross margin %** KPI card: `(total_sales - fifo_cogs_sum) / total_sales * 100`. Requires FIFO batches from Migration v2.
- **Inventory value** KPI: sum of current `InventoryBatch.quantity_remaining * landed_cost_per_unit`.
- **Low stock count** KPI: count of `InventoryLevel` rows where `quantity_on_hand <= low_stock_threshold`.
- **Top 5 products by revenue** (replace "recent 5 sales" in `recent_sales`): group by `product_id`, sum `total_amount`, top 5.
- **Sales returns KPI**: `total_sell_return` already in dashboard schema but not visible in the UI — add a card.

## 11. Tests (TDD — write first)

**Backend:**
- `test_profit_loss_purchase_due_not_zero`
- `test_profit_loss_sales_due_not_zero`
- `test_profit_loss_includes_sales_returns`
- `test_purchase_sale_report_includes_sell_returns`
- `test_opening_stock_differs_from_closing_stock_when_purchases_in_period`
- `test_profit_loss_location_filter`
- `test_product_sales_report_groups_by_product`
- `test_product_sales_report_margin_calculation`
- `test_expense_report_groups_by_category`
- `test_trending_products_sorted_by_revenue`
- `test_stock_history_endpoint_returns_movements`

**Frontend E2E:**
- `reports-profit-loss.spec.ts`: verify purchase_due, sales_due, sales_returns show non-zero values after data is present.
- `reports-stock-drill-down.spec.ts`: click product row → slide-over shows movement history.
- `reports-product-sales.spec.ts`: filter by date range → table updates.
- `reports-expense.spec.ts`: date range → category breakdown visible.

tasks.title: Business settings — persist business profile, currency, tax config, and fix dead UI fields
tasks.description: ModishLog's settings backend is extremely thin: only fiscal year start date and API keys are stored. Business profile (name, logo, address, tax number), default currency, global stock threshold, and tax configuration are either absent from the DB entirely or present in the UI but never saved. This task adds a proper business profile table, wires up the dead UI fields, and imports the business settings from the POS.
tasks.details:
## Current gaps

| Setting | Backend state | Frontend state |
|---------|--------------|----------------|
| Business name | Not stored anywhere | Not in UI |
| Business logo | Not stored anywhere | Not in UI |
| Business address | Only on `BusinessLocation`, not a global profile | Not in UI |
| Tax / VAT number | Not stored anywhere | Not in UI |
| Default currency | Not stored anywhere | In UI as local var, never saved |
| Global low-stock threshold | Not stored anywhere | In UI as local var (`globalStockThreshold`), never saved |
| Financial year | `UserPreferences.fiscal_year_start_month/day` ✅ | Saved correctly ✅ |
| Anthropic API key | `UserApiKey` table ✅ | Saved correctly ✅ |
| "Test API connection" button | No backend endpoint | Stub — `apiKeyStatus.set('testing')` only |
| Invoice defaults (footer text, default notes) | Not stored | Not in UI |
| Default payment terms | Not stored | Not in UI |
| Multi-location POS data | Only 1 location hardcoded in migration | Locations CRUD exists ✅ |

---

## 1. New `BusinessProfile` model

New file: `src/settings/models.py` — add `BusinessProfile` (single-row table, one record per deployment):

```python
class BusinessProfile(UUIDMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
    __tablename__ = "business_profile"

    business_name: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255))
    logo_url: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(500))
    address_line_1: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255))
    address_line_2: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255))
    city: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(100))
    state: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(100))
    country: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(100))
    zip_code: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(20))
    phone: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(50))
    email: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255))
    website: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255))
    tax_number: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(100))   # VAT/TIN/RC number
    registration_number: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(100))
    currency: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(3), default="NGN")
    timezone: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(60), default="Africa/Lagos")
    updated_by: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("users.id"))
```

Generate Alembic migration: `alembic revision --autogenerate -m "add_business_profile"`.

---

## 2. New `AppSettings` model (global key-value store)

For settings that don't fit the structured profile (global thresholds, feature flags, invoice defaults):

```python
class AppSetting(Base):
    __tablename__ = "app_settings"
    key: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(100), primary_key=True)
    value: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text)
    updated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(...)
    updated_by: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("users.id"))
```

Pre-defined keys (seed on first run):
- `global_low_stock_threshold` (default `"10"`)

- `invoice_footer_text` (default `""`)
- `invoice_default_notes` (default `""`)

---

## 3. New backend endpoints

Add to `src/settings/router.py`:

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/settings/business-profile` | Return current `BusinessProfile` (upsert-on-read: create empty row if absent) |
| PUT | `/settings/business-profile` | Update any/all fields; require ADMIN role |
| POST | `/settings/business-profile/logo` | Upload logo image → store to `/app/uploads/logo/`; return URL |
| GET | `/settings/app` | Return all `AppSetting` key-value pairs as a dict |
| PUT | `/settings/app/{key}` | Update a single setting by key; require ADMIN role |
| GET | `/settings/api-key/{key_name}/test` | Actually test the Anthropic key (fix current stub) |

**Fix "Test API Connection"** (`GET /settings/api-key/anthropic/test`):
Retrieve the stored key, make a minimal `POST /v1/messages` call to the Anthropic API with `max_tokens=1`, return `{ "success": true/false, "model": "...", "latency_ms": N }`.

---

## 4. Update `UserPreferences` — add per-user settings

Extend `UserPreferences` model with commonly needed per-user prefs:

```python
notification_low_stock: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, default=True)
notification_order_received: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, default=True)
notification_sale_completed: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, default=False)
default_location_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("business_locations.id"))
```

Add `GET /settings/preferences` and `PUT /settings/preferences` endpoints.

---

## 5. Import business settings from POS

Add to `pos_migrate.py` — step 3b (after business location):

**Add to POSClient:**
```python
def fetch_business_settings(self) -> dict:
    return self._json_get("/business-settings")

def fetch_business_locations(self) -> list[dict]:
    return self._json_get("/business-locations?per_page=50").get("data", [])
```

**Import into `BusinessProfile`:**
From `/business-settings` response, map:

- `city`, `state`, `country`, `zip_code` → corresponding fields

**Import all business locations** (not just one hardcoded):
Replace the single hardcoded `BusinessLocation` with fetching `/business-locations` and creating one `BusinessLocation` per POS location. Build a `location_map: dict[str, uuid.UUID]` (POS location_id → local uuid). Use this map when importing sales and purchases so each record is correctly assigned to its actual location.

---

## 6. Frontend — business profile settings section

**Update `settings-page.component.ts`** — add a "Business Profile" section at the top of the settings page:

**Fields to render (two-column grid):**
- Business Name, Phone, Email, Website

**Wire up dead fields:**

- `globalStockThreshold` (currently local var line 248) → save to `PUT /settings/app/global_low_stock_threshold`

**Fix "Test API Connection" button** (currently `apiKeyStatus.set('testing')` only):

**Add "Notifications" subsection** (renders `UserPreferences` notification toggles):

## 7. BusinessLocation — add missing fields

Extend `BusinessLocation` model:

tasks.title: Add product variant support across backend and frontend
tasks.description: Add first-class product variant support to ModishLog. A product (e.g. "T-Shirt") can have multiple variants (e.g. Red/S, Red/M, Blue/L), each with its own SKU, barcode, price override, cost price override, and independent inventory tracking. This is a prerequisite for the data migration framework — external POS systems (UltimatePOS, Shopify, Square) model variants natively and the import pipeline must be able to resolve them.
tasks.details:
## New model: `ProductVariant` (backend/src/products/models.py)

```python
class ProductVariant(Base):
    __tablename__ = "product_variants"

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(primary_key=True, default=uuid4)
    business_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("businesses.id"), nullable=False)
    product_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("products.id"), nullable=False)
    name: Mapped[str]          # e.g. "Red / Large" — display label
    sku: Mapped[str | None]
    barcode: Mapped[str | None]
    attributes: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(JSONB)  # {"size": "L", "color": "Red"}
    price_override: Mapped[Decimal | None]    # NULL = inherit from parent product
    cost_price_override: Mapped[Decimal | None]
    is_active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(default=True)
    created_at: Mapped[datetime]
    updated_at: Mapped[datetime]

    product: Mapped["Product"] = relationship(back_populates="variants")
```

Add to `Product` model:
```python
has_variants: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(default=False)
variants: Mapped[list["ProductVariant"]] = relationship(
    back_populates="product", cascade="all, delete-orphan"
)
```

## Schema changes on existing tables

Add `variant_id UUID NULLABLE FK → product_variants.id` to:
- `inventory_levels`
- `inventory_batches`
- `stock_movements`
- `sale_lines` (or equivalent sales line table)
- `order_line_items`
- `price_history`
- `low_stock_alerts`
- `supplier_products`
- `stock_count_items`

Rule: if `variant_id IS NOT NULL`, it takes precedence over `product_id` for inventory/pricing lookups. A product with `has_variants = TRUE` should never be sold/stocked at the product level — only at the variant level.

## Alembic migration

Single migration file. Add `product_variants` table first, then add `variant_id` column to each of the above tables. No data backfill needed — all existing rows have `variant_id = NULL` (meaning "no variant, use product directly"), which is valid.

Use `values_callable` on any new Enum columns per project rules.

## Backend API changes (backend/src/products/)

New endpoints:
- `POST /products/{product_id}/variants` — create a variant
- `GET /products/{product_id}/variants` — list variants for a product
- `PUT /products/{product_id}/variants/{variant_id}` — update a variant
- `DELETE /products/{product_id}/variants/{variant_id}` — deactivate (soft delete)

`GET /products` and `GET /products/{id}` responses must include `has_variants: bool` and `variants: []` (via `selectinload(Product.variants)`).

Pricing resolution helper in `products/service.py`:
```python
def resolve_price(product: Product, variant: ProductVariant | None) -> Decimal:
    if variant and variant.price_override is not None:
        return variant.price_override
    return product.selling_price
```

Same pattern for `resolve_cost_price`.

## Inventory service changes

`InventoryLevel` lookups must be variant-aware:
- When `variant_id` is provided, filter `WHERE product_id = ? AND variant_id = ?`
- When no variant, filter `WHERE product_id = ? AND variant_id IS NULL`

Low stock alerts must fire per variant, not just per product.

## Sales and orders service changes

`SaleLine` / `OrderLineItem` creation must accept optional `variant_id`. If the product `has_variants = True` and no `variant_id` is supplied, return HTTP 422 with message: "This product requires a variant to be selected."

## Frontend changes (frontend/src/app/features/products/)

Product detail/edit page:
- Add "Variants" section (shown only when `has_variants` toggled on)
- Table of variants with columns: Name, SKU, Barcode, Price Override, Cost Override, Active
- Add/edit/delete variant inline
- Toggling `has_variants` OFF when variants exist should warn the user

Sale creation / order creation:
- When a product with `has_variants = true` is selected, show a variant picker dropdown before allowing quantity entry
- Display selected variant's resolved price

Product list page:
- Show variant count badge on products that have variants

## TDD

Write tests BEFORE implementation in `backend/tests/test_products.py`:
- Create product with variants — happy path
- Sell a variant product without specifying variant — expect 422
- Inventory level isolated per variant
- Price resolution: variant override takes precedence over parent price
- Deactivating a variant does not delete historical sale lines referencing it
tasks.testStrategy:
Backend (pytest):
- POST /products/{id}/variants → 201, variant created with correct attributes
- GET /products/{id} → includes variants array
- POST /sales with variant_id → sale line references variant, uses variant price_override
- POST /sales with has_variants product but no variant_id → 422
- Inventory level query returns correct stock for each variant independently
- Deactivated variant still appears on historical sale lines (soft delete)

Frontend (Playwright e2e):
- Create a product, toggle on variants, add 3 variants (Red/S, Red/M, Blue/L) with different prices
- Create a sale — select the product, verify variant picker appears, select Red/M, verify price shown is variant price
- Check inventory page shows per-variant stock levels

tasks.title: Add tax, discount and payment method fields to sales, orders and expenses
tasks.description: Extend the sales, purchase order, sale line, order line item, and expense tables with tax, discount and payment method fields so that migrated data from external POS/accounting systems (UltimatePOS, QuickBooks, Sage, Shopify) is imported as-is without information loss. These fields are required by the ETL migration framework and also improve native ModishLog functionality for businesses that charge VAT or apply discounts.
tasks.details:
## Schema changes (Alembic migration)

### `sales` table — add columns:
```sql
discount_amount   NUMERIC(18,6)  NULL  DEFAULT 0
discount_type     VARCHAR(20)    NULL              -- 'percentage' | 'fixed'
tax_amount        NUMERIC(18,6)  NULL  DEFAULT 0
tax_rate          NUMERIC(7,4)   NULL              -- e.g. 0.075 for 7.5%
payment_method    VARCHAR(50)    NULL              -- 'cash' | 'card' | 'bank_transfer' | 'mobile_money' | 'credit' | 'other'
payment_reference VARCHAR(100)   NULL              -- e.g. card last 4, transfer ref
```

### `sale_lines` (or equivalent) table — add columns:
```sql
line_discount_amount  NUMERIC(18,6)  NULL  DEFAULT 0
line_tax_amount       NUMERIC(18,6)  NULL  DEFAULT 0
tax_rate              NUMERIC(7,4)   NULL
```

### `purchase_orders` table — add columns:
```sql
tax_amount        NUMERIC(18,6)  NULL  DEFAULT 0
discount_amount   NUMERIC(18,6)  NULL  DEFAULT 0
payment_method    VARCHAR(50)    NULL
payment_reference VARCHAR(100)   NULL
```

### `order_line_items` table — add columns:
```sql
line_tax_amount   NUMERIC(18,6)  NULL  DEFAULT 0
line_discount_amount NUMERIC(18,6) NULL DEFAULT 0
```

### `expenses` table — add columns (if not already present):
```sql
tax_amount        NUMERIC(18,6)  NULL  DEFAULT 0
payment_method    VARCHAR(50)    NULL
payment_reference VARCHAR(100)   NULL
```

All new columns are nullable with sensible defaults so existing rows are unaffected.

## Enum handling

`discount_type` and `payment_method` are VARCHAR not Enum — they use string values to avoid enum migration pain and to accommodate future values from import adapters without schema changes. Validate the value set in the Pydantic schema layer, not the DB layer.

Valid `payment_method` values (open list, validated in schema):
`cash`, `card`, `bank_transfer`, `mobile_money`, `credit`, `cheque`, `other`

Valid `discount_type` values:
`percentage`, `fixed`

## Pydantic schema changes

Update `SaleCreate`, `SaleRead`, `SaleLineCreate`, `SaleLineRead`, `PurchaseOrderCreate`, `PurchaseOrderRead`, `OrderLineItemCreate`, `OrderLineItemRead`, `ExpenseCreate`, `ExpenseRead` to include the new optional fields.

All new fields are `Optional[Decimal] = None` or `Optional[str] = None`.

## Service layer changes

### sales/service.py
- When `discount_type = 'percentage'`, validate that `discount_amount` is between 0 and 100
- When creating a sale, compute and store `total_amount` as:
  `subtotal - discount_amount + tax_amount`
  (Previously total_amount = subtotal only)
- Do NOT auto-compute tax or discount — store exactly what is passed in

### P&L / reports service
- Update gross profit calculation: `net_revenue = total_amount - tax_amount`
- Dashboard KPI for "Total Sales" should use `net_revenue` (ex-tax) not `total_amount`
- Add new KPI: "Total Tax Collected" (sum of `tax_amount` across sales in period)

## Frontend changes

### Sales creation form
- Add optional "Discount" field (type selector: % or fixed amount) below subtotal
- Add optional "Tax" field (rate % auto-computes amount, or enter amount directly)
- Add "Payment Method" dropdown (cash / card / bank transfer / mobile money / credit / other)
- Add "Payment Reference" text field (shown only if payment_method ≠ cash)
- Show live-computed total: subtotal − discount + tax

### Purchase order form
- Add "Tax" and "Discount" fields at order level
- Add "Payment Method" and "Payment Reference"

### Expense form
- Add "Tax Amount" optional field
- Add "Payment Method" dropdown

### Sales list / sale detail view
- Show payment method badge on each sale row
- Sale detail modal: show tax, discount, net amount breakdown

## TDD

Write tests BEFORE implementation in `backend/tests/test_sales.py` and `backend/tests/test_orders.py`:
- Create sale with percentage discount → total_amount computed correctly
- Create sale with fixed discount → total_amount computed correctly
- Create sale with tax_rate → tax_amount stored, net_revenue excludes it
- P&L report: tax_amount excluded from net revenue
- Create purchase order with tax and payment_method → stored and returned correctly
- All new fields default to NULL/0 — existing test suite must still pass unchanged
tasks.testStrategy:
Backend (pytest):
- Sale with 10% discount on ₦5,000 subtotal → discount_amount=500, total_amount=4,500+tax
- Sale with tax_rate=0.075 on ₦5,000 → tax_amount=375, net_revenue=5,000
- P&L report total_sales excludes tax_amount
- PO with payment_method='bank_transfer' + payment_reference='REF-001' → returned on GET
- All existing sales tests pass (new fields are optional/nullable)

Frontend (Playwright e2e):
- Create a sale with 5% discount and 7.5% VAT → verify total displayed correctly in UI
- Create a sale with payment_method=card and reference → reference field appears
- Sales list shows payment method badge

tasks.title: Build ETL data import framework (backend) — Extract, Transform, Load pipeline
tasks.description: Build a general-purpose ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) data import backend that allows any business to migrate their historical data into ModishLog from CSV files or supported source systems (UltimatePOS, QuickBooks CSV, Shopify CSV, Generic CSV). Supports full transaction history replay, variant-aware product import, deduplication, ID remapping, ghost record creation for deleted source records, and atomic rollback via migration_id tagging. This is the core engine that the frontend wizard (Task 163) drives.
tasks.details:
## New domain: `backend/src/data_import/`

Files: `router.py`, `service.py`, `models.py`, `schemas.py`, `exceptions.py`
Plus: `backend/src/data_import/etl/` sub-package with one file per layer:
- `extractor.py` — CSV parsing, format detection
- `transformer.py` — ID remapping, dedup, normalisation, ghost records
- `validator.py` — referential integrity, required fields, data quality
- `loader.py` — FK-ordered inserts, migration_id tagging, single transaction

---

## Database models (`models.py`)

```python
class MigrationJob(Base):
    __tablename__ = "migration_jobs"
    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(primary_key=True, default=uuid4)
    business_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("businesses.id"))
    status: Mapped[str]   # 'pending' | 'validating' | 'ready' | 'importing' | 'done' | 'failed' | 'rolled_back'
    source_system: Mapped[str]   # 'ultimatepos' | 'quickbooks' | 'shopify' | 'generic'
    created_at: Mapped[datetime]
    completed_at: Mapped[datetime | None]
    row_counts: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(JSONB)   # {"products": 120, "sales": 4500, ...}
    validation_errors: Mapped[list] = mapped_column(JSONB)  # [{entity, row, field, message}]
    validation_warnings: Mapped[list] = mapped_column(JSONB)
    options: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(JSONB)   # {"mode": "full_replay", "location_map": {...}}
```

Add `migration_id UUID NULL` column to ALL importable tables via Alembic:
`products`, `product_variants`, `product_categories`, `customers`, `suppliers`,
`supplier_products`, `sales`, `sale_lines`, `purchase_orders`, `order_line_items`,
`order_payments`, `inventory_levels`, `inventory_batches`, `stock_movements`,
`expenses`, `expense_categories`, `price_history`, `stock_counts`, `stock_count_items`

---

## API endpoints (`router.py`)

All routes scoped under `/api/v1/import/` and require auth (business_id from JWT):

```
GET  /import/templates                     → ZIP of all CSV templates with headers + example row
GET  /import/templates/{entity}            → single CSV template for one entity
POST /import/jobs                          → create job, upload files (multipart), returns job_id
GET  /import/jobs                          → list jobs for this business
GET  /import/jobs/{job_id}                 → job status + row_counts + errors
POST /import/jobs/{job_id}/validate        → run validation dry-run, populate errors/warnings
POST /import/jobs/{job_id}/confirm         → run full import in single transaction
DELETE /import/jobs/{job_id}              → rollback: DELETE WHERE migration_id = job_id
```

Static routes before parameterised — `/import/templates` before `/import/templates/{entity}`.

---

## ETL Layer 1 — Extractor (`extractor.py`)

Responsibilities:
- Parse CSV files (handle BOM, UTF-8, Latin-1 encoding detection)
- Detect date format automatically: try ISO 8601 first, then DD/MM/YYYY, MM/DD/YYYY, `01-Jul-26`
- Detect currency format: strip `₦`, `$`, `£`, `€`, handle `1,200.00` vs `1.200,00` (European)
- Return rows as `list[dict[str, str]]` — raw strings, no type coercion yet
- Detect source system from uploaded file headers (if headers match UltimatePOS/Shopify/QuickBooks known patterns, set `source_system` automatically)

---

## ETL Layer 2 — Transformer (`transformer.py`)

### ID remapping
Maintain a per-job mapping registry:
```python
id_map: dict[str, dict[str, UUID]] = {
    "products": {"POS-123": UUID("...")},
    "customers": {"C-456": UUID("...")},
    ...
}
```
When loading a sale that references `product_id = "POS-123"`, look up `id_map["products"]["POS-123"]` to get the ModishLog UUID. Raise `TransformError` if not found (unless ghost record mode handles it).

### Deduplication
- **Customers**: match on `email` first, then `phone`. If match found, use existing record's ID and update name if blank.
- **Suppliers**: match on `name` (case-insensitive) + `email`.
- **Products**: match on `barcode` first (globally unique), then `sku` (business-scoped), then `name` (fuzzy warn only — never auto-merge on name alone).
- **Users**: match on `email` — never create duplicate user accounts.

### Ghost record creation
If a sale line references a product that doesn't appear in the products CSV (deleted in source system), create a ghost product:
```python
Product(
    name=f"[Deleted Product: {source_name or source_id}]",
    is_active=False,
    migration_id=job_id,
    ...
)
```
Ghost records are flagged in the validation report as warnings, not errors.

### Variant resolution
If source row has variant attributes (e.g., Shopify `Option1 Name/Value`, UltimatePOS `variation_id`):
- Find or create `ProductVariant` under the parent product
- Map all line items to the resolved variant_id

### Location mapping
Source system may have location names ("Main Store", "Warehouse"). Apply `options.location_map` dict from job options: `{"Main Store": <business_location_id>}`. If a source location has no mapping, assign to the business's default location and warn.

### Normalisation
- All dates → `date` or `datetime` Python objects
- All amounts → `Decimal` (ROUND_HALF_UP, 6dp)
- All quantities → `int`
- `payment_method` values normalised: "Credit Card" → "card", "Bank" → "bank_transfer", etc.

---

## ETL Layer 3 — Validator (`validator.py`)

Runs as a dry-run WITHOUT writing to DB. Returns structured report:

```python
class ValidationError(BaseModel):
    entity: str       # "sales"
    row: int          # 1-indexed CSV row number
    field: str        # "product_id"
    severity: str     # "error" | "warning"
    message: str      # "Product POS-123 not found and cannot be ghost-created"
```

Checks:
- Required fields present
- Date fields parseable
- Amount fields numeric and non-negative
- `variant_id` set when product `has_variants = True`
- All FK references resolvable (via id_map or dedup match or ghost creation)
- Duplicate detection across upload (e.g., same product SKU appears twice in CSV)
- Row count summary per entity

Job transitions to `status = 'ready'` only if zero errors (warnings allowed). If errors exist, job stays `'validating'` and client must fix CSV and re-upload.

---

## ETL Layer 4 — Loader (`loader.py`)

Insert order (respects FK dependency chain):
1. `business_locations` (if any new ones)
2. `users` (staff accounts — set `must_reset_password = True`, email invite triggered)
3. `expense_categories`
4. `product_categories` (parent before child — topological sort on `parent_id`)
5. `products` (with `migration_id = job_id`)
6. `product_variants`
7. `customers`
8. `suppliers`
9. `supplier_products`
10. `purchase_orders`
11. `order_line_items`
12. `order_payments`
13. `order_status_history`
14. `inventory_batches` (reference purchase_orders)
15. `stock_movements`
16. `inventory_levels` (computed from movements OR imported directly)
17. `price_history`
18. `sales`
19. `sale_lines`
20. `sell_returns`
21. `sale_audit_entries`
22. `expenses`
23. `stock_counts`
24. `stock_count_items`

All inserts in a single `async with session.begin()` block. Any exception rolls back the entire transaction. After commit, update `MigrationJob.status = 'done'` and `row_counts`.

---

## CSV Template format

Each template CSV has:
- Row 1: column headers (snake_case matching ModishLog field names)
- Row 2: example data row (commented with `#EXAMPLE` in first column)
- Row 3+: business fills in their data

Template ZIP includes a `README.txt` with:
- Import order (which files to fill first)
- Field-by-field descriptions
- Required vs optional fields
- Accepted date formats
- Accepted payment_method values

---

## Source system adapters

Thin transform wrappers that map source column names → ModishLog column names before passing to the generic transformer. One file per supported system:

- `adapters/ultimatepos.py` — maps UltimatePOS column names, handles `variation_id`, `tax_amount`, `discount_amount` from UltimatePOS sell data
- `adapters/quickbooks.py` — maps QuickBooks export format (Items, Invoices, Bills, Vendors)
- `adapters/shopify.py` — maps Shopify orders/products CSV export (handles `Option1 Name/Value` for variants)
- `adapters/generic.py` — passthrough, expects ModishLog column names exactly

Adapter selection: auto-detected from file headers or specified in job `source_system` field.

---

## Rollback

`DELETE /import/jobs/{job_id}` triggers:
```python
for table in reversed(INSERT_ORDER):
    await session.execute(
        delete(table).where(table.migration_id == job_id)
    )
await session.commit()
job.status = "rolled_back"
```

Reverse insert order ensures FK constraints don't block deletes.
tasks.testStrategy:
Backend (pytest) — write BEFORE implementation:
- Upload products CSV + sales CSV → validate → confirm → products and sales exist with migration_id
- Sale referencing deleted product → ghost product created, warning emitted, sale imports successfully
- Duplicate customer email → dedup merges, not duplicates
- Invalid date format in sales CSV → validation error on that row, job stays in 'validating'
- Rollback after confirm → all rows with migration_id deleted, counts return to pre-import state
- UltimatePOS adapter: column names mapped correctly before transformer runs
- Shopify adapter: Option1/Option2 columns mapped to ProductVariant attributes
- Full replay: 1000 sales imported → inventory_levels computed correctly from movements
- Location mapping: source location "Main Store" mapped to correct business_location_id

subtasks.title: Add live API extractor path alongside CSV extractor
subtasks.description: The ETL Extract layer must support two parallel extraction modes — CSV upload (for technical users) and live API connection (for non-technical users). Both modes feed into the same Transform → Validate → Load pipeline. Only the extraction step differs.
subtasks.details:
## Dual extraction architecture

The extractor interface must be abstract so both modes satisfy the same contract:

```python
class BaseExtractor(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    async def extract(self, job: MigrationJob) -> ExtractedData:
        """Return normalised raw rows per entity, ready for transformer."""
        ...

class CSVExtractor(BaseExtractor):
    """Reads from files uploaded by the user."""
    async def extract(self, job: MigrationJob) -> ExtractedData: ...

class APIExtractor(BaseExtractor):
    """Pulls live data from the source system API."""
    async def extract(self, job: MigrationJob) -> ExtractedData: ...
```

The loader picks the extractor based on `job.extraction_mode` field:
- `'csv'` → CSVExtractor
- `'api'` → APIExtractor (source-system-specific subclass per adapter)

## MigrationJob model additions

```python
extraction_mode: Mapped[str]          # 'csv' | 'api'
api_base_url: Mapped[str | None]      # only for api mode, e.g. https://pos.store.com
# NOTE: credentials are NEVER persisted — only passed in the request body and
# used for the duration of the extraction step, then discarded.
```

## New endpoint: test connection

```
POST /import/jobs/test-connection
Body: { source_system, api_base_url, username, password }  # or OAuth token
```

- Attempts authentication against the source system
- If successful, returns live row counts per entity and detected date range:
  ```json
  {
    "connected": true,
    "source_system": "ultimatepos",
    "counts": {
      "products": 342,
      "customers": 156,
      "sales": 4821,
      "purchase_orders": 203
    },
    "date_range": { "earliest": "2021-03-01", "latest": "2026-07-07" }
  }
  ```
- If authentication fails, returns 400 with a clear error message (wrong URL, bad credentials, network timeout)
- Credentials are used only for this request — never written to DB

## APIExtractor implementation

For UltimatePOS: extract the authentication and data-pull logic from the existing `pos_migrate.py` `POSClient` class into `adapters/ultimatepos_api.py`. The script already proves this works.

For Shopify: use Shopify Admin API (REST) with API key + secret.
For QuickBooks Online: OAuth 2.0 flow, access token passed from frontend after OAuth redirect.

## Checkpoint / resume for long API pulls

Large API migrations (50,000+ transactions) may take 10–20 minutes. If the connection drops mid-pull:
- Store extracted rows to a temporary table or serialised file keyed on `job_id`
- Track last successfully extracted entity and page number in `MigrationJob.checkpoint` (JSONB)
- `POST /import/jobs/{job_id}/confirm` resumes from checkpoint rather than restarting

## Credential security rules (non-negotiable)

- Credentials passed in request body only — never logged, never stored in DB, never appear in responses
- Use HTTPS only for any outbound API calls to source systems
- After extraction completes (or fails), credentials are garbage collected — no reference kept
- Log only: `"UltimatePOS extraction started for job {job_id}"` — never log credential values

subtasks.title: Mandatory pre-import confirmation snapshot — both extraction paths
subtasks.description: Before any data is written to the database, the ETL pipeline must produce a full confirmation snapshot that the user must explicitly approve. This applies to both CSV and live API extraction modes. No insert may occur until the user has seen and approved this snapshot.
subtasks.details:
## Confirmation snapshot endpoint

After extraction + transformation + validation complete (but before loading), the job enters `status = 'awaiting_confirmation'`. The frontend fetches the snapshot via:

```
GET /import/jobs/{job_id}/confirmation-snapshot
```

Response structure:
```json
{
  "job_id": "...",
  "extraction_mode": "api",
  "source_system": "ultimatepos",
  "status": "awaiting_confirmation",
  "snapshot": {
    "entities": [
      {
        "name": "products",
        "count": 342,
        "sample_rows": [
          { "name": "Ankara Print Fabric", "sku": "AFK-001", "price": "4500.00" },
          { "name": "White Lace (per yard)", "sku": "WL-003", "price": "1200.00" }
        ]
      },
      {
        "name": "customers",
        "count": 156,
        "sample_rows": [
          { "name": "Adaeze Okonkwo", "email": "adaeze@...", "phone": "+234..." }
        ]
      },
      {
        "name": "sales",
        "count": 4821,
        "date_range": { "earliest": "2021-03-01", "latest": "2026-07-07" },
        "sample_rows": []
      }
    ],
    "warnings": [
      { "entity": "products", "count": 12, "message": "12 deleted products will be imported as ghost records to preserve sale history" },
      { "entity": "sales", "count": 8, "message": "8 sales have unrecognised payment method — normalised to 'other'" }
    ],
    "ghost_records": { "products": 12 },
    "estimated_duration_seconds": 180,
    "total_rows": 5634
  }
}
```

- `sample_rows`: first 3 rows of each entity so the user can verify the data looks right
- `warnings`: non-blocking issues that will be handled automatically
- `estimated_duration_seconds`: rough estimate based on total row count
- `ghost_records`: count of placeholder records that will be created

## Confirmation endpoint

```
POST /import/jobs/{job_id}/confirm
Body: { "approved": true }
```

- If `approved: false` → job cancelled, extracted data discarded, status = `'cancelled'`
- If `approved: true` → loading begins, status transitions to `'importing'`
- If called while `status != 'awaiting_confirmation'` → 409 Conflict

This endpoint is the **only** way to trigger the Load phase. The Load phase cannot be triggered internally without explicit approval. This is enforced at the service layer, not just the router.

## Status flow

```
pending
  → extracting       (extraction running)
  → transforming     (transform + validate running)
  → awaiting_confirmation  ← USER MUST ACT HERE
  → importing        (load running — after approval)
  → recomputing      (post-import recomputation)
  → done
  → failed           (any step)
  → cancelled        (user declined at confirmation)
  → rolled_back      (user undid after done)
```

No status may skip `awaiting_confirmation` and go directly to `importing`.

tasks.title: Build data import wizard frontend (Angular multi-step)
tasks.description: Build an Angular multi-step import wizard that guides a business owner through migrating their existing data into ModishLog. Drives the ETL backend (Task 162). Steps: source system selection → template download → file upload → location mapping → validation preview → confirm import → summary. Accessible from Settings or the onboarding flow for new businesses.
tasks.details:
## Feature location
`frontend/src/app/features/data-import/`

Structure:
```
data-import/
  pages/
    import-wizard-page.component.ts   ← main page (routes to /settings/import)
  components/
    step-source.component.ts          ← step 1: source system picker
    step-templates.component.ts       ← step 2: download templates
    step-upload.component.ts          ← step 3: file upload
    step-location-map.component.ts    ← step 4: location mapping
    step-validate.component.ts        ← step 5: validation preview
    step-confirm.component.ts         ← step 6: confirm + progress
    step-summary.component.ts         ← step 7: done summary
  services/
    import.service.ts                 ← calls /api/v1/import/* endpoints
  models/
    import.models.ts                  ← MigrationJob, ValidationError, etc.
```

---

## Step 1 — Source system selection

4 cards, icon + description:
- **UltimatePOS** — "Export from UltimatePOS/Laravel. We auto-detect your column names."
- **QuickBooks** — "Use QuickBooks CSV export (Items, Invoices, Bills, Vendors)."
- **Shopify** — "Use Shopify's built-in Products and Orders CSV export."
- **Generic CSV** — "Use our templates. Works with any spreadsheet (Excel, Google Sheets)."

Selecting a source sets `job.source_system`. User can proceed.

---

## Step 2 — Download templates

Show a list of all entities with their template CSV download links:
`GET /import/templates` returns a ZIP, or `GET /import/templates/{entity}` for individual files.

Table shows:
| Entity | Required? | Download |
|---|---|---|
| Product Categories | Optional | ↓ CSV |
| Products | Required | ↓ CSV |
| Customers | Optional | ↓ CSV |
| ... | | |

"Download all templates (ZIP)" button at top.
Each template CSV opens with correct headers and one example row.

For UltimatePOS/QuickBooks/Shopify source: show instructions specific to how to export from that system (static help text per source_system).

---

## Step 3 — File upload

Drag-and-drop zone that accepts:
- Individual CSV files (user picks which entity each file is)
- A single ZIP file (auto-detected by filename: `products.csv`, `sales.csv`, etc.)

Show a checklist of entities. As files are dropped, the corresponding entity row shows ✅ with file name + row count preview.

Required entities (products) shown in red until uploaded. Optional entities shown in grey.

`POST /import/jobs` called on "Next" — creates job and uploads all files. Returns `job_id`.

---

## Step 4 — Location mapping

Only shown if the uploaded data contains location names.

`GET /import/jobs/{job_id}` returns detected location names from source data.
User maps each source location name → a ModishLog business location (dropdown of their locations).
Option: "Create as new location" for unmapped ones.

Submit updates job options with `location_map`.

If no locations detected in source data, this step is skipped automatically.

---

## Step 5 — Validation preview

`POST /import/jobs/{job_id}/validate` is called on entering this step. Show a loading spinner while validation runs (polling `GET /import/jobs/{job_id}` every 2s until `status !== 'validating'`).

Display:
- Summary table: entity → row count → error count → warning count
- Expandable error list per entity (show up to 50 rows, "Download full error report" for more)
- Error row format: `Row 23 | field: product_id | Product "POS-999" not found — will be imported as ghost record [warning]`

If **errors** exist:
- "Fix & Re-upload" button (goes back to step 3)
- Cannot proceed until error count = 0

If **warnings only** (no errors):
- "Proceed with warnings" button available
- Warnings listed but non-blocking (e.g., ghost products created, unmapped payment methods normalised to 'other')

If **no issues**:
- "Looks good — proceed to import" button

---

## Step 6 — Confirm & import

Summary of what will be imported:
```
Products:          342 records
Product Variants:   89 records
Customers:         156 records
Sales:           4,821 records (from 2021-03-01 to 2026-07-01)
Purchase Orders:   203 records
Expenses:           94 records
...
```

"Start Import" button calls `POST /import/jobs/{job_id}/confirm`.

subtasks.title: Dual extraction path choice in wizard — API connection vs CSV upload
subtasks.description: The wizard must present both migration methods as explicit choices at step 2. Both paths are first-class options, not fallbacks. The choice should guide less technical users toward the live API connection and technical users toward CSV upload, but never force either.
subtasks.details:
## Step 2 UI — method selection

After choosing the source system (step 1), the user sees two cards side by side:

```
┌─────────────────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────────────────┐
│  🔌 Connect directly        │   │  📄 Upload CSV files        │
│                             │   │                             │
│  We connect to your system  │   │  Download our templates,    │
│  and pull everything        │   │  fill them in, upload back  │
│  automatically.             │   │                             │
│                             │   │  Best for: technical users, │
│  Best for: most businesses. │   │  offline data, custom       │
│  No file handling needed.   │   │  formats.                   │
│                             │   │                             │
│  [Select]                   │   │  [Select]                   │
└─────────────────────────────┘   └─────────────────────────────┘
```

Selecting a card highlights it and enables the Next button. The choice sets `job.extraction_mode`.

If the selected source system does not support live API connection (e.g. a generic/unknown system), the "Connect directly" card is shown as disabled with a tooltip: "Direct connection not available for this source. Use CSV upload."

## API path steps (steps 3a–4a)

**Step 3a — Credentials**

Form fields vary by source system:

- UltimatePOS: URL field + Username + Password
- Shopify: Store subdomain (mystore.myshopify.com) + API key + API secret
- QuickBooks Online: "Connect with QuickBooks" OAuth button (redirects to QB login, returns token)

Password fields use `type="password"`. No credentials ever appear in network logs or stored state beyond the in-memory Angular form.

"Test connection" button at bottom — calls `POST /import/jobs/test-connection`. Shows inline result:
- ✅ Connected — displays live counts and date range immediately below the button
- ❌ Failed — shows specific error (wrong URL, bad credentials, timeout) with suggested fix

User cannot proceed to step 4a until connection test passes.

**Step 4a — What will be pulled (pre-extraction preview)**

Shown immediately after a successful connection test (data already in hand from test-connection response):

```
Connected to UltimatePOS at pos.yourstore.com

What we found:
  Products        342
  Customers       156
  Suppliers        28
  Sales          4,821   (Mar 2021 – Jul 2026)
  Purchase Orders  203
  Expenses          94

Full history will be imported (5 years, 3 months)
Estimated time: ~3 minutes
```

"Continue" advances to the shared confirmation screen (step 5).

## CSV path steps (steps 3b–4b)

**Step 3b — Download templates**
Unchanged from original design in Task #163.

**Step 4b — Upload files**
Unchanged from original design. After upload, file parsing happens server-side and row counts are returned. User sees the same "what we found" summary as the API path before proceeding.

## Both paths converge at step 5

From this point the wizard is identical regardless of extraction mode.

## Long-running job UX (API path)

When the user clicks "Start Import" on the confirmation screen and the estimated duration is > 60 seconds:

Show a dismissible info banner:
```
⏱ This import will take about 3 minutes.
   You can safely close this tab — we'll email you when it's done.
   Or stay here to watch live progress.
```

If the user closes the tab:
- Job continues server-side
- Email sent on completion (or failure) with a link back to `/settings/import/{job_id}`
- Next time they open the app, a notification badge appears on the Settings nav item

If the user stays:
- Progress bar updates every 2 seconds via polling
- Shows current entity being loaded: "Importing sales... (2,341 / 4,821)"

subtasks.description: A dedicated confirmation screen shown to ALL users before any data is written, regardless of extraction mode. The user must read the snapshot, review warnings, and explicitly click "Yes, import this data" before the Load phase starts. Declining cancels the job cleanly.
subtasks.details:
## When this screen appears

Both the API path and CSV path arrive here after extraction + transformation + validation complete and the job reaches `status = 'awaiting_confirmation'`. The screen polls `GET /import/jobs/{job_id}` and renders as soon as that status is reached.

## Layout

```
│  What will be imported                                          │
│                                                                 │
│  Entity              Records    Sample                          │

│  Products               342    Ankara Print Fabric, ...        │
│  Product Variants        89    Red/S, Blue/L, ...              │

│    (needed to preserve historical sale accuracy)               │
│  • 8 sales have unknown payment method → stored as "other"     │
│                                                                 │

```

## Rules

- The "Yes, import this data" button calls `POST /import/jobs/{job_id}/confirm` with `{ "approved": true }`
- The "Cancel" button calls `POST /import/jobs/{job_id}/confirm` with `{ "approved": false }`, then redirects to `/settings/import` with a toast: "Import cancelled. No data was changed."
- There is no way to skip this screen in the UI — the wizard step order enforces it
- The screen is also accessible by direct URL (`/settings/import/{job_id}`) so a user who closed the tab can return and still approve or cancel
- If the job's `status` is no longer `'awaiting_confirmation'` when the user arrives (e.g. it expired or was already confirmed from another tab), show a clear message: "This import has already been processed. View its status in Data Imports history."
- The notices/warnings section is always shown even if empty (show "No issues detected" in that case) — the user must always see the full picture

## Confirmation of what is NOT imported

Below the table, show a collapsed "What is not included" section:
- If any entities had zero records: "No expenses found in your data"
- If any entities had errors that prevented import: list them with explanation
- This ensures the user understands the boundaries of the migration, not just what is included

tasks.title: Post-import recomputation service — rebuild inventory, P&L and AI signals after migration
tasks.description: After a data migration completes (Task 162), the platform's derived/computed data is stale or empty — inventory levels, dashboard KPIs, low stock alerts, demand elasticity and pricing suggestions all need to be rebuilt from the imported transaction history. This task builds a recomputation service that the ETL loader triggers automatically after a successful import, and that can also be triggered manually (e.g. after an undo/rollback).
tasks.details:
## Why this is needed

The ETL loader (Task 162) writes raw records: sales, purchase orders, stock movements, etc. But several tables hold DERIVED state that is normally updated incrementally as transactions happen in real time:

| Derived table / field | Normally updated by |
|---|---|
| `inventory_levels.quantity` | sales service, orders service |
| `low_stock_alerts` | inventory service on each movement |
| `price_history` | pricing service on each price change |
| Dashboard KPI cache (if any) | dashboard service |
| `demand_elasticity` | AI engine background job |
| `reorder_suggestions` | AI engine background job |
| `price_suggestions` | AI engine background job |
| `cashflow_projections` | cashflow service |

After a full history import, these tables are either empty (new business) or out of sync (if partial data existed). This service rebuilds them from scratch for the business.

---

## New service: `backend/src/data_import/recompute.py`

```python
async def recompute_after_import(
    session: AsyncSession,
    business_id: UUID,
    job_id: UUID,
) -> None:
    await _recompute_inventory_levels(session, business_id)
    await _recompute_low_stock_alerts(session, business_id)
    await _recompute_price_history_gaps(session, business_id)
    await _trigger_ai_recomputation(session, business_id)
```

Called by the loader at the end of `POST /import/jobs/{job_id}/confirm`, inside a separate transaction (so a recomputation failure doesn't roll back the import itself — the import data is safe).

Also exposed as a standalone endpoint for manual re-trigger:
```
POST /import/jobs/{job_id}/recompute
```

---

## `_recompute_inventory_levels`

Algorithm:
1. Zero out all `inventory_levels.quantity` for this business (or delete and re-insert)
2. Replay all `stock_movements` in chronological order (`movement_type`, `quantity`, `variant_id`):
   - `PURCHASE` → +quantity
   - `SALE` → -quantity
   - `ADJUSTMENT` → +/- quantity
   - `RETURN_IN` → +quantity
   - `RETURN_OUT` → -quantity
   - `TRANSFER` → -quantity from source location, +quantity at destination
3. For each product (and variant), compute final quantity per `business_location_id`
4. Upsert into `inventory_levels`

Must be variant-aware: separate `inventory_levels` row per `(product_id, variant_id, location_id)`.

This is the authoritative approach — it ensures inventory levels are always consistent with transaction history even if individual movements were created in non-chronological order by the importer.

---

## `_recompute_low_stock_alerts`

1. Clear all existing `low_stock_alerts` for this business
2. For each product/variant where `inventory_levels.quantity <= products.reorder_point` (or `reorder_configs.reorder_point`), create a `LowStockAlert`
3. Skip products with `is_active = False`

---

## `_recompute_price_history_gaps`

If the imported data includes `price_history` rows (from the CSV), validate they are in order and there are no gaps (missing records between known price points). Flag any gaps as warnings on the `MigrationJob`.

If no `price_history` was imported, create a single opening `price_history` row for each product using its current `selling_price` and `created_at` as the date.

---

## `_trigger_ai_recomputation`

Fire background tasks (using `asyncio.create_task` or a task queue) for:
- Demand elasticity model rebuild (`ai_engine/service.py`: `compute_demand_elasticity`)
- Reorder suggestion refresh (`ai_engine/service.py`: `generate_reorder_suggestions`)
- Price suggestion refresh (`ai_engine/service.py`: `generate_price_suggestions`)

These are slow (seconds to minutes depending on data volume) so they run in the background. The migration is marked `status = 'done'` before these complete — they update the `MigrationJob` with an `ai_recompute_status` field when they finish.

---

## Progress tracking

Update `MigrationJob` model with additional fields:
```python
recompute_status: Mapped[str | None]   # 'pending' | 'running' | 'done' | 'failed'
recompute_started_at: Mapped[datetime | None]
recompute_completed_at: Mapped[datetime | None]
recompute_errors: Mapped[list] = mapped_column(JSONB, default=list)
```

The frontend wizard step 7 (summary) polls `GET /import/jobs/{job_id}` and shows:
- "✅ Import complete — rebuilding inventory and analytics..." while `recompute_status = 'running'`
- "✅ Everything ready — go to dashboard" when `recompute_status = 'done'`

---

## Rollback integration

When `DELETE /import/jobs/{job_id}` (rollback) runs, it must also:
1. Re-run `_recompute_inventory_levels` and `_recompute_low_stock_alerts` after deleting the migration rows — because rolling back sales and purchases changes inventory
2. Clear AI suggestions that were generated from the now-deleted data

---

## Idempotency

`recompute_after_import` must be safe to call multiple times. Each step deletes its derived data first, then rebuilds. Running it twice produces the same result.

---

## Performance considerations

- `_recompute_inventory_levels` may process 100,000+ stock movement rows for a large business. Use `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` batches of 5,000 rows or a single aggregate SQL query instead of loading all rows into memory.
- Preferred approach: single `GROUP BY product_id, variant_id, location_id, movement_type` aggregate query, then apply +/- logic in Python — much faster than row-by-row replay.
- Run inside `asyncio.to_thread` if blocking, to avoid blocking the event loop.
tasks.testStrategy:
Backend (pytest) — write BEFORE implementation:

- Import sale for variant Red/L and Blue/M of same product → inventory levels computed independently per variant
- Import product with reorder_point=5, final quantity=3 → low_stock_alert created after recompute

- Rollback import → recompute runs again, inventory returns to pre-import state
