tasks.title: Add variant_id to InventoryBatch for variant-aware FIFO costing
tasks.description: FIFO COGS is pooled across sibling variants of the same product because InventoryBatch/fifo_deduct() have no variant scoping.
tasks.details:
Found during task 164's PR #306 review (rounds 8/12/14). InventoryBatch has no variant_id column, and fifo_deduct(db, product_id, quantity) only filters by product_id. For a product with variants replenished via separate purchase orders, selling variant A can consume variant B's batches, misattributing landed cost and silently misstating gross profit across both variants — for every sale of a variant product, not just imported ones (sales/service.py's create_sale already has this behavior, confirmed pre-existing).

Fix requires:
1. New Alembic migration adding nullable variant_id to inventory_batches
2. Update InventoryBatch model + create_batch() to accept/set variant_id
3. Update fifo_deduct() to accept and filter by variant_id
4. Update every caller: sales/service.py's create_sale, orders/service.py's transition_status (PO delivery batch creation — needs OrderLineItem.variant_id propagated), data_import/recompute.py's _compute_fifo_cogs_for_imported_sales
5. Check whether OrderLineItem currently tracks variant_id at all — if not, that's a prerequisite

Out of scope for task 164 — spans sales/orders/inventory domains, not just data_import.

tasks.title: Add a sale-to-batch consumption ledger so FIFO batch consumption can be reversed
tasks.description: Neither void_sale() nor data_import rollback restores InventoryBatch.quantity_remaining consumed by fifo_deduct(), because there's no record of which batches a given sale actually consumed.
tasks.details:
Found during task 164's PR #306 review (round 16). Confirmed pre-existing and systemic: sales/service.py's void_sale() already only restores InventoryLevel.quantity_on_hand via adjust_stock() — it never touches InventoryBatch.quantity_remaining. data_import's rollback_job() has the identical gap for imported sales whose stock was FIFO-deducted during recompute.

Symptom: after a voided sale or a rolled-back import, on-hand quantity looks correct again, but the InventoryBatch rows that fifo_deduct() decremented stay short. Future real sales run out of matching FIFO batches earlier than they should, silently understating COGS / overstating gross profit going forward.

Fix requires a proper consumption ledger (e.g. a SaleBatchConsumption table recording {sale_id, batch_id, quantity_consumed} written by fifo_deduct() at consumption time), then:
1. New migration for the ledger table
2. fifo_deduct() writes one ledger row per batch it draws from
3. void_sale() and data_import's rollback_job() use the ledger to restore exact quantities to exact batches instead of guessing
4. Handle the case where a ledger-referenced batch was itself deleted (e.g. by data_import rollback's loader_rollback())

Out of scope for task 164 — this is a sales/inventory domain feature, not specific to data import.

tasks.title: Fix MovementType enum schema drift (values_callable + normalize drifted labels)
tasks.description: inventory_levels' movement_type Postgres enum has mixed-case labels from past migrations, and the SQLAlchemy column lacks values_callable, making STOCK_ADJUSTMENT and OPENING_STOCK permanently uninsertable.
tasks.details:
Found during task 164's PR #306 review (rounds 8/16). backend/src/inventory/models.py's `movement_type: Mapped[MovementType] = mapped_column(Enum(MovementType))` has no values_callable (unlike every other enum column in the codebase, e.g. data_import/models.py's MigrationJobStatus/SourceSystem/ExtractionMode), so it serializes new inserts via the Python enum's .name (upper-case). But STOCK_ADJUSTMENT/OPENING_STOCK were only ever migrated into the Postgres enum type as lower-case values, so inserting either of those two members fails at the DB level.

data_import/service.py's rollback_job() currently works around this by using MANUAL_ADD/MANUAL_REMOVE instead of the semantically-correct STOCK_ADJUSTMENT — documented in a comment, but any other/future caller that needs to record a genuine stock_adjustment or opening_stock movement will hit the identical silent-until-runtime failure.

Fix requires:
1. Migration to ALTER TYPE the movementtype Postgres enum, normalizing every drifted label to one consistent case (check current DB state first — some labels may already be relied upon by existing rows/queries)
2. Add values_callable=lambda x: [e.value for e in x] to the Enum(MovementType) column definition
3. Once fixed, data_import's rollback_job() can use the semantically-correct STOCK_ADJUSTMENT movement type instead of MANUAL_ADD/MANUAL_REMOVE

Out of scope for task 164 — this is inventory-domain schema drift predating this task, not something task 164 introduced.

tasks.title: Fix variant pooling in sales/service.py's _deduct_lot_units lot-tracking system
tasks.description: A second, parallel FIFO-like tracking system (OrderLineItem.units_remaining, distinct from InventoryBatch.quantity_remaining) has the identical cross-variant pooling bug that task 165 fixed for InventoryBatch/fifo_deduct.
tasks.details:
Found while implementing task 165 (variant-aware FIFO costing, PR for feat/165-variant-aware-fifo-costing). sales/service.py's create_sale() calls two separate consumption mechanisms per sale: fifo_deduct() (now variant-aware) against InventoryBatch, AND _deduct_lot_units() against OrderLineItem.units_remaining — the latter has no variant_id filter at all, even though OrderLineItem already has a variant_id column (task 165 confirmed this while checking prerequisites).

_deduct_lot_units(db, product_id, quantity) queries `OrderLineItem.product_id == product_id, OrderLineItem.units_remaining > 0` ordered by order date, with no variant scoping — so selling variant A can deplete units_remaining on a lot that was actually delivered for variant B.

Not clear whether OrderLineItem.units_remaining and InventoryBatch.quantity_remaining are two independent sources of truth for the same concept (lot-level remaining stock) or serve different purposes (units_remaining backs the /orders/{id}/lots endpoint per test_orders.py's TestLotInventoryTracking). Investigate the relationship between the two systems before deciding whether to add variant scoping to _deduct_lot_units() alone, or consolidate the two mechanisms.

tasks.title: update_sale() doesn't re-run FIFO deduction when quantity changes
tasks.description: Editing a sale's quantity via update_sale() adjusts InventoryLevel via adjust_stock() but never re-runs fifo_deduct(), so InventoryBatch.quantity_remaining and the sale's fifo_cogs/fifo_gross_profit drift out of sync with the corrected quantity.
tasks.details:
Found during task 165's PR #307 review (variant-aware FIFO costing). Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to variant scoping specifically — sales/service.py's update_sale() was never touched by task 165's changes, and this gap exists for non-variant sales too.

update_sale() calls adjust_stock(..., variant_id=...) to correct InventoryLevel.quantity_on_hand when quantity_diff != 0, but never calls fifo_deduct() again. Result: InventoryBatch.quantity_remaining stays based on the sale's original quantity (overstating remaining batch stock after a quantity increase, understating it after a decrease), and sale.fifo_cogs/fifo_gross_profit are never recalculated — a P&L report reading those fields directly sees stale, wrong figures for any edited sale.

Fix requires deciding the right correction strategy: naively calling fifo_deduct() again for just the delta would double up (or under-count) against the original consumption unless the original batches consumed are tracked (see task #166's consumption-ledger follow-up — likely a shared prerequisite). A simpler interim fix: reverse the original fifo_cogs proportionally and re-run fifo_deduct() for the new total quantity, accepting that this can still misattribute cost if batches have been partially consumed by other sales in between.

tasks.title: void_sale() doesn't reverse OrderLineItem.units_remaining deduction
tasks.description: void_sale() reverses InventoryLevel and InventoryBatch.quantity_remaining (via reverse_fifo_consumption()'s FifoConsumption ledger, task 166) but has no mechanism to restore OrderLineItem.units_remaining consumed by _deduct_lot_units(). There's no ledger recording which specific lots a sale's _deduct_lot_units() call touched, so voiding a sale leaves that lot's units_remaining permanently short — under-reporting available units on the /orders/{id}/lots endpoint and LOT-type stock counts indefinitely.
tasks.details: Found during PR #310's review (task 168). Likely fix mirrors task 166's FifoConsumption pattern: add a ledger table (e.g. LotConsumption(sale_id, order_line_item_id, quantity_consumed)) written by _deduct_lot_units(), then a reverse_lot_consumption(db, sale_ids) helper called from void_sale() and data_import's rollback_job(), analogous to reverse_fifo_consumption(). Investigate whether a lighter-weight approach (recording just enough to reverse, without a full new table) is possible before committing to the full ledger design.

tasks.title: pricing compute_suggestion() doesn't scope weighted-average lot cost by variant_id
tasks.description: pricing/service.py's compute_suggestion() (around line 1233-1267) computes a weighted-average unit_cost_ngn across all OrderLineItem lots with units_remaining > 0 for a product, but has no variant_id filter — the same cross-variant pooling bug task 165 fixed for fifo_deduct()/InventoryBatch and task 168 fixed for _deduct_lot_units()/OrderLineItem, on a third consumer of the units_remaining ledger. For a product with variants of differing cost, this blends sibling variants' lot costs into one product-level price suggestion instead of a per-variant one.
tasks.details: Found during PR #310's review (task 168). Fix should mirror task 168's approach: accept a variant_id param on compute_suggestion()'s cost-lookup query and apply src/core/query_helpers.py's variant_or_untagged_filter(OrderLineItem.variant_id, variant_id) (added in task 168, shared with sales/service.py's _deduct_lot_units() and inventory/service.py's fifo_deduct()). Check compute_suggestion()'s call sites to confirm a variant_id is available/threadable through to this query.

tasks.title: update_sale() doesn't resync OrderLineItem.units_remaining on quantity change
tasks.description: update_sale()'s FIFO resync (task 169, PR #311) corrects InventoryLevel and InventoryBatch/FifoConsumption when a sale's quantity is edited, but never touches OrderLineItem.units_remaining — the parallel lot-tracking ledger _deduct_lot_units() (task 168) depletes on sale creation. Editing a sale's quantity down leaves units_remaining permanently short by the difference; editing it up doesn't restore/re-deduct it either. Same root cause as task #170 (void_sale() has the identical gap) — no ledger exists yet to reverse a specific sale's units_remaining consumption precisely.
tasks.details: Found during PR #311's review (task 169). Should likely be fixed together with task #170 once the lot-consumption reversal ledger design lands — investigate whether one shared ledger (e.g. LotConsumption(sale_id, order_line_item_id, quantity_consumed)) can serve both void_sale() and update_sale(), the same way FifoConsumption (task 166) serves both void_sale() and update_sale()'s InventoryBatch-side resync.

tasks.title: Fix InventoryLevel rows not tagged with migration_id on new-variant PO delivery
tasks.description: ensure_inventory_level_exists() in inventory/service.py never tags the InventoryLevel row it backfills with migration_id, breaking data_import rollback for jobs that create a new product+variant and deliver stock to it in the same import.
tasks.details:
Found via code review (PR #321 review, 2026-07-23). ensure_inventory_level_exists()'s only real caller is orders/service.py's transition_status(), invoked from data_import's load_purchase_orders() when a PO delivers to a brand-new variant created in the same import job. The InventoryLevel(product_id, variant_id) row it creates has migration_id=None since the function has no migration_id parameter. On rollback, loader.py's rollback() does `DELETE FROM inventory_levels WHERE migration_id = :job_id` (misses the untagged row), then deletes product_variants tagged with that migration_id — violating the FK from the surviving InventoryLevel.variant_id -> product_variants.id (no ondelete cascade), raising an unhandled IntegrityError that aborts the whole rollback transaction. The import can never be rolled back; the API request 500s instead of undoing the import.

Fix: thread migration_id through ensure_inventory_level_exists() (optional param, default None) from transition_status() -> load_purchase_orders(), so the backfilled row is correctly tagged when created during an import.

tasks.title: Static-file mount failures in main.py now silently swallowed
tasks.description: os.makedirs()/app.mount() setup for serving uploaded files used to crash the app at startup on failure; now a PermissionError/RuntimeError is caught and discarded with no log line, so a misconfigured uploads volume ships a silently broken image-serving path.
tasks.details:
Found via code review (PR #321 review, 2026-07-23). backend/src/main.py:~185. If settings.UPLOAD_DIR is root-owned or otherwise unwritable in a given deploy (a real Docker named-volume scenario), the setup raises PermissionError, which is now caught and discarded with no log line. The app reports healthy and starts normally, but the /static route was never mounted, so every request for a previously-uploaded product image 404s in production with no error surfaced anywhere. Before this change the same misconfiguration would fail the deploy immediately and visibly instead.

Fix: log the error (at minimum) when the static mount setup fails, rather than silently swallowing it — consider whether it should still fail loudly at startup given the previous behavior was intentional.

tasks.title: Orders page variant picker leaves stale unit_cost when variant has no cost override
tasks.description: orders-page.component.ts's onOrderVariantChange only overwrites item.unit_cost when the selected variant has a non-null cost_price_override; otherwise unit_cost silently keeps the previous variant/product's value, so a PO line item can be submitted with a stale, wrong cost.
tasks.details:
Found via code review (PR #321 review, 2026-07-23). frontend/src/app/features/orders/pages/orders-page.component.ts:~1176-1187. Compare to sales-page.component.ts's near-identical onVariantChange (line ~1539-1550) for prices, which always resets row.unit_price (falling back to the product's selling_price, or null) so it never exhibits this bug. The variant-picker logic (product lookup, active-variant filtering, price/cost pre-fill) is duplicated near-identically across orders-page and sales-page instead of factored into one shared component/service, which is how this divergence happened unnoticed.

Fix: make onOrderVariantChange always reset unit_cost on variant change (falling back to the product's own cost when the variant has no override), matching sales-page's pattern. Consider factoring the shared variant-picker logic (also flagged: duplicated formatMoney() helper, same two files) into one place to prevent future divergence — separate follow-up if scope allows.

tasks.title: Cleanup: dedupe migration_id column mixin and duplicated formatMoney() helper
tasks.description: Two low-severity duplication cleanups found via code review (PR #321 review, 2026-07-23): the migration_id FK column is hand-copied across 23 model definitions instead of a shared mixin, and formatMoney() is duplicated verbatim between orders-page.component.ts and sales-page.component.ts.
tasks.details:
1. `migration_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("migration_jobs.id"), nullable=True, index=True, default=None)` is repeated character-for-character across 10 backend model files (23 occurrences): customers, auth, expenses (x2), inventory (x3), locations, orders (x4), stockcount (x2), products (x4), sales (x3), suppliers (x2). The codebase already has a UUIDMixin/TimestampMixin pattern in backend/src/core/database.py for exactly this — a MigrationTaggedMixin there would collapse all 23 copies to one definition. Note stockcount/models.py already differs slightly (imports Optional[uuid.UUID] instead of uuid.UUID | None), an early sign of drift.

2. `formatMoney(amount: string | number): string { return new Intl.NumberFormat('en-NG', { style: 'currency', currency: 'NGN', maximumFractionDigits: 0 }).format(Number(amount)); }` is defined identically in both frontend/src/app/features/orders/pages/orders-page.component.ts (~1189-1191) and sales-page.component.ts (~1552-1554). Extract to a shared util/pipe.

Low priority — pure cleanup, no functional bug. Bundle with the variant-picker dedup task (see sibling task) if doing a shared-component refactor of orders-page/sales-page anyway.

tasks.title: Business owners (role OWNER) can never pass require_admin — can't invite staff or unlock accounts in their own business
tasks.description: require_admin() in auth/dependencies.py checks current_user.role != UserRole.ADMIN only — UserRole.OWNER (the role /auth/onboard assigns to every self-serve-created business owner) is rejected. This means the owner of a business can never call any admin-gated endpoint (POST /auth/register to invite staff, PATCH /auth/admin/unlock, and likely the rest of the admin user-management router) within their own business.
tasks.details:
Found while fixing the E2E test bootstrap (2026-07-23) — frontend/e2e/auth.spec.ts's "Account lockout" describe block's afterAll unlock call (PATCH /auth/admin/unlock) 403s with the E2E owner account's token for this exact reason. Worked around that one call by not depending on it in the E2E fix, but the underlying gap is a real product question, not just a test issue: right now the ONLY way any business gets an admin-capable user is the hardcoded prod/staging admin@modishlog.com account (see reference_production_infra memory) — a self-serve business created via onboarding has no path to ever using admin-gated endpoints for its own business (inviting staff via /register, unlocking a locked-out staff account, etc.).

Needs a product/security decision, not a unilateral code change:
- Should require_admin() also accept OWNER (i.e., owners are admin-equivalent within their own business)?
- Or should there be a separate require_admin_or_owner dependency, keeping ADMIN's semantics narrower (e.g. platform-level admin) distinct from OWNER (business-level admin)?
- Either way, every admin-gated endpoint should be scoped to the actor's own business_id, not global — verify this is already true before loosening who can call them.

Once decided, backend/src/auth/dependencies.py's require_admin() (or a new dependency) needs updating, and frontend/e2e/auth.spec.ts's lockout afterAll can then use the E2E owner's own token again instead of whatever workaround is in place.

tasks.title: Speed up the E2E CI gate — 490 tests on 1 worker takes 20-30+ minutes
tasks.description: playwright.config.ts deliberately pins workers: 1 (tests share one Postgres DB/business and would race on shared state if parallelized) — a fully healthy full E2E run still takes ~20-30 minutes on a single worker, which is slow for a CI gate blocking every frontend PR.
tasks.details:
Investigated 2026-07-23 while diagnosing what looked like E2E "hangs" (actual root cause was unrelated — see PR #322/#323). Once those were fixed, the suite runs correctly but still takes its full serial runtime since parallelism is deliberately disabled (see playwright.config.ts's comment on `fullyParallel: false` / `workers: 1`).

Two viable permanent fixes, discussed with the user 2026-07-23 (deferred, not implemented yet):

1. **CI sharding (recommended, lower risk)**: keep workers:1 and the shared-DB test design untouched. Split the 490 tests across N parallel GitHub Actions matrix jobs (`npx playwright test --shard=i/N`), each spinning up its own fully isolated backend+Postgres+Redis stack (each CI runner is already isolated — no cross-shard race). Restructure `.github/workflows/frontend-build.yml`: turn the current single `gate` job into a matrix job (`e2e-shard`, e.g. 4-way), then add a new fan-in `gate` job requiring `needs: [build, e2e-shard]` to all succeed, mirroring the existing dependency-scan+test fan-in pattern already used in `backend-tests.yml`. No test-code changes needed. Expected ~4x wall-clock speedup with 4 shards.

2. **Per-worker tenant isolation (bigger, more powerful)**: ModishLog already has full business_id multi-tenancy — give each Playwright worker its own isolated business (instead of the current single shared "E2E Test Business" every spec file's `ensureTestUser()` creates) so `fullyParallel: true` becomes safe within a single job. Also incidentally closes off any other latent shared-state flakiness. Requires reworking test setup/teardown across the suite (every spec file currently assumes one shared E2E_EMAIL/business) — bigger, riskier change than sharding.

Recommendation from discussion: start with sharding (option 1) since it's lower-risk and doesn't touch test logic; revisit per-worker isolation later if sharding isn't enough or other shared-state flakiness surfaces.

tasks.title: No supported way to correct costs on a DELIVERED purchase order — cascades through inventory batches and sales COGS
tasks.description: update_order() flatly rejects any edit once an order is DELIVERED (EDITABLE_STATUSES excludes it by design), and even if that guard were lifted it has no code path touching InventoryBatch or recomputing Sale.fifo_cogs — those are only ever written once, at delivery time. There is currently no supported operation to correct a delivered order's unit costs against reality (e.g. the actual supplier invoice) without a one-off script.
tasks.details:
Found while manually correcting PO-2026-00004's costs against a real supplier proforma invoice (dogfood session, 2026-08-12) — required a standalone script (not committed, run once against local dev data) since no built-in operation does this. The script: 1) updated order_line_items.unit_cost/line_total + purchase_orders.total_amount, 2) updated the order's InventoryBatch.unit_cost_usd/landed_cost_per_unit (via compute_landed_cost()), 3) recomputed fifo_cogs/fifo_gross_profit for every sale with a FifoConsumption against those batches — re-summing each sale's FULL consumption set (not just this order's portion), since some sales draw from multiple orders' batches for the same product.

Needs a narrow, purpose-built service function + endpoint (NOT loosening update_order()'s general edit-lock — that lock is intentional, see task 94 'sec: remove DELIVERED from EDITABLE_STATUSES', and touches quantities/supplier/dates which must stay locked post-delivery). Scope should be limited to per-line-item unit_cost corrections on already-DELIVERED orders, with the same three-step cascade the script performed. Consider: should this require ADMIN role given it retroactively changes historical COGS/margin figures? Should it be logged/audited distinctly from a normal order edit?

Resolved (PR: fix/delivered-order-cost-correction): implemented as POST /orders/{id}/cost-corrections. Uses the same ownership check as every other order mutation (record_payment, void_payment), not require_admin — the OWNER role every self-serve business actually has cannot pass require_admin (task 177), which would have made this unusable for real businesses correcting their own orders.

tasks.title: Delivered-order edit form still shows non-cost fields as editable (silently no-op on save)
tasks.description: order-detail-page saveEdit() now routes DELIVERED orders through the cost-corrections endpoint (unit_cost/fx_rate_at_creation/shipping_cost only), but the edit UI itself still lets users interact with supplier name, dates, notes, quantities, and line-item deletion while editing a DELIVERED order — none of those are sent to the new endpoint, so those edits silently do nothing on save with no error telling the user why.
tasks.details:
Found via code review, PR #335 (2026-08-12). Not a data-safety bug (nothing gets corrupted server-side — update_order() still rejects those fields entirely, and the new endpoint just does not send them), but a real UX trap: a user could believe they changed the supplier or removed a line item on a delivered order and only discover otherwise later.

Fix: when order.status === 'DELIVERED', disable/hide the non-cost fields in the edit form (supplier_name, expected_delivery_date, notes, quantity inputs, the line-item delete button, pay_term_number/type, supplier_invoice_number/date) and leave only unit_cost per line item + fx_rate_at_creation + shipping_cost editable, matching exactly what correct_delivered_order_costs() actually supports.

tasks.title: fx_rate_at_delivery is never required/defaulted — COGS silently falls back to the (less accurate) creation-time rate
tasks.description: transition_status()'s DELIVERED handling computes FIFO landed cost from `transition.fx_rate_at_delivery or order.fx_rate_at_creation or Decimal("1500")` (orders/service.py ~line 586-589). The UI exposes an FX Rate (delivery) field on the delivery transition, but nothing requires it to be filled in, so it's easy to click through delivery without setting it — PO-2026-00004 did exactly this (fx_rate_at_delivery is NULL in prod/local data) and its COGS was booked at the ₦1,400 creation-time rate instead of whatever the actual rate was on the 2026-07-03 arrival date.
tasks.details:
Found 2026-08-12 while explaining to the user which FX rate the cost breakdown actually uses (creation vs. delivery vs. payment-time rates — see conversation same day). Confirmed via `_sync_payment_status`-adjacent code read of orders/service.py's DELIVERED transition block and a direct DB check of PO-2026-00004 (fx_rate_at_creation=1400, fx_rate_at_delivery=NULL).

Not urgent/high-risk — the fallback chain means nothing crashes and a rate always gets used — but it silently degrades costing accuracy whenever a user skips the field. Two options to consider (not yet decided):
1. Make fx_rate_at_delivery required in the DELIVERED transition schema/UI (blocks transition until set) — most correct, but adds friction to a workflow that currently allows one-click delivery.
2. Keep it optional but surface a visible warning/banner on the order once delivered without it ("COGS was booked at the creation-time rate — no delivery rate was recorded"), and let the existing correct_delivered_order_costs() endpoint (task 179) fix it after the fact.
Lean toward option 2 first (lower friction, non-blocking), with option 1 only if inaccurate COGS turns out to be a recurring problem in practice.

tasks.title: No visibility into FX variance between booked landed-cost rate and actual payment rates
tasks.description: COGS/landed cost is correctly computed from fx_rate_at_delivery (or fx_rate_at_creation as fallback) — a transaction-date snapshot, per standard inventory accounting (IAS 21/ASC 830: inventory is a non-monetary asset valued at the historical rate; payment-date FX differences are a realized gain/loss, not a cost-of-goods adjustment). Confirmed correct by design 2026-08-12 when the user asked whether payment-time FX rates should be averaged into COGS instead — they should not. But there is currently no reporting or UI surface showing the *difference* between that booked rate and what was actually paid, so a business has no visibility into FX gain/loss exposure on an order.
tasks.details:
Proposed 2026-08-12 alongside task 181 as the two follow-ups from the same FX-rate-methodology discussion (PO-2026-00004 dogfood session). Purely additive/informational — must NOT feed back into InventoryBatch.landed_cost_per_unit or Sale.fifo_cogs, which should stay locked to the transaction-date rate per task 181's reasoning.

Suggested shape: a computed (not stored) 'fx_variance' figure per order — booked rate (fx_rate_at_delivery/fx_rate_at_creation) vs. the payment-amount-weighted average of that order's OrderPayment.fx_rate values — surfaced either as a field on the order detail page (next to FX Rate (creation)) or as a line in an existing report (e.g. logistics-efficiency or a new FX exposure report). Needs product-side decision on where this is most useful before implementing.

tasks.title: compute_suggestion()'s lot/product queries don't filter by business_id — cross-tenant COGS/cost leak via product_id guessing
tasks.description: POST /pricing/suggest/{product_id} (compute_suggestion() in pricing/service.py) never filtered its OrderLineItem/PurchaseOrder lot query or its Product lookup by business_id — any authenticated user of ANY business could get a price suggestion (which reveals another business's landed cost, FX rate used, and catalog price) for an arbitrary product_id belonging to a different business, just by guessing/enumerating UUIDs.
tasks.details:
Found 2026-08-12 while wiring MarginTarget (Settings-configured target margins) into compute_suggestion() and suggest_prices_for_order() — doing that required adding a business_id param to compute_suggestion() for the new MarginTarget lookup only. Deliberately did NOT extend that business_id filtering to the function's PRE-EXISTING lot query (OrderLineItem joined to PurchaseOrder, ~line 1286-1298) or Product lookup (~line 1325-1330), since that's an unrelated, separately-shipped endpoint and fixing it silently inside an unrelated PR risked changing behavior without dedicated review/testing.

Fix: add `PurchaseOrder.business_id == business_id` to the lot query's where_clauses and `Product.business_id == business_id` to the product lookup, using the business_id param that now already flows into compute_suggestion() from the router (compute_suggestion_endpoint now depends on get_current_business_id — this task is now trivial/low-risk since the plumbing already exists, it's just applying the filter and adding a regression test for cross-tenant isolation, matching the pattern used across every other domain's business_id isolation task).

tasks.title: E2E gate: duplicate 'Add X' button strict-mode violations across list pages — RESOLVED
tasks.description: Several list pages (customers, suppliers, locations, stock-count, recommendations, expenses) rendered an 'Add X' call-to-action with IDENTICAL accessible text twice — once in the toolbar, once inside the empty-state row — so Playwright's getByRole('button', { name: 'Add X' }) threw a strict-mode violation (2+ matching elements) whenever the seeded E2E test business had an empty list for that page. This was a large chunk of the E2E gate's chronic failures, distinct from task #178 (which is about serial-run speed/timeout flakiness, not correctness).
tasks.details:
Root-caused and fixed 2026-08-13 (PR #335) after the user asked for a permanent fix. Confirmed via live CI failure logs (84 failing tests in one run) that this was actually two separate pre-existing issues compounding: (1) this deterministic duplicate-button bug, (2) task #178's timeout flakiness deep into the ~28min serial run. Fixed (1) only, per user's explicit scoping decision, since (2) needs a bigger sharding effort already tracked separately.

Fix applied: gave each empty-state CTA distinct text instead of repeating the toolbar's exact label (matching products-page.component.ts's existing 'Add your first product' convention):
- customers-page: 'Add Customer' -> 'Add your first customer'
- suppliers-page: 'Add Supplier' -> 'Add your first supplier'
- locations-page: 'Add Location' -> 'Add your first location'
- stock-count-list-page: 'New Stock Count' -> 'Start your first count'
- recommendations-page: 'Generate New' -> 'Generate Recommendations'
- expenses.spec.ts: scoped the category-manager modal's 'Add' button locator to the dialog (Playwright's default name match is a case-insensitive substring, so it also matched the page's own 'Add Expense' button)
- sales-page: added a disambiguating aria-label to the 'Add Sale' tab (visually unchanged) — a latent, not-yet-triggered collision with the real 'Add Sale' action button

Verified live against the isolated e2e stack: all previously-failing tests in these 6 areas now pass. Remaining E2E failures after this fix are confirmed unrelated (a missing 'Deactivate' button in customers, a stock-count finalization flow issue, a locations duplicate-code toast timing issue, and task #178's flakiness) — filed separately if not already tracked.

Marked done since the fix is verified and shipped; if the pattern recurs on a new page, the fix is the same: never let an empty-state CTA repeat the toolbar button's exact accessible name.

tasks.title: user-management.spec.ts: hardcoded wrong email assertion + Invite dialog labels not associated with inputs
tasks.description: Found 2026-08-13 while verifying task 177's fix end-to-end against the isolated E2E stack. Two independent, pre-existing bugs surfaced now that /admin/users/* endpoints actually work for the E2E OWNER account (previously masked by the 403 task 177 fixed): (1) 'Users page shows current admin user in list' asserts getByText('soji.soyoye@gmail.com') — the real prod admin's email, not the E2E suite's own E2E_EMAIL ('e2e-suite@modishlogtest.com') — so it can never pass against the E2E business's own user list. (2) 'Invite User dialog opens on button click' asserts getByLabel(/email/i) and getByLabel(/full name/i), but users-page.component.ts's invite dialog (~line 199-215) uses plain <label> tags with no for attribute and inputs with no id — Playwright's getByLabel can't associate them.
tasks.details: Confirmed both are pre-existing via git blame (last touched by PR #229/#244/#206, well before this session) — not introduced by task 177's business_id/OWNER changes. Fixed 2026-08-13 (PR #341, stacked on #340): (1) test now imports E2E_EMAIL from ./helpers/auth and asserts that instead of the hardcoded prod email. (2) added matching id/for attributes to the invite and edit dialogs' full_name/email/role/password fields in users-page.component.ts. Verified 24/24 pass against the isolated E2E stack.
